Skills-3 surfaces installed skills to the user via <code>tau skill list</code> and <code>tau skill show <name></code>.</p> <h2 id="decision-22"><a class="header" href="#decision-22">Decision</a></h2> <p>Two subcommands:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>tau skill list</code></strong> — enumerate installed skills (lockfile only; zero per-skill disk reads, consumes Skills-2's <code>LockedSkill.frontmatter</code> cache).</li> <li><strong><code>tau skill show <name></code></strong> — inspect one skill (lockfile + one <code>tau.toml</code> disk read; optional <code>--body</code> adds one <code>SKILL.md</code> read).</li> </ul> <p>Both subcommands support <code>--json</code> for canonical machine-readable output (matches existing <code>tau resolve --json</code> / <code>tau verify --json</code> convention). Both default to human-formatted terminal output.</p> <p><code>show --body</code> <strong>renders markdown via termimad by default</strong>, matching <code>tau chat</code>'s precedent. <code>--raw</code> flag opts out for pipe / grep / diff workflows. The trade-off favors the interactive default (most users running <code>tau skill show --body</code> are reading interactively, not piping).</p> <p>Unknown-name handling: Levenshtein distance ≤ 2 surfaces a "did you mean…?" suggestion; otherwise prints the full installed list. Exit 2 in both cases (matches existing <code>tau install</code> not-found convention).</p> <p>No new lockfile schema bump in Skills-3. <code>tau.toml</code> is re-read from disk on each <code>show</code> invocation (small + fast). Caching capabilities</p> <ul> <li>requires_tools + requires_skills in the lockfile would require Skills-2 schema churn for a marginal perf gain — rejected.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-19"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-19">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <h3 id="default-to-raw-markdown-for---body"><a class="header" href="#default-to-raw-markdown-for---body">Default to raw markdown for <code>--body</code></a></h3> <p>Considered: pipe-friendly out of the box, no rendering hop. Rejected:</p> <ul> <li>Tau's existing precedent (<code>tau chat</code> streams rendered markdown) is render-by-default. Skills should match.</li> <li>The interactive case is the most common one. Render makes content scannable; raw markdown forces the user to mentally parse.</li> <li><code>--raw</code> is one flag away for scripting workflows.</li> </ul> <h3 id="tau-skill-uninstall-name-alias"><a class="header" href="#tau-skill-uninstall-name-alias"><code>tau skill uninstall <name></code> alias</a></h3> <p>Considered: discoverability — a user running <code>tau skill list</code> might look for a parallel <code>tau skill uninstall</code>. Rejected:</p> <ul> <li>Pure alias for the generic <code>tau uninstall <name></code> — no skill-specific behavior.</li> <li>API surface bloat.</li> </ul> <h3 id="cache-capabilities--requires_tools--requires_skills-in-lockfile"><a class="header" href="#cache-capabilities--requires_tools--requires_skills-in-lockfile">Cache <code>capabilities</code> + <code>requires_tools</code> + <code>requires_skills</code> in lockfile</a></h3> <p>Considered: would make <code>show</code> zero-disk-read like <code>list</code>. Rejected:</p> <ul> <li>Skills-2 just shipped lockfile schema v5. Bumping to v6 for marginal perf is churn-without-justification.</li> <li><code>tau.toml</code> reads are fast; one file, small payload.</li> <li>Drift would require another sha256 cache (Skills-2 has one for SKILL.md content; adding another for <code>tau.toml</code> is more surface).</li> </ul> <h3 id="--format-template-flag"><a class="header" href="#--format-template-flag"><code>--format <template></code> flag</a></h3> <p>Considered: power-user feature for scripting. Rejected:</p> <ul> <li><code>--json | jq</code> covers the same use case better.</li> <li>Template language is its own design problem.</li> <li>YAGNI for v1.</li> </ul> <h3 id="--sortinstalled-atversionname"><a class="header" href="#--sortinstalled-atversionname"><code>--sort=installed-at|version|name</code></a></h3> <p>Considered: useful for "what did I install recently?" workflows. Rejected for v1:</p> <ul> <li>Feature surface for the initial ship.</li> <li>Easy additive enhancement when a user asks.</li> <li>Alphabetic by name is the most predictable default.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-24"><a class="header" href="#consequences-24">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>tau-cli</code>'s public surface grows by <code>Command::Skill</code> + <code>SkillSubcommand</code> + <code>SkillListArgs</code> + <code>SkillShowArgs</code>.</li> <li>New <code>crates/tau-cli/src/cmd/skill/</code> module tree (5 files).</li> <li>No <code>tau-pkg</code> or <code>tau-domain</code> changes. Skills-2's <code>LockedSkill</code> schema is consumed read-only.</li> <li><code>cargo-deny</code> allow-list unchanged (no new external deps).</li> <li><code>tau install <skill-pkg></code> + <code>tau skill list</code> + <code>tau skill show</code> now form a complete user-facing workflow for skill packages.</li> <li>Skills-4 (runtime invocation) is unblocked.</li> </ul> <h2 id="out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-4"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-4">Out of scope (deferred to Skills-4+)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Runtime invocation</strong> — <code>agent.<skill-name>.spawn</code> resolution → Skills-4 (the most strategic remaining sub-project).</li> <li><strong>Agent Skills spec export / import</strong> → Skills-5.</li> <li><strong>Reference skill packages + user docs</strong> → Skills-6.</li> <li><strong><code>--sort</code> / filter flags</strong> — additive enhancement when needed.</li> <li><strong>User-customizable termimad skins</strong> — Skills-5 or separate ROADMAP item.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-14"><a class="header" href="#references-14">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-13-skills-3-discovery-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-13-skills-3-discovery.md</code></li> <li>Skills-1 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0025-skills-foundation.md</code></li> <li>Skills-2 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0026-skills-install-pipeline.md</code></li> <li>ROADMAP §16</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0028--docs-deployment-github-pages-auto-cd"><a class="header" href="#adr-0028--docs-deployment-github-pages-auto-cd">ADR-0028 — Docs deployment (GitHub Pages auto-CD)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted 2026-05-13. <strong>Branch / PR:</strong> <code>feat/docs-publish</code> (PR pending). <strong>Spec:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-13-docs-deploy-design.md</code>. <strong>Plan:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-13-docs-deploy.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="context-29"><a class="header" href="#context-29">Context</a></h2> <p>Documentation lives in <code>docs/</code> (Diátaxis structure per QG8) as plain markdown. There is no published site. Contributors and users read docs by browsing the repository on github.com. This is acceptable for a pre-1.0 project but creates two problems as the project matures:</p> <ol> <li>There is no per-version snapshot. A user on <code>tau 0.5</code> reading docs at <code>HEAD</code> sees behavior that may not match their installed version.</li> <li>ADRs, the Constitution, and the cheatsheet are not navigable as a single site with search.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-23"><a class="header" href="#decision-23">Decision</a></h2> <p>Publish <code>docs/</code> as a versioned <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/">mdBook</a> site on GitHub Pages. The site lives on a <code>gh-pages</code> branch with this layout:</p> <ul> <li><code>/</code> redirects to <code>/latest/</code>.</li> <li><code>/latest/</code> is the most recently released build (overwritten each release).</li> <li><code>/v0.X/</code> (pre-1.0) or <code>/vX/</code> (post-1.0) are frozen per-tag builds.</li> <li><code>/preview/pr-NNN/</code> are ephemeral PR-preview builds.</li> <li><code>/versions.json</code> is a manifest for a future version-picker UI.</li> </ul> <p>Deploys are triggered by:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Release tag push</strong> matching <code>v[0-9]+.0.0</code> or <code>v0.[0-9]+.0</code> (major-equivalent bump per QG11): build → publish <code>/vX/</code> + replace <code>/latest/</code>.</li> <li><strong>Push to <code>main</code> with <code>[publish-docs]</code> in the commit message</strong>: replace <code>/latest/</code> only. Force-publish for hot-fixing docs without cutting a release.</li> <li><strong>PR labeled <code>docs:publish</code></strong>: publish ephemeral <code>/preview/pr-NNN/</code>, comment URL on the PR. NEVER touches <code>/latest/</code>.</li> <li><strong><code>workflow_dispatch</code></strong>: manual run.</li> </ol> <p>The deploy uses <code>peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3</code> with <code>keep_files: true</code> to overlay builds into per-version subdirectories without disturbing sibling directories. <code>/latest/</code> and <code>/preview/pr-NNN/</code> are wiped before the overlay (because they represent a single "current" state); <code>/vX/</code> are write-once.</p> <p>A separate PR gate workflow (<code>docs-check.yml</code>) runs <code>mdbook build</code> plus <code>mdbook-linkcheck</code> on every PR that touches <code>docs/**</code> or either workflow file. The gate does not deploy.</p> <h2 id="consequences-25"><a class="header" href="#consequences-25">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Users on a specific tau version can read docs that match.</li> <li>The full site is searchable, navigable, and link-checked.</li> <li>Force-publish marker lets us fix doc typos without a release.</li> <li>PR previews make rendered-doc review possible before merge.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A second markdown source-of-truth surface exists (<code>SUMMARY.md</code>) that must be updated when files are added. Mitigated by the PR gate failing when <code>SUMMARY.md</code> references a missing file.</li> <li>The <code>gh-pages</code> branch must be created manually once before the first deploy.</li> <li>Fork PRs cannot trigger preview deploys (we use <code>pull_request</code> not <code>pull_request_target</code> for security). Acceptable trade-off.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Neutral:</strong></p> <ul> <li>This is a docs-publishing concern only; no Rust code changes.</li> <li>rustdoc is not published as part of this ADR. A follow-up may publish <code>cargo doc</code> output under <code>/api/</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-20"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-20">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>MkDocs / MkDocs Material</strong>: nicer default theme, Python-based. Rejected because it pulls Python into the docs pipeline of an otherwise pure-Rust project, and mdBook is the idiomatic choice (Rust Book, Cargo Book, rustc dev guide all use it).</li> <li><strong>Docusaurus</strong>: built-in versioning and i18n, MDX support. Rejected as overkill — drags Node into docs, far more configuration surface than the project needs.</li> <li><strong>Jekyll (GitHub Pages default)</strong>: zero CI required, but very limited theming and search; harder to extend later.</li> <li><strong><code>actions/deploy-pages</code> with <code>actions/upload-pages-artifact</code></strong>: cleaner atomic single-artifact model, but forces rebuilding the entire multi-version tree on every deploy. Rejected in favor of the overlay model on <code>gh-pages</code>.</li> <li><strong>Single-version (always overwrite)</strong>: simplest, but loses historical docs. Rejected because per-tag snapshots are the motivating use case.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0028--skills-runtime-invocation-skills-4"><a class="header" href="#adr-0028--skills-runtime-invocation-skills-4">ADR-0028 — Skills runtime invocation (Skills-4)</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> <code>tau_runtime::*</code> paths below now read as <code>tau_runtime_core::*</code> for kernel-side symbols and <code>tau_runtime_tokio::*</code> for host-shell symbols. <code>skill.<name>.spawn</code> dispatch lives in <code>tau_runtime_core::orchestration</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted 2026-05-14. <strong>Branch / PR:</strong> <code>feat/skills-4-runtime-invocation</code> (PR pending). <strong>Spec:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-14-skills-4-runtime-invocation-design.md</code> (merged at PR #69). <strong>Plan:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-14-skills-4-runtime-invocation.md</code>. <strong>Depends on:</strong> ADR-0025 (Skills-1), ADR-0026 (Skills-2), ADR-0027 (Skills-3), ADR-0024 (multi-agent orchestration v1.1 + v1.2).</p> <h2 id="context-30"><a class="header" href="#context-30">Context</a></h2> <p>Fourth of 6 sub-projects from ROADMAP §16 (Skills as first-class packages, Constitution G10). The runtime piece that makes installed skills usable by agents.</p> <p>When an agent emits a <code>skill.<name>.spawn</code> virtual tool call, the runtime resolves <code><name></code> to an installed skill, builds a child agent run from the skill's declared <code>system_prompt</code> + capabilities (with <code>${SKILL_DIR}</code> substituted + optional caller <code>scope_paths</code> narrowing), and recursively invokes <code>Runtime::run_with_history</code> via the v1.1 agent-spawn machinery shipped in PR #60.</p> <h2 id="decision-24"><a class="header" href="#decision-24">Decision</a></h2> <p>Three locked decisions (from brainstorming):</p> <h3 id="d1-separate-uri-namespace--capability-variant"><a class="header" href="#d1-separate-uri-namespace--capability-variant">D1: Separate URI namespace + capability variant</a></h3> <p><code>skill.<name>.spawn</code> parallel to existing <code>agent.<kind>.spawn</code>. New <code>Capability::Skill(SkillCapability::Spawn { allowed_skills })</code>.</p> <p>TOML form:</p> <pre><code class="language-toml">[[capabilities]] kind = "skill.spawn" allowed_skills = ["critic", "fact-checker"] </code></pre> <p>No namespace collision possible between custom agent kinds and skill names. Authorization (parent has <code><name></code> in <code>allowed_skills</code>) is enforced in <code>validate_skill_spawn</code>, independent of the agent-spawn authorization path.</p> <h3 id="d2-caller-scope_paths-optionvecstring-narrows-fs-paths-only"><a class="header" href="#d2-caller-scope_paths-optionvecstring-narrows-fs-paths-only">D2: Caller <code>scope_paths: Option<Vec<String>></code> narrows fs.* paths only</a></h3> <p>Per-kind intersection; hard-fail on uncovered <code>scope_path</code> (typo detection); non-fs capabilities pass through unchanged. Caller cannot add new capabilities or change capability kinds — skill author owns the capability contract; caller can tighten scope only.</p> <p>Semantics (per <code>apply_scope_paths</code>):</p> <ul> <li>For each <code>fs.*</code> capability the skill declares, the child's effective paths = intersect(declared paths, <code>scope_paths</code>). Non-fs caps unchanged.</li> <li>If a <code>scope_path</code> is not covered by ANY declared fs.* path → <code>SkillScopePathNotCovered</code> error (typo detection).</li> <li>If intersection is empty for a given fs.* kind → drop that capability entirely.</li> </ul> <h3 id="d3-full-multi-turn-mockllmbackend-test-fixture-in-this-pr"><a class="header" href="#d3-full-multi-turn-mockllmbackend-test-fixture-in-this-pr">D3: Full multi-turn <code>MockLlmBackend</code> test fixture in this PR</a></h3> <p>Lifts the existing <code>ScriptedLlm</code> pattern from <code>tests/run_with_tool_calls.rs</code> into reusable <code>crates/tau-runtime/tests/common/mock_llm.rs</code>. Builder API: <code>MockLlmBackend::new(name).add_text("...").add_tool_call(name, args).add_end()</code>.</p> <p>Bonus: 5 <code>#[ignore]</code>'d orchestration pattern test skeletons from PR #59 are un-ignored using this fixture (Tasks 9 patterns: linear, worker-pool, supervisor-critic, hierarchical, plan-revise).</p> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-21"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-21">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Reuse <code>agent.<kind>.spawn</code> URI for skills</strong> (Option A in brainstorm): namespace collision risk with custom kinds; capability conflation between agent-defined and skill-installed children.</li> <li><strong>Caller-supplied <code>grant: Vec<Capability></code> override</strong> (Option B in brainstorm): too much rope; precedence rules become unnecessary public surface; skill author no longer owns capability contract.</li> <li><strong>No caller knob at all</strong> (Option X in brainstorm): loses per-spawn narrowing use cases (one skill, multiple project scopes).</li> <li><strong>Defer MockLlmBackend to follow-up PR</strong>: weaker Skills-4 coverage; fixture has to be built eventually for the multi-agent pattern tests anyway.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-26"><a class="header" href="#consequences-26">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>tau-domain</code> public surface grows by <code>SkillCapability</code> + <code>Capability::Skill</code> variant + <code>CapabilityShape::SkillSpawn</code>.</li> <li><code>tau-pkg</code> public surface grows by <code>find_installed_skill</code> + <code>InstalledSkill</code> + <code>FindSkillError</code>.</li> <li><code>tau-runtime</code> adds <code>orchestration::skill_resolve</code> module + 5 <code>OrchestrationError</code> variants + <code>validate_skill_spawn</code> + <code>is_skill_spawn</code> branch in <code>run_streaming_inner</code>.</li> <li><code>crates/tau-runtime/tests/common/mock_llm.rs</code> is the canonical multi-turn LLM test fixture — future test suites can reuse. Copied verbatim into <code>crates/tau-cli/tests/common/mock_llm.rs</code> for cross-crate test reuse (~180 LOC; not a real maintenance burden, but ROADMAP-tracked for future shared-test-support extraction).</li> <li>5 previously-<code>#[ignore]</code>'d pattern tests from PR #59 are now running, providing real e2e coverage of multi-agent orchestration patterns.</li> <li>No new external deps.</li> <li>No CI changes.</li> </ul> <h2 id="discovered-during-implementation"><a class="header" href="#discovered-during-implementation">Discovered during implementation</a></h2> <p>Skills-4 T8 e2e tests surfaced three gaps in <code>capability_satisfies</code>:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong><code>Capability::Skill</code> arm missing</strong> — fixed in this PR. Added <code>skill_satisfies</code> helper with <code>string_subset</code> semantics matching <code>agent_satisfies</code>. Without this fix, every <code>skill.<name>.spawn</code> would silently PolicyDeny.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>Capability::TaskList</code> / <code>Capability::Plan</code> arms missing</strong> — fixed independently on main (merged before this PR rebased; visible in <code>capability.rs</code> as <code>task_list_satisfies</code> + <code>plan_satisfies</code> helpers with mode-rank subsumption). Merge resolved by keeping both branches' arms.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>check_capability_subset()</code> uses literal JSON string comparison</strong> (<code>tau-runtime/src/orchestration/virtual_tools.rs</code>): subset law check compares JSON serialisations rather than semantic capability comparison. Means a narrowed <code>agent.spawn(["coder","tester"])</code> isn't recognized as subset of <code>agent.spawn(["team-lead","coder","tester"])</code>. <strong>Still deferred</strong> — T9 pattern D works around by granting the child the full grant. Deserves its own ROADMAP entry.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-5"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-5">Out of scope (deferred to Skills-5+)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Agent Skills spec export / import</strong> → Skills-5</li> <li><strong>Reference skill packages + user docs</strong> → Skills-6</li> <li><strong>Sub-skill <code>requires_skills</code> runtime enforcement</strong> — advisory only</li> <li><strong>Body parse caching across spawns</strong> — YAGNI</li> <li><strong>Caller-side capability merge (<code>grant_extend</code>)</strong> — add when use case surfaces</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-15"><a class="header" href="#references-15">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-14-skills-4-runtime-invocation-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-14-skills-4-runtime-invocation.md</code></li> <li>Skills-1 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0025-skills-foundation.md</code></li> <li>Skills-2 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0026-skills-install-pipeline.md</code></li> <li>Skills-3 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0027-skills-discovery.md</code></li> <li>Multi-agent ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0024-multi-agent-orchestration.md</code></li> <li>Multi-agent v1.1 PR: #60 (recursive <code>agent.<kind>.spawn</code>)</li> <li>Multi-agent v1.2 PR: #61 (per-spawn <code>system_prompt</code>)</li> <li>ROADMAP §16</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0029--skills-anthropic-interop-skills-5"><a class="header" href="#adr-0029--skills-anthropic-interop-skills-5">ADR-0029 — Skills Anthropic interop (Skills-5)</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> runtime references below are split between <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (no_std + alloc kernel) and <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> (host shell).</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted 2026-05-16. <strong>Branch / PR:</strong> <code>feat/skills-5-anthropic-interop-design</code> (PR #102). <strong>Spec:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-skills-5-anthropic-interop-design.md</code>. <strong>Plan:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-skills-5-anthropic-interop.md</code>. <strong>Depends on:</strong> ADR-0025 (Skills-1), ADR-0026 (Skills-2), ADR-0027 (Skills-3), ADR-0028 (Skills-4).</p> <h2 id="context-31"><a class="header" href="#context-31">Context</a></h2> <p>Fifth of 6 sub-projects from ROADMAP §16. Skills-1 established the two-layer architecture ("a tau skill IS an Anthropic skill plus tau.toml"). Skills-5 ships the tooling that makes that bidirectional in practice: import vanilla Anthropic skills into tau, export tau-installed skills back to vanilla Anthropic format, and validate Anthropic-conformance of installed skills.</p> <h2 id="decision-25"><a class="header" href="#decision-25">Decision</a></h2> <p>Five locked decisions:</p> <h3 id="d1--bidirectional-scope-export--import--conformance"><a class="header" href="#d1--bidirectional-scope-export--import--conformance">D1 — Bidirectional scope (export + import + conformance)</a></h3> <p>Picked from a 4-option scope question (export-only / bidirectional / conformance-only / extension-key full-interop). Bidirectional gives ergonomic UX for the common "consume an Anthropic skill from GitHub" flow; conformance closes the validation loop. The <code>x-tau-capabilities</code> YAML extension for round-trippable export of capability-bearing skills was rejected as premature — only export-without-capabilities use case is concrete today.</p> <h3 id="d2--both-auto-detect-inside-tau-install-and-explicit-tau-skill-import"><a class="header" href="#d2--both-auto-detect-inside-tau-install-and-explicit-tau-skill-import">D2 — Both auto-detect inside <code>tau install</code> AND explicit <code>tau skill import</code></a></h3> <p><code>tau install <src></code> detects Anthropic format and synthesizes a <code>tau.toml</code> transparently (ergonomic happy path). <code>tau skill import <src> --output <dir></code> produces an editable directory so users can inspect or customize the synthesized tau.toml before installing.</p> <h3 id="d3--capabilities-dropped-on-export"><a class="header" href="#d3--capabilities-dropped-on-export">D3 — Capabilities dropped on export</a></h3> <p>Synthesized manifests start <code>capabilities = []</code>. Skill authors who want capabilities must add them by hand (via <code>tau skill import</code> + edit). On export, capabilities (and <code>requires_skills</code>) are silently dropped from the output with an stderr note. <code>tau skill export --strict</code> makes drops a hard error.</p> <p>For non-SKILL.md content (refs/, assets/, etc.), export uses a simple <strong>copy-everything-except-tau.toml</strong> strategy. <code>SkillManifest</code> does not currently carry a <code>files</code> glob (Skills-1 schema), so this is the natural approach: the install pipeline already copies the full source tree into <code><scope>/.tau/packages/<name>/<version>/</code>, and export walks that directory verbatim minus <code>tau.toml</code>.</p> <h3 id="d4--lockfile-schema-v5--v6-with-synthesized_from"><a class="header" href="#d4--lockfile-schema-v5--v6-with-synthesized_from">D4 — Lockfile schema v5 → v6 with <code>synthesized_from</code></a></h3> <p><code>LockedPackage.synthesized_from: Option<SynthesizedSource></code> records the manifest origin. Enum currently has one variant: <code>SynthesizedSource::Anthropic</code>. Field defaults to <code>None</code> for v5 entries on read; lockfile auto-upgrades to v6 on next write (existing pattern from v4→v5 in PR #64). <code>tau skill show</code> displays <code>Source format: synthesized (Anthropic Agent Skills)</code> when the field is <code>Some</code>.</p> <h3 id="d5--tau-verify---anthropic-strict"><a class="header" href="#d5--tau-verify---anthropic-strict">D5 — <code>tau verify --anthropic-strict</code></a></h3> <p>New flag on the existing <code>tau verify</code> command. Without the flag, behavior unchanged. With the flag, additionally checks each installed skill against Anthropic SKILL.md conformance:</p> <ul> <li>Frontmatter must parse as valid YAML with required <code>name</code> + <code>description</code></li> <li><code>description</code> must be non-whitespace</li> <li>Body must be non-whitespace</li> </ul> <p>Emits <code>VerifyStatus::AnthropicConformance { skill_name, issue }</code> with <code>AnthropicConformanceIssue::{MissingDescription, EmptyBody, MalformedFrontmatter}</code> failure modes.</p> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-22"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-22">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Conformance-only Skills-5</strong> (no commands, just validation in <code>tau install</code> + <code>tau verify --anthropic-strict</code>). Rejected: import is the highest-leverage ergonomic feature; defers the most valuable UX gain.</li> <li><strong>Export-only Skills-5</strong> (no import). Rejected for the same reason.</li> <li><strong>Auto-detect only inside <code>tau install</code></strong> (no explicit <code>tau skill import</code>). Rejected: power users want to inspect/edit the synthesized tau.toml; without explicit import, they'd have to edit the on-disk install location post-fact (awkward).</li> <li><strong>Explicit <code>tau skill import</code> only</strong> (no auto-detect). Rejected: forces every user to know about format mismatch and run extra steps; common case should Just Work.</li> <li><strong><code>x-tau-capabilities</code> YAML extension key for round-trippable export.</strong> Rejected: YAGNI; no real use case yet for round-trip with capability preservation.</li> <li><strong>Plural-format <code>--format <foo></code> flag.</strong> Rejected: only Anthropic format is in scope; premature plumbing.</li> <li><strong>Bulk export (<code>tau skill export --all</code>).</strong> Rejected: YAGNI; trivially scriptable via <code>tau skill list --json | jq | xargs</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-27"><a class="header" href="#consequences-27">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong><code>tau-domain</code></strong> public surface grows by <code>SkillFormat</code>, <code>detect_format</code>, <code>synthesize_manifest_from_skill_md</code>, <code>SynthesizeError</code>.</li> <li><strong><code>tau-pkg</code></strong> public surface grows by new <code>synthesize</code> module (<code>synthesize_anthropic_skill</code> + tau-pkg's own <code>SynthesizeError</code>) + <code>SynthesizedSource</code> + 2 new <code>InstallError</code> variants (<code>NotASkillPackage</code>, <code>SynthesizeFailed</code>) + <code>AnthropicConformanceIssue</code> + new <code>VerifyStatus::AnthropicConformance</code> variant + <code>verify_all_with_options(scope, anthropic_strict)</code> entry point. Existing <code>verify_all</code> preserved as a delegating wrapper.</li> <li><strong><code>tau-pkg::install</code></strong>: Anthropic-format installs now write the synthesized <code>tau.toml</code> to disk at <code><scope>/.tau/packages/<name>/<version>/tau.toml</code> — surfaced during T7 integration as a gap; without it <code>tau skill show</code> + <code>tau skill export</code> couldn't operate on Anthropic-installed packages.</li> <li><strong><code>tau-cli</code></strong> public surface grows by <code>SkillSubcommand::{Import, Export}</code> + <code>--anthropic-strict</code> flag on <code>tau verify</code>.</li> <li><strong>Lockfile schema v6</strong> (additive); v5 reads cleanly with <code>synthesized_from = None</code>; v5→v6 upgrade is automatic on next write.</li> <li><strong><code>tau skill import</code> URL handling</strong>: All Git-scheme URLs (including <code>file://</code>) route through <code>git clone</code>. Only bare local paths (no scheme) use filesystem copy. This was a T7 integration fix.</li> <li><strong>No new external dependencies.</strong> No CI changes.</li> </ul> <h2 id="discovered-during-implementation-1"><a class="header" href="#discovered-during-implementation-1">Discovered during implementation</a></h2> <p>Two T7 integration gaps surfaced and were fixed in scope:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Synthesized <code>tau.toml</code> was never written to the install directory.</strong> T3 added the in-memory manifest synthesis path but kept the install behavior unchanged in terms of what landed on disk. <code>tau skill show</code> + <code>tau skill export</code> failed for Anthropic-installed skills because they require <code>tau.toml</code> to exist. Fixed by writing the synthesized manifest to the staging directory before the staging→final rename.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>tau skill import</code> treated <code>file://</code> URLs as local-path fs copies.</strong> For bare git repos, this copied <code>.git/</code> metadata instead of working-tree content. Fixed by routing all Git-scheme URLs (including <code>file://</code>) through <code>git clone</code>; only bare local paths now use fs copy.</p> </li> </ol> <p>Both gaps blocked the Skills-5 user story end-to-end. T7's roundtrip e2e tests caught them; the fix landed in scope so the un-ignored tests pass.</p> <h2 id="out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-6--future"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-deferred-to-skills-6--future">Out of scope (deferred to Skills-6+ / future)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Reference skill packages</strong> themselves — Skills-6.</li> <li><strong>Sub-skill <code>requires_skills</code> cross-format mapping</strong> — silently dropped on export (advisory only).</li> <li><strong>Conformance against future Anthropic spec revisions</strong> — re-evaluate when the next major spec lands.</li> <li><strong><code>tau skill convert</code></strong> as an alias or alternative to import/export — Skills-5 v2 if requested.</li> <li><strong>MCP-adjacent interop</strong> (consuming MCP server descriptors as tau skills) — separate sub-project; out of ROADMAP §16 scope.</li> <li><strong><code>x-tau-capabilities</code> YAML extension key</strong> for capability preservation across export — revisit if a concrete use case emerges.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-16"><a class="header" href="#references-16">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-skills-5-anthropic-interop-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-skills-5-anthropic-interop.md</code></li> <li>Skills-1 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0025-skills-foundation.md</code></li> <li>Skills-2 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0026-skills-install-pipeline.md</code></li> <li>Skills-3 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0027-skills-discovery.md</code></li> <li>Skills-4 ADR: <code>docs/decisions/0028-skills-runtime-invocation.md</code></li> <li>ROADMAP §16</li> <li>Priority queue: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-12-post-multi-agent-priority-queue.md</code></li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0030--skills-reference-packages--user-docs-skills-6"><a class="header" href="#adr-0030--skills-reference-packages--user-docs-skills-6">ADR-0030 — Skills reference packages + user docs (Skills-6)</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> runtime references below are split between <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (no_std + alloc kernel) and <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> (host shell).</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted 2026-05-16. <strong>Branch / PR:</strong> <code>feat/skills-6-reference-packages</code> (PR #115). <strong>Spec:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-skills-6-reference-packages-design.md</code>. <strong>Plan:</strong> <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-16-skills-6-reference-packages.md</code>. <strong>Depends on:</strong> ADR-0025 (Skills-1), ADR-0026 (Skills-2), ADR-0027 (Skills-3), ADR-0028 (Skills-4), ADR-0029 (Skills-5).</p> <h2 id="context-32"><a class="header" href="#context-32">Context</a></h2> <p>Final sub-project of ROADMAP §16. Skills-1 through Skills-5 built the infrastructure; Skills-6 ships the <strong>content</strong> that turns the infrastructure into a complete, usable product:</p> <ul> <li>3 exemplary skill packages under <code>skills/</code> (critic, fact-checker, pr-reviewer) covering pure-prompt / fs.read / process.spawn axes.</li> <li>6 mdBook documentation pages filling all four Diátaxis quadrants.</li> <li>9 end-to-end integration tests proving the user story works in CI across Linux, macOS, Windows.</li> </ul> <p>After Skills-6, a new contributor can clone tau, build it, install a reference skill, render it, and export it back to Anthropic format — the entire Skills track makes sense end-to-end without prior knowledge.</p> <h2 id="decision-26"><a class="header" href="#decision-26">Decision</a></h2> <p>Three locked decisions:</p> <h3 id="d1--three-reference-skills-covering-three-capability-axes"><a class="header" href="#d1--three-reference-skills-covering-three-capability-axes">D1 — Three reference skills covering three capability axes</a></h3> <ul> <li><code>critic</code> (no capabilities) → Anthropic-roundtrip proof</li> <li><code>fact-checker</code> (fs.read on <code>${SKILL_DIR}/references/**</code>) → substitution + multi-file</li> <li><code>pr-reviewer</code> (process.spawn on git + rg) → third axis</li> </ul> <p>Rejected: 1-skill (too minimal) and 2-skill (skips the process.spawn axis).</p> <h3 id="d2--add-only-no-refactor-of-existing-tempdir-test-fixtures"><a class="header" href="#d2--add-only-no-refactor-of-existing-tempdir-test-fixtures">D2 — Add-only: no refactor of existing tempdir test fixtures</a></h3> <p>Skills-1–5 inline-synthesize critic fixtures in 10+ test files. Refactoring them to reference <code>skills/critic/</code> would risk subtle regressions and merge conflicts with parallel Claude sessions for marginal benefit. Skills-6 ADDS new integration tests against the in-tree skills; existing fixtures stay as-is.</p> <h3 id="d3--full-diátaxis-mdbook-documentation"><a class="header" href="#d3--full-diátaxis-mdbook-documentation">D3 — Full Diátaxis mdBook documentation</a></h3> <p>mdBook is already wired with the four Diátaxis quadrants (tutorials / how-to / reference / explanation). Skills-6 fills each quadrant: tutorial (narrative walkthrough), 3 how-to recipes, manifest schema reference, two-layer architecture explanation. Auto-deploys to GitHub Pages via PR #67's existing workflow.</p> <p>Rejected: in-repo README only (under-invests in user-facing surface); how-to + reference only (lacks tutorial narrative + explanation anchoring).</p> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-23"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-23">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li>1-skill scope (just critic). Rejected: doesn't prove capability story.</li> <li>2-skill scope (critic + fact-checker, no pr-reviewer). Rejected: skips the process.spawn capability axis.</li> <li>Refactor existing test fixtures. Rejected: 10+ files touched, refactor risk, merge-conflict risk.</li> <li>Separate <code>tau-skills</code> git repo. Rejected: in-tree is fine for proof-of-concept; external repo addressable when external versioning needs emerge.</li> <li>In-repo README only. Rejected: mdBook is already wired + auto-deploys.</li> <li>Tutorial-only docs. Rejected: reference + explanation are load-bearing for authoring + understanding.</li> <li><code>tau skill new <name></code> scaffolding command. Rejected: useful but separate sub-project; not blocking the user story Skills-6 ships.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-28"><a class="header" href="#consequences-28">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>New top-level <code>skills/</code> directory</strong> (sibling to <code>crates/</code>). Future reference skills land here.</li> <li><strong>New <code>docs/tutorials/build-your-first-skill.md</code></strong>, three <code>docs/how-to/</code> recipes, <code>docs/reference/skill-manifest-schema.md</code>, <code>docs/explanation/two-layer-skills.md</code>. All indexed in <code>docs/SUMMARY.md</code>.</li> <li><strong>9 new integration tests</strong> across <code>crates/tau-pkg/tests/</code> and <code>crates/tau-cli/tests/</code>. Existing tests untouched.</li> <li><strong><code>.gitattributes</code></strong> forces LF on <code>skills/**/SKILL.md</code> to keep the byte-identical export roundtrip test passing on Windows.</li> <li><strong>No new external dependencies. No CI changes.</strong> The new tests run under the existing <code>test-stable</code> matrix.</li> </ul> <h2 id="closes-roadmap-16"><a class="header" href="#closes-roadmap-16">Closes ROADMAP §16</a></h2> <p>Skills-6 is the final sub-project of the Skills track. ROADMAP §16 is complete after this PR merges. Future Skills work is additive (more reference packages, <code>tau skill new</code>, marketplace, etc.) and sits outside §16.</p> <h2 id="references-17"><a class="header" href="#references-17">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-16-skills-6-reference-packages-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-16-skills-6-reference-packages.md</code></li> <li>Predecessor ADRs: 0025 (foundation), 0026 (install pipeline), 0027 (discovery), 0028 (runtime invocation), 0029 (Anthropic interop)</li> <li>ROADMAP §16</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0031-tau-observe-as-the-canonical-tracing-subscriber-init-crate"><a class="header" href="#adr-0031-tau-observe-as-the-canonical-tracing-subscriber-init-crate">ADR-0031: <code>tau-observe</code> as the canonical tracing-subscriber init crate</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> <code>tau-observe</code> remains the canonical tracing-subscriber init crate for the tokio host shell. The executor-agnostic kernel (<code>tau-runtime-core</code>, β.1) keeps a <code>#[doc(hidden)]</code> mirror of the §3.9 vocabulary; a drift test in <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> cross-checks both lists.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="status"><a class="header" href="#status">Status</a></h2> <p>Accepted. Implemented in PR <number-to-fill-at-merge-time>.</p> <h2 id="context-33"><a class="header" href="#context-33">Context</a></h2> <p><code>tracing</code> adoption (ADR-0006 §3.9, NG9) leaves subscriber install to the caller. In practice every tau binary/library that produces logs has re-implemented the same <code>tracing_subscriber::fmt()</code> + <code>EnvFilter</code> dance. Two near-identical implementations exist today:</p> <ul> <li><code>crates/tau-cli/src/tracing.rs</code> — human format to stderr, CLI-flag-to- filter mapping, panicking <code>init()</code>.</li> <li><code>crates/tau-plugin-sdk/src/tracing_layer.rs</code> — JSON to stderr, idempotent <code>Once</code>-gated install.</li> </ul> <p>Sub-projects B (§3.9 span vocabulary), C (preview helpers), D (workflow</p> <ul> <li>recording as <code>Layer</code>s), E (<code>tracing-appender</code>), F (OTLP export) all need a single place that owns the subscriber registry. Continuing to add layers from two different crates with two different init policies would lock in the divergence.</li> </ul> <h2 id="decision-27"><a class="header" href="#decision-27">Decision</a></h2> <p>Promote the existing <code>tau-observe</code> crate (currently a stub) to the canonical owner of:</p> <ul> <li><code>tau_observe::install::install(InstallOptions) -> Result<InstallGuard, InstallError></code> with idempotent global init and an <code>InstallGuard</code> that future sub- projects can hang flush behavior off (sub-project E).</li> <li><code>tau_observe::filter::env_or_directive(&str) -> EnvFilter</code> — the only place that interprets <code>RUST_LOG</code>.</li> <li><code>tau_observe::vocabulary</code> — <code>&'static str</code> constants for every §3.9 span and event name.</li> </ul> <p><code>tau-cli</code> and <code>tau-plugin-sdk</code> keep their public <code>install</code> functions (signatures unchanged) but their bodies become one-liners that build the appropriate <code>InstallOptions</code> and delegate to <code>tau_observe::install</code>.</p> <h2 id="consequences-29"><a class="header" href="#consequences-29">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>One subscriber init code path. Sub-projects B/C/D/E/F each layer onto this surface without further divergence.</li> <li><code>tau-observe</code> becomes a workspace dependency. Build time impact is negligible (the crate has three direct deps; all are already in the workspace).</li> <li>Plugin authors who previously imported <code>tau_plugin_sdk::tracing_layer</code> see no source-level change; the layer continues to be re-exported.</li> <li>NG9 still holds: <code>tau-observe</code> exposes helpers but does not enforce any redaction policy on the caller.</li> </ul> <h2 id="trigger-to-revisit"><a class="header" href="#trigger-to-revisit">Trigger to revisit</a></h2> <p>A second subscriber init pattern lands that doesn't fit <code>InstallOptions</code> (e.g. multi-sink, dynamic reconfiguration). At that point reconsider whether <code>tau-observe::install</code> should grow or whether a layered API (<code>tau_observe::build_layers() -> impl Layer<S></code>) is a better surface.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0032-relocate-capabilityoverride-from-tau-runtime-to-tau-pkg"><a class="header" href="#adr-0032-relocate-capabilityoverride-from-tau-runtime-to-tau-pkg">ADR-0032: Relocate CapabilityOverride from tau-runtime to tau-pkg</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> <code>tau-runtime</code> has since split into <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (kernel) + <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> (host shell). The <code>tau-pkg</code> location for <code>CapabilityOverride</code> is unchanged.</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-17 <strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <h2 id="context-34"><a class="header" href="#context-34">Context</a></h2> <p><code>CapabilityOverride</code> was introduced in tau-runtime as part of Tier 2 priority 4 (capability override implementation, see ROADMAP). The type describes how a project's <code>tau.toml</code> <code>[[agents.<id>.capabilities]]</code> block narrows the grants in a package manifest. Until now, the canonical home was <code>tau_runtime::capability_override</code>.</p> <p>Phase 1 priority §15 (<code>tau serve</code> mode) requires a new binary in <code>tau-app</code> that resolves agents and constructs runtime invocations. To avoid a dependency cycle once <code>tau-cli</code> depends on <code>tau-app</code> for the <code>tau serve</code> subcommand wiring, the project-config types (<code>AgentEntry</code>, <code>ProjectConfig</code>, <code>build_agent_definition</code>) move from <code>tau-cli</code> to <code>tau-pkg</code> (see the diff in this PR's first commit and §13 in the tau-serve-mode spec).</p> <p>Project-config types reference <code>CapabilityOverride</code> directly — a <code>tau.toml</code> agent entry CAN contain a <code>[capabilities]</code> override that the kernel applies at runtime. Moving project config into <code>tau-pkg</code> would create a cycle:</p> <pre><code>tau-pkg::project ──imports──► tau_runtime::CapabilityOverride tau-runtime ───────────────► tau-pkg (existing dep) </code></pre> <p>Two ways to break the cycle:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Don't import the type.</strong> tau-pkg::project keeps the field but uses a sentinel type (<code>serde_json::Value</code>, a string, a private wrapper). Defers the binding to runtime call sites. Worse ergonomics; loses compile-time validation.</li> <li><strong>Move <code>CapabilityOverride</code> to tau-pkg.</strong> The type is more naturally a tau-pkg concept anyway — it lives in <code>tau.toml</code>, which tau-pkg owns. tau-runtime keeps the public symbol via a re-export shim.</li> </ol> <p>Constitution G6 / QG12: tau-runtime's public API surface is one of two SemVer-stable commitments. Per QG18, changes to that surface require an ADR. This ADR records the relocation.</p> <h2 id="decision-28"><a class="header" href="#decision-28">Decision</a></h2> <p><code>CapabilityOverride</code>, <code>EffectiveCapability</code>, <code>OverrideExpandError</code>, <code>compute_effective</code>, and the <code>glob_subset</code> helper move from <code>crates/tau-runtime/src/capability_override/</code> to <code>crates/tau-pkg/src/capability_override/</code>.</p> <p><code>crates/tau-runtime/src/capability_override/mod.rs</code> becomes a thin re-export shim:</p> <pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust"><span class="boring">#![allow(unused)] </span><span class="boring">fn main() { </span>pub use tau_pkg::capability_override::*; <span class="boring">}</span></code></pre></pre> <p><code>tau-runtime</code>'s public API is unchanged from a consumer's perspective — <code>tau_runtime::CapabilityOverride</code> and friends remain importable at the same paths and resolve to identical types. Direct importers from <code>tau_pkg::capability_override</code> are also supported (and preferred for new code).</p> <p>The relocation is purely a refactor: no behavior change, no SemVer-breaking change, no test deltas in this PR.</p> <h2 id="consequences-30"><a class="header" href="#consequences-30">Consequences</a></h2> <h3 id="positive-11"><a class="header" href="#positive-11">Positive</a></h3> <ul> <li>Breaks the dependency cycle that would have blocked Phase 1 §15.</li> <li><code>CapabilityOverride</code> now lives next to the types it operates on (<code>AgentEntry</code>, <code>ProjectConfig</code>, lockfile entries). Reduces conceptual scatter.</li> <li>Future tau bindings (<code>tau-app::serve</code>, hypothetical <code>tau-tui</code>, etc.) can import directly from tau-pkg without pulling in the full runtime.</li> </ul> <h3 id="negative-7"><a class="header" href="#negative-7">Negative</a></h3> <ul> <li><code>tau-runtime</code> now has a re-export shim that future maintainers must remember exists. If <code>tau-runtime::capability_override::mod.rs</code> is ever rewritten without the re-export, downstream importers break.</li> <li>One more crate-level entry point that needs versioning discipline. <code>tau-pkg</code> is also a public-surface concern per G6 (the lockfile + manifest formats are stable surfaces), so this isn't a new responsibility category, just a new symbol within it.</li> </ul> <h3 id="neutral-2"><a class="header" href="#neutral-2">Neutral</a></h3> <ul> <li>No ADR amendments required to ADR-0006 / ADR-0007 / ADR-0014 (which introduced and refined the capability machinery). Those ADRs described semantics; the location was not load-bearing.</li> </ul> <h3 id="follow-ups"><a class="header" href="#follow-ups">Follow-ups</a></h3> <ul> <li>A future ADR may officially deprecate the <code>tau_runtime::capability_override</code> re-export and point all consumers at <code>tau_pkg::capability_override</code>. Not in scope for this ADR; the shim has zero cost as long as it stays.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-24"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-24">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Alternative</th><th>Why rejected</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Keep <code>CapabilityOverride</code> in <code>tau-runtime</code>, change <code>tau-pkg::project</code> field to opaque <code>Value</code> or wrapper</td><td>Loses compile-time validation. Pushes type-correctness into runtime checks. Bad ergonomics for tau-pkg's downstream consumers.</td></tr> <tr><td>Keep <code>CapabilityOverride</code> in <code>tau-runtime</code>, duplicate logic in <code>tau-app::serve</code> (don't lift project config to tau-pkg)</td><td>Creates two implementations of <code>build_agent_definition</code> (tau-cli + tau-app). Drift risk. The same forces that motivated lifting project config to tau-pkg apply here.</td></tr> <tr><td>Move both <code>project</code> AND <code>capability_override</code> to a new <code>tau-config</code> crate</td><td>Crate proliferation (tau already has 14 crates). YAGNI — no third consumer in sight.</td></tr> <tr><td>Keep status quo, accept dependency cycle</td><td>Cargo does not permit dependency cycles. Not an option.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="references-18"><a class="header" href="#references-18">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Constitution G6, QG12, QG18.</li> <li>ROADMAP §15 (tau serve mode), §4 (capability override implementation).</li> <li>This PR: <code>refactor: lift tau-cli::config to tau-pkg::project</code> (#133).</li> <li>Spec for tau-serve-mode: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-17-tau-serve-mode-design.md</code> §13.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0033-tau-serve-mode-v1--json-rpc-20-over-ndjson-framed-stdio"><a class="header" href="#adr-0033-tau-serve-mode-v1--json-rpc-20-over-ndjson-framed-stdio">ADR-0033: Tau serve mode v1 — JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON-framed stdio</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> runtime references below are split between <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (no_std + alloc kernel) and <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> (host shell, where serve-mode lives).</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-17 <strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <h2 id="context-35"><a class="header" href="#context-35">Context</a></h2> <p>Phase 1 priority §15. Constitution G6 / QG12 commit to two public API surfaces: the <code>tau-runtime</code> Rust crate and a serve-mode IPC protocol. Serve mode has been deferred since Phase 0 — the empty <code>tau-app</code> crate was reserved for it. Phase 1 cannot close without it: Phase 3+ SDKs (npm/pip/etc.) wrap this protocol, IDE integrations have no embedding path otherwise, and high-throughput consumers can't amortize tau's plugin cold-start cost.</p> <p>Per QG18, this ADR is required because serve mode is one of the two public API surfaces; SemVer applies.</p> <p>See the spec at <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-17-tau-serve-mode-design.md</code> for full motivation and design.</p> <h2 id="decision-29"><a class="header" href="#decision-29">Decision</a></h2> <p>Ship v1 of serve mode as JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON-framed stdio.</p> <p><strong>Method surface (5 methods + 1 notification):</strong></p> <ul> <li><code>meta.handshake</code> — first call, establishes protocol_version. Required before any non-meta method.</li> <li><code>meta.ping</code> — liveness check; works pre-handshake.</li> <li><code>runtime.run</code> — batch agent run; returns RunOutcome.</li> <li><code>runtime.run_streaming</code> — streaming agent run; emits <code>runtime.event</code> notifications correlated by request id, then a final response.</li> <li><code>runtime.cancel</code> — cancel an in-flight request by id (cooperative cancellation).</li> <li><code>runtime.event</code> — server-initiated notification carrying a <code>RunEvent</code> payload (TextDelta, ToolCallStarted, ToolCallCompleted, TurnCompleted, RunCompleted, FatalError).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Wire format:</strong> newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) over the child's stdin/stdout. Each JSON value occupies exactly one line.</p> <p><strong>Lifecycle:</strong> one <code>tau-runtime::Runtime</code> per process. Built at startup from <code>--project <path></code> (defaults to cwd). All RPC calls share the runtime via <code>Arc<Runtime></code>. Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM / SIGINT / stdin EOF / parent death (<code>PR_SET_PDEATHSIG</code> on Linux). Configurable max_concurrent cap (default 8); <code>--idle-timeout</code> initiates graceful shutdown on no activity.</p> <p><strong>Reuses <code>RunEvent</code> shape canonicalized by ADR-0011.</strong> Each <code>RunEvent</code> becomes one <code>runtime.event</code> notification with the variant name as <code>kind</code> and the variant payload as <code>data</code>.</p> <p><strong>Tau-namespaced JSON-RPC error codes in -32000..-32099:</strong> HANDSHAKE_MISMATCH (-32000), CANCELLED (-32001), HANDSHAKE_REQUIRED (-32002), ALREADY_HANDSHAKEN (-32003), SERVER_BUSY (-32004), PROJECT_ERROR (-32005), RUNTIME_ERROR (-32006), CAPABILITY_DENIED (-32007), TOOL_ERROR (-32008), LLM_ERROR (-32009), UNKNOWN_AGENT (-32010). -32011..-32099 reserved for future ADR amendments.</p> <h2 id="consequences-31"><a class="header" href="#consequences-31">Consequences</a></h2> <h3 id="positive-12"><a class="header" href="#positive-12">Positive</a></h3> <ul> <li>Phase 1 closes once this lands. Phase 2 (tau as a compiled language for agentic workflows) becomes the active phase.</li> <li><code>tau-app</code> crate exits stub status; gains the <code>serve</code> module (~2k LOC across 13 submodules).</li> <li>Serve mode is a versioned public surface. Future additive method namespaces (<code>session.*</code>, <code>pkg.*</code>, <code>skill.*</code>, <code>workflow.*</code>) land via ADR amendments.</li> <li>External SDKs and IDE integrations now have a stable embedding path.</li> </ul> <h3 id="negative--new-surface"><a class="header" href="#negative--new-surface">Negative / new surface</a></h3> <ul> <li><strong>New public method on <code>tau-runtime::RuntimeBuilder</code></strong>: <code>build_allow_empty()</code> — same semantics as <code>build()</code> but skips the <code>NoLlmBackend</code> check. Required because serve mode must boot even when the project has no agents (handshake reports <code>agents: []</code>; calls to <code>runtime.run</code> then return <code>-32010 UNKNOWN_AGENT</code>). This is a strict additive change to tau-runtime's public API (existing <code>build()</code> behavior is unchanged).</li> <li>Plugin host integration in serve mode uses default <code>PluginHostOptions</code> (no recorder, synthetic TraceContext, no sandbox enforcement). Real sandbox honoring is deferred. Production deployments that need sandboxed serve-mode plugin hosts should track a follow-up.</li> <li>Per-tool config selectors not implemented — all tools receive <code>{}</code> config in v1. Future enhancement.</li> </ul> <h3 id="ci-gate"><a class="header" href="#ci-gate">CI gate</a></h3> <ul> <li>No new CI job required. The existing <code>test-stable</code> job runs <code>cargo nextest run --profile ci --workspace --all-targets</code>, which covers <code>tau-app</code> (Layer 2 in-process tests) and <code>tau-cli</code> (Layer 3 e2e serve tests) because both crates are workspace members. <code>CARGO_BIN_EXE_tau</code> is populated automatically by nextest's binary build phase before the integration tests run.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-25"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-25">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Alternative</th><th>Why rejected</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>JSON-RPC 2.0 + LSP-style framing (Content-Length headers)</td><td>More complex parser; harder to debug with shell pipes; no current IDE-extension consumer to justify it. Additive opt-in possible later via <code>--transport lsp</code>.</td></tr> <tr><td>MessagePack-RPC</td><td>Diverges from Constitution wording ("JSON-RPC over stdio"); requires Constitution amendment. External SDK clients in every language would need msgpack libs. Loses the operational property that anyone can debug the protocol with <code>cat</code>/<code>jq</code>.</td></tr> <tr><td>HTTP transport</td><td>Tau is not a hosted service (NG3) and explicitly does no auth (NG9). Subprocess-over-stdio is the lightest possible IPC. HTTP would add attack surface the design rejects.</td></tr> <tr><td>Per-call project switching</td><td>RuntimeBuilder is expensive (tau.toml parse, dep resolution, plugin spawn, capability shape build). Building per call defeats cold-start-amortization.</td></tr> <tr><td>Full CLI parity in v1</td><td>15-method surface locked forever. Forces premature decisions about session/skill/pkg method shapes. v1 ships kernel; later ADRs add increments.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h2 id="follow-ups-deferred"><a class="header" href="#follow-ups-deferred">Follow-ups (deferred)</a></h2> <ul> <li>Session/persistence methods (<code>session.*</code>). Phase 1 §11 already exposes these via CLI; serve-mode coverage waits for concrete demand.</li> <li>Package management methods (<code>pkg.*</code>). External orchestrators can shell out to <code>tau install</code> / <code>tau resolve</code> as setup steps before <code>tau serve</code>.</li> <li>Skill / workflow methods. Same reasoning.</li> <li>LSP-style framing transport via <code>--transport lsp</code>.</li> <li>Sandbox enforcement (currently bypassed via <code>sandbox_plan = None</code> in build_runtime).</li> <li>Per-tool config selectors (all tools currently receive <code>{}</code>).</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-19"><a class="header" href="#references-19">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Constitution G6, QG12, QG18.</li> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-17-tau-serve-mode-design.md</code>.</li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-17-tau-serve-mode.md</code>.</li> <li>ADR-0011 (RunEvent canonical shape).</li> <li>ADR-0032 (CapabilityOverride relocation; sibling refactor).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0034-tau-target-triple-registry"><a class="header" href="#adr-0034-tau-target-triple-registry">ADR-0034: Tau target triple registry</a></h1> <blockquote> <p><strong>Updated 2026-05-31 (β.1.4):</strong> the triple registry on <code>tau-ports</code> is unchanged; only the runtime crate split (<code>tau-runtime</code> → <code>tau-runtime-core</code> + <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code>) affected the downstream targets table.</p> </blockquote> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-19 <strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <h2 id="context-36"><a class="header" href="#context-36">Context</a></h2> <p>Phase 2 §B per ROADMAP.md. Tau treats agent workflows as a compiled language (see <code>docs/explanation/tau-as-language.md</code>): write a tau program once, compile it for a sandbox target triple, and the bundle runs anywhere a matching adapter exists. §C (<code>tau build --target</code>) will produce content-hashed deployment bundles pinning a target; §D will guarantee forward-compat for capability vocabulary. Both §C and §D need a stable, parseable, structural identifier for what a bundle is built for.</p> <p>Before this ADR, target triples were informal strings only in <code>tau-as-language.md</code> prose (<code>linux-native-strict</code>, <code>container-podman</code>, <code>remote-vercel</code>, <code>wasi-p2</code>). The shapes were inconsistent and the identifiers were not code-callable.</p> <h2 id="decision-30"><a class="header" href="#decision-30">Decision</a></h2> <p>Codify the target triple as a Bazel-inspired 3-axis structural identifier living in <code>tau-ports::target</code>:</p> <ul> <li><code>Platform</code>: Linux | Darwin | Windows | Any</li> <li><code>AdapterFamily</code>: Native | Container | Remote | Wasi | Passthrough</li> <li><code>SandboxTier</code>: Strict | Light | None (existing in <code>tau-ports</code>)</li> </ul> <p>Canonical display: <code><platform>-<adapter>-<tier></code>. Single-segment <code>passthrough</code> is a reserved special.</p> <p>Adapter ↔ triple satisfaction is a struct comparison: an adapter satisfies a triple when its platform set includes the triple's platform, its <code>RegistryKind</code> maps to the triple's <code>AdapterFamily</code>, and its <code>tiers_supported</code> contains the triple's tier.</p> <p>v1 ships 5 Available triples and reserves 3 namespaces:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Triple</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>linux-native-strict</code></td><td>Available</td></tr> <tr><td><code>linux-native-light</code></td><td>Available</td></tr> <tr><td><code>linux-container-strict</code></td><td>Available</td></tr> <tr><td><code>darwin-native-strict</code></td><td>Available</td></tr> <tr><td><code>passthrough</code></td><td>Available</td></tr> <tr><td><code>windows-native-strict</code></td><td>Reserved (scaffold; probe Unavailable)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>remote-*</code></td><td>namespace reserved (no individual entries)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>wasi-*</code></td><td>namespace reserved (no individual entries)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>CLI surface: <code>tau target list</code>, <code>tau target show <triple></code>, <code>tau check --target <triple></code>.</p> <h2 id="stability-discipline"><a class="header" href="#stability-discipline">Stability discipline</a></h2> <p>Once a triple ships as Available, it is <strong>immutable</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Adding a new triple is forward-compatible.</li> <li>Renaming an Available triple is forbidden.</li> <li>Removing an Available triple is forbidden.</li> <li>Changing an Available triple's required_shapes set is forbidden (would silently invalidate bundles compiled before the change).</li> <li>Promoting Reserved → Available is allowed (adds a working adapter).</li> <li>Demoting Available → Reserved is forbidden.</li> </ul> <p>Adding a new triple lands via an amendment to this ADR plus a registry entry.</p> <h2 id="forward-compat-hook"><a class="header" href="#forward-compat-hook">Forward-compat hook</a></h2> <p>§D may add a <code>capability_vocab_version: u32</code> field to <code>TargetTriple</code> with default <code>1</code>. Old bundles parse with the default; the new field surfaces only when an explicit non-default value is requested.</p> <h2 id="out-of-scope-1"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-1">Out of scope</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>tau build --target</code> — Phase 2 §C.</li> <li>Bundle format — Phase 2 §C.</li> <li>Capability vocabulary versioning — Phase 2 §D.</li> </ul> <h2 id="spec"><a class="header" href="#spec">Spec</a></h2> <p>See <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-target-triple-registry-design.md</code>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0035-tau-bundle-format-c1"><a class="header" href="#adr-0035-tau-bundle-format-c1">ADR-0035: Tau bundle format (§C.1)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-19 <strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <h2 id="context-37"><a class="header" href="#context-37">Context</a></h2> <p>Phase 2 §C produces the deployment artifact for tau workflows. The scope estimate (~6 weeks) decomposes into §C.1 (this ADR — bundle format), §C.2 (<code>tau build</code> producer), and §C.3 (<code>tau run --bundle</code> consumer). C.1 lands first because C.2 and C.3 both depend on a stable format.</p> <h2 id="decision-31"><a class="header" href="#decision-31">Decision</a></h2> <p>A bundle is a <strong>single <code>.tau</code> TOML file</strong>, reference-only (no embedded plugin binaries). Schema v1 holds:</p> <ul> <li><code>schema_version</code> (u32, currently 1)</li> <li><code>[bundle]</code> — self-hash + created_at + tau_version + target</li> <li><code>[project]</code> — name + version + tau_toml_sha256</li> <li><code>[[packages]]</code> — one per resolved package (name, version, source, tree_sha256, optional binary_sha256, required_shapes)</li> <li><code>[[agents]]</code> — one per agent (id, backend, system_prompt_sha256, required_tools, optional effective_capabilities table)</li> </ul> <p>See spec §4 for the full schema and §6 for code surface.</p> <h3 id="self-hash"><a class="header" href="#self-hash">Self-hash</a></h3> <p><code>bundle.sha256</code> is the SHA-256 of the canonical-TOML serialization of the manifest with <code>bundle.sha256</code> itself set to the empty string. A hand-written <code>to_canonical_toml</code> emitter guarantees byte-stable output across <code>toml</code> crate versions; the same emitter is used at both producer and consumer ends.</p> <h3 id="stability-discipline-1"><a class="header" href="#stability-discipline-1">Stability discipline</a></h3> <p>v1.x is <strong>additive</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>New optional fields land with <code>#[serde(default)]</code> defaults.</li> <li>New top-level tables are reserved (e.g., <code>[binaries]</code> for a future self-contained mode); v1 producers MUST NOT emit reserved tables. v1 consumers MUST ignore unknown top-level tables.</li> </ul> <p>v2 is a <strong>breaking change</strong>. Consumers fail loudly (<code>BundleParseError::UnsupportedSchemaVersion</code>) when they meet a schema_version they don't support.</p> <p>The capability-vocabulary forward-compatibility rules (the additive discipline for adding new capability shapes to bundles) are codified in ADR-0036.</p> <h3 id="reference-only-deferral"><a class="header" href="#reference-only-deferral">Reference-only deferral</a></h3> <p>Self-contained bundles (with embedded plugin binaries) are deferred indefinitely per the §C brainstorm. The reservations in v1's schema preserve forward-compat: a future <code>[binaries]</code> table can be added without breaking existing v1 bundles. The decision to embed binaries is gated on a concrete air-gap or remote-runner use case.</p> <h2 id="out-of-scope-2"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-2">Out of scope</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>tau build --target</code> — Phase 2 §C.2.</li> <li><code>tau run --bundle</code> — Phase 2 §C.3.</li> <li>Bundle signing / authenticity — Phase 3+.</li> <li>Cross-machine reproducibility verification — Phase 2 §E.</li> <li>Embedded plugin binaries — deferred per §C brainstorm.</li> </ul> <h2 id="spec-1"><a class="header" href="#spec-1">Spec</a></h2> <p>See <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-bundle-format-design.md</code>.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0036-capability-vocabulary-forward-compatibility"><a class="header" href="#adr-0036-capability-vocabulary-forward-compatibility">ADR-0036: Capability vocabulary forward-compatibility</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-05-29 <strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <h2 id="context-38"><a class="header" href="#context-38">Context</a></h2> <p>A deployment bundle compiled against tau v1.2 must continue to run on tau v1.3+ as new capability shapes are added (Phase 2 §D). The mechanism already exists — <code>Capability</code>/<code>CapabilityShape</code> are <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> with <code>Custom</code> escape hatches (ADR-0002), and the bundle format is additive with a <code>schema_version</code> hard-gate and no <code>deny_unknown_fields</code> (ADR-0035). What was missing is <em>discipline</em>: nothing prevented a future change from silently breaking these guarantees, and the rules were not stated in one place.</p> <h2 id="decision-32"><a class="header" href="#decision-32">Decision</a></h2> <p>The following rules are binding and enforced by the forward-compat guard tests in <code>crates/tau-pkg/src/bundle/manifest.rs</code> and <code>crates/tau-pkg/src/bundle/build.rs</code>:</p> <ul> <li><strong>R1.</strong> Wire-format structs (<code>BundleManifest</code> and its sub-structs; package/agent manifest structs) MUST NOT use <code>#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]</code>. Unknown fields and tables are tolerated and ignored.</li> <li><strong>R2.</strong> <code>Capability</code> and <code>CapabilityShape</code> remain <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> and retain their <code>Custom</code> variants. An unknown capability <code>kind</code> deserializes to <code>Custom</code> (never an error); the <code>Custom</code> match arm is load-bearing.</li> <li><strong>R3.</strong> <code>BundleManifest.schema_version</code> stays <code>1</code> for all additive changes. A bump to <code>2</code> is BREAKING, requires its own ADR and a migration story, and is not routine.</li> <li><strong>R4.</strong> New capability shapes are added additively: a new typed <code>Capability</code> variant plus, where it fits the <code>Vec<String></code> allow/deny shape, a new pair on <code>BundleEffectiveCapabilities</code> with <code>#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]</code>. Older parsers ignore the new field; the guard tests must keep passing.</li> <li><strong>R5.</strong> Any new <code>BundleEffectiveCapabilities</code> field MUST also be emitted in <code>bundle/canonical.rs::write_effective_capabilities</code> (the hand-rolled canonical serializer bypasses serde) — otherwise it is excluded from the self-hash.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-32"><a class="header" href="#consequences-32">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Forward-compatibility is now regression-protected: the guard tests fail CI if any rule is violated.</li> <li>Adding <code>skill.spawn</code> to <code>BundleEffectiveCapabilities</code> (the §C.2.3 gap) is the first worked example of R4/R5.</li> <li><code>task_list</code>, <code>plan</code>, <code>custom</code>, and the <code>fs.write max_bytes</code> / <code>net.http methods</code> sub-fields remain unrepresented in the bundle record (documented limitation); the runtime still enforces them.</li> <li>New obligation: future capability-shape additions follow R4/R5 and must extend the guard tests.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-26"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-26">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>A <code>min_tau_version</code> / version-negotiation field on bundles.</strong> Rejected: the <code>schema_version</code> hard-gate plus the additive rule already deliver the §D guarantee; negotiation adds wire complexity for no benefit at v1 (YAGNI).</li> <li><strong><code>deny_unknown_fields</code> + explicit migration shims per version.</strong> Rejected: it inverts the forward-compat default (old parsers would reject new bundles) — exactly the failure mode §D must prevent.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0037-workflow-ir--typed-content-hashed-phased-lowering"><a class="header" href="#adr-0037-workflow-ir--typed-content-hashed-phased-lowering">ADR-0037: Workflow IR — typed, content-hashed, phased lowering</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted</p> <p><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-01</p> <p><strong>Deciders:</strong> titouanlebocq</p> <p><strong>Spec:</strong> <a href="decisions/../superpowers/specs/2026-05-31-workflow-ir-design.html"><code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-31-workflow-ir-design.md</code></a>.</p> <h2 id="context-39"><a class="header" href="#context-39">Context</a></h2> <p>ROADMAP §β.2 — the workflow IR is tau's compiler thesis made concrete. Phase α.1 (Framing D) enumerated D-1 through D-7b; the design spec settled each. This ADR records the binding decisions for durability.</p> <h2 id="decision-33"><a class="header" href="#decision-33">Decision</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>D-1:</strong> Typed full node taxonomy (Agent + Tool + Deterministic + Subflow).</li> <li><strong>D-2:</strong> New <code>tau_ir::Message</code> + bidirectional adapter to <code>tau_domain::Message</code>.</li> <li><strong>D-3:</strong> WASI + tau custom-section capability lowering.</li> <li><strong>D-3b:</strong> Strict build-time refusal, no override.</li> <li><strong>D-4:</strong> Monolithic component per workflow.</li> <li><strong>D-5:</strong> Phased: interpret v0 (β.2), AOT v1 (β.7/γ.x).</li> <li><strong>D-6:</strong> Per-target hashing; <code>ir_format</code> separate from <code>tau_version</code>.</li> <li><strong>D-7a:</strong> Multiset side-effect conformance.</li> <li><strong>D-7b:</strong> ~6 fixtures.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-33"><a class="header" href="#consequences-33">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><code>tau-ir</code> is a new <code>no_std</code> + <code>alloc</code> crate alongside <code>tau-runtime-core</code>.</li> <li><code>tau_ir::IrModule</code> + <code>tau_ir::Workflow</code> + <code>tau_ir::Node</code> + variants (Agent, Tool, Deterministic, Subflow) form the canonical IR shape.</li> <li><code>BundleManifest::schema_version</code> bumped 1 → 2 with the new <code>ir_payload</code> field; legacy v1 bundles still parse and run.</li> <li><code>tau verify --bundle</code> extends to compare IR canonical bytes via <code>tau_ir::canonical_bytes()</code> + SHA-256 hash.</li> <li>The conformance suite in <code>crates/tau-ir-conformance/</code> becomes a permanent CI gate (β.6 lane). <strong>v0 ships scaffold + 1 fixture; remaining 5 fixtures + bundle_mode runner deferred to β.2.6.1</strong> once <code>tau run --bundle</code> interpreter dispatch is unstubbed (from β.2.5).</li> <li><code>tau run --bundle</code> parses <code>ir_payload</code> and logs the entry agent, but <strong>interpreter dispatch is deferred to β.2.6.1</strong>.</li> <li>The IR is the canonical intermediate form; <code>tau.toml</code> and <code>workflows/*.toml</code> are source dialects that lower into it. Round-trip determinism is enforced: the same manifest re-lowered must produce identical IR bytes.</li> </ul> <h2 id="open-questions-deferred-to-future-adrs"><a class="header" href="#open-questions-deferred-to-future-adrs">Open questions deferred to future ADRs</a></h2> <ul> <li>AOT codegen design (β.7).</li> <li>TS sugar surface (β.8 / δ.2).</li> <li>Multi-workflow composition (<code>SubflowKind::Compose</code>).</li> <li>Multi-format reader policy (whether tau N reads bundles from N-1).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0038--mcp-facilitator-β3"><a class="header" href="#adr-0038--mcp-facilitator-β3">ADR-0038 — MCP Facilitator (β.3)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-10 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none (finalises the placeholder shipped in β.3 PR-1, #280)</p> <h2 id="context-40"><a class="header" href="#context-40">Context</a></h2> <p>tau's plugin protocol predated the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem. The philosophy pivot of 2026-05-29 (<code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code>) named MCP as the canonical multi-vendor tool contract that tau should adopt as a first-class equal of the bespoke plugin protocol. The β.3 sub-project introduces an MCP-client facilitator so IR programs can reference MCP servers via <code>[tools.<name>] mcp = "..."</code> without changing the IR itself.</p> <p>This ADR records the as-shipped reality across the six β.3 PRs (#280–#284, #287, and this PR-6).</p> <h2 id="decision-34"><a class="header" href="#decision-34">Decision</a></h2> <p>Adopt MCP as a first-class tool contract on equal footing with the bespoke plugin protocol. Specifically:</p> <h3 id="1-two-new-crates-tau-mcp-and-tau-mcp-tokio"><a class="header" href="#1-two-new-crates-tau-mcp-and-tau-mcp-tokio">1. Two new crates: <code>tau-mcp</code> and <code>tau-mcp-tokio</code></a></h3> <p>Following the β.1 core/tokio split discipline:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>tau-mcp</code></strong> — <code>no_std</code>-friendly. Protocol wire types (JSON-RPC envelopes, <code>initialize</code>, <code>tools/list</code>, <code>tools/call</code>, <code>sampling/createMessage</code>, <code>roots/list</code>, <code>notifications/*</code>, <code>cancellation</code>). Contract types, canonical-hash function, pinned-contract I/O helpers, <code>HostHandlers</code> trait, and the transport-agnostic cassette recorder/replayer.</li> <li><strong><code>tau-mcp-tokio</code></strong> — tokio runtime + transports. stdio subprocess spawn, Streamable HTTP client, <code>host_lifecycle::open</code> dispatch, and <code>McpBridge</code> (composable <code>ToolDispatcher</code> adapter).</li> </ul> <h3 id="2-transport-surface--four-url-schemes"><a class="header" href="#2-transport-surface--four-url-schemes">2. Transport surface — four URL schemes</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>URL scheme</th><th>Module</th><th>Use case</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>stdio:<argv></code></td><td><code>tau-mcp-tokio::transport_stdio</code></td><td>subprocess MCP server (most ecosystem servers)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>http://…</code></td><td><code>tau-mcp-tokio::transport_http</code></td><td>plain-HTTP Streamable MCP (accepted; <code>tau build</code> warns)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>https://…</code></td><td><code>tau-mcp-tokio::transport_http</code></td><td>HTTPS Streamable MCP (production)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>cassette:<path></code></td><td><code>tau-mcp-tokio::host_lifecycle::cassette_dial</code></td><td>recorded MCP traffic replayed from JSONL</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><code>host_lifecycle::open(url, plan, gate, options)</code> dispatches on the parsed <code>McpUrl</code> variant and returns a unified <code>McpClient</code>.</p> <h3 id="3-pinned-contracts-taumcpnamecontractjson"><a class="header" href="#3-pinned-contracts-taumcpnamecontractjson">3. Pinned contracts (<code>.tau/mcp/<name>.contract.json</code>)</a></h3> <p>Every referenced server has its <code>ServerContract</code> captured at install time as a <code>PinnedContract</code> (schema v1, defined in <code>tau_mcp::contract::pinned</code>). Carries:</p> <ul> <li><code>schema_version: 1</code></li> <li><code>url</code>: server URL (matches <code>[tools.<name>] mcp = "..."</code>)</li> <li><code>contract_hash_hex</code>: canonical SHA-256 of the contract body (lowercase hex)</li> <li><code>contract</code>: the full <code>ServerContract</code> snapshot</li> </ul> <p>Self-integrity is verified via <code>PinnedContract::verify_self_hash</code>. Used by <code>tau build --offline</code>, <code>tau verify --bundle</code>, and the <code>tau check mcp-contracts</code> phase (PR-6).</p> <h3 id="4-ir-shape-β2-toolimplmcp-extended"><a class="header" href="#4-ir-shape-β2-toolimplmcp-extended">4. IR shape (β.2 <code>ToolImpl::Mcp</code> extended)</a></h3> <p><code>ToolImpl::Mcp</code> gains <code>server_tool_name: String</code> so the IR carries the per-tool routing info needed at runtime without a runtime lookup.</p> <p>IR <code>ToolId</code> convention for expanded MCP entries: <code>"<entry>.<server-tool>"</code>, e.g. <code>weather.get_forecast</code>.
