The author writes <code>tool_refs = ["weather"]</code>; lowering rewrites it to <code>["weather.get_current", "weather.get_forecast", ...]</code> after the <code>tools/list</code> expansion stage.</p> <p>Server-tool names containing <code>.</code> are rejected at build time with <code>McpBuildError::ServerToolNameContainsDot</code> (forward-defense against <code>ToolId</code> namespace collisions).</p> <h3 id="5-lockfile-v7"><a class="header" href="#5-lockfile-v7">5. Lockfile v7</a></h3> <p>Adds <code>mcp_entries: Vec<LockedMcpEntry></code> to <code>LockFile</code>. Each entry records:</p> <ul> <li><code>entry</code>: tool name from <code>[tools.<entry>]</code></li> <li><code>url</code>: resolved MCP server URL</li> <li><code>contract_hash</code>: hex SHA-256 of the canonical resolved contract</li> <li><code>pinned_contract: Option<String></code>: path to the pin file (relative to project root)</li> <li><code>expanded_tools: Vec<LockedMcpExpandedTool></code>: server-side tool names + cap shapes + schema hashes</li> </ul> <p>v6→v7 migration is silent (an empty <code>mcp_entries</code> is correct for v6 projects). <code>SchemaTooNew</code> handles forward compat without new code.</p> <h3 id="6-build-time-invariants"><a class="header" href="#6-build-time-invariants">6. Build-time invariants</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Invariant</th><th>Error variant</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Contract reachable at build (live mode)</td><td><code>McpBuildError::ContractUnreachable</code></td></tr> <tr><td>Envelope ⊇ every server-tool's declared caps</td><td><code>McpBuildError::EnvelopeCoversContract</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>roots</code> ⊆ tool's <code>fs.read</code> caps</td><td><code>McpBuildError::RootsExceedFsCaps</code></td></tr> <tr><td>Server contract requires sampling AND <code>sampling.models</code> is empty</td><td><code>McpBuildError::SamplingRequiredByContract</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>--offline</code> mode + pinned file missing</td><td><code>McpBuildError::PinnedContractMissing</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>--offline-strict</code> mode + pinned hash ≠ live hash</td><td><code>McpBuildError::PinnedContractStale</code></td></tr> <tr><td>Server-tool name contains <code>.</code></td><td><code>McpBuildError::ServerToolNameContainsDot</code></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="7-runtime-boot--per-turn-dispatch"><a class="header" href="#7-runtime-boot--per-turn-dispatch">7. Runtime: boot + per-turn dispatch</a></h3> <p>At <code>ForwardingDispatcher::new</code>, for each distinct MCP server URL:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>{url, contract_hash, expanded_tools}</code> from the lockfile entry.</li> <li>Read <code>{sampling.models, roots, caps}</code> from <code>tau.toml [tools.<name>]</code>.</li> <li>Construct <code>CapabilityPlan</code> and call <code>host_lifecycle::open</code>.</li> <li>Handshake (initialize + <code>tools/list</code>); re-hash and compare against <code>lockfile.contract_hash</code>. Mismatch → <code>ContractDriftAtBoot</code> hard error.</li> <li>Construct <code>HostHandlers</code> with sampling allowlist + roots + trace notifications + abort cancellation.</li> <li>Wrap in <code>McpBridge</code> (<code>impl ToolDispatcher</code>).</li> </ol> <p><code>ForwardingDispatcher</code> composes: <code>McpBridge</code> routes first; bespoke <code>plugin_host</code> handles the rest.</p> <h3 id="8-capability-gate--two-enforcement-points"><a class="header" href="#8-capability-gate--two-enforcement-points">8. Capability gate — two enforcement points</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Point</th><th>stdio MCP server</th><th>HTTP MCP server</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Spawn-time (OS boundary)</td><td><code>ProcessGate::Sandbox::wrap_spawn</code> → landlock / seccomp / sandbox-exec / podman</td><td>n/a — no spawn</td></tr> <tr><td>Per-call (contract boundary)</td><td><code>McpBridge::cap_gate.check_outbound</code></td><td>same + reqwest middleware enforces <code>net.http</code> host pinning</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Default-deny inbound handlers:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Inbound</th><th>Default-allow?</th><th>Author opt-in</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>sampling/*</code></td><td>no</td><td><code>sampling.models = [...]</code> in <code>tau.toml</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>roots/list</code></td><td>no (returns <code>[]</code>)</td><td><code>roots = [...]</code> in <code>tau.toml</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>notifications/*</code></td><td>yes (observational)</td><td>n/a</td></tr> <tr><td><code>cancellation/*</code></td><td>yes (control plane)</td><td>n/a</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <h3 id="9-cli-surface-pr-6"><a class="header" href="#9-cli-surface-pr-6">9. CLI surface (PR-6)</a></h3> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Verb</th><th>Effect</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>tau mcp pin <name> [--from URL]</code></td><td>Probe a server, write <code>.tau/mcp/<name>.contract.json</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>tau mcp ls [--json]</code></td><td>Enumerate pinned contracts</td></tr> <tr><td><code>tau mcp show <name> [--json|--sarif]</code></td><td>Show one pin (human / JSON / SARIF)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>tau mcp refresh <name> [--json]</code></td><td>Re-probe and overwrite the pin; report changed/unchanged</td></tr> <tr><td><code>tau mcp diff <name> [--json]</code></td><td>Read-only drift check. Exit 0 unchanged, exit 64 drift</td></tr> <tr><td><code>tau check mcp-contracts</code></td><td>Aggregator phase: verify pin self-hashes + lockfile drift</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>CLI modules live at <code>tau-cli/src/cmd/mcp/{mod,pin,ls,show,refresh,diff}.rs</code>, mirroring the <code>cmd/skill/</code> layout from Skills-3 (PR #66).</p> <h3 id="10-drift-defence-in-depth--three-independent-checks"><a class="header" href="#10-drift-defence-in-depth--three-independent-checks">10. Drift defence-in-depth — three independent checks</a></h3> <ol> <li><strong><code>PinnedContract::verify_self_hash</code></strong> — internal pin integrity (the pin's <code>contract_hash_hex</code> matches a fresh hash of its own <code>contract</code> field).</li> <li><strong><code>tau check mcp-contracts</code></strong> — pin vs lockfile (the pin's hash matches <code>LockedMcpEntry.contract_hash</code>).</li> <li><strong>Runtime drift check</strong> — live server vs lockfile hash at <code>McpClient</code> construction time (every boot).</li> </ol> <p>Any mismatch fails closed.</p> <h3 id="11-cassette-format"><a class="header" href="#11-cassette-format">11. Cassette format</a></h3> <p>Transport-agnostic message-level JSONL in <code>tau-mcp::cassette</code>. First line: <code>{"version":1}</code>. Subsequent lines are <code>CassetteMessage</code> records with <code>dir</code> (<code>"in"</code> = host→server, <code>"out"</code> = server→host), <code>kind</code> (<code>"request"</code> | <code>"response"</code> | <code>"notification"</code>), optional <code>id</code>, <code>method</code>, and <code>payload</code>. Replayer matches on <code>(method, normalized_args)</code> (sorted keys, stripped whitespace).</p> <h3 id="12-conformance-fixture-07"><a class="header" href="#12-conformance-fixture-07">12. Conformance fixture #07</a></h3> <p><code>crates/tau-ir-conformance/fixtures/07_mcp_weather_cassette/</code> exercises a <code>cassette:</code> URL through the IR-level conformance harness (DevMode + cross-mode equivalence with BundleMode).</p> <h2 id="consequences-34"><a class="header" href="#consequences-34">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Users can adopt arbitrary MCP servers without writing bespoke plugin code.</li> <li>Cassettes make MCP-backed tools fully testable and reproducible without network or subprocess at test time.</li> <li>The bespoke plugin protocol is now slated for eventual replacement-by-MCP per the philosophy pivot; β.3 is the foundation for that work.</li> <li>All five in-tree bespoke plugins are unchanged (Lane 1 preserved).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Three drift checks must be kept in lockstep across <code>tau-mcp</code>, <code>tau-pkg</code>, and <code>tau-cli</code>. Conformance fixtures #02 and #07 plus <code>cassette_dial.rs</code> integration tests act as the canaries.</li> <li>Each pinned contract is committed to the repo (small JSON files, ~5–50 KB each).</li> <li>Windows stdio sandbox is stub-only (pre-existing gap from ADR-0023); stdio MCP on Windows runs without OS-level cap enforcement until sandbox-windows Phase 2.</li> <li><code>net.*</code> OS-level enforcement is advisory on Linux (seccomp cannot filter outbound network egress); v0 stdio MCP relies on contract-level host pinning and wire-level enforcement (HTTP) for <code>net.http</code> caps.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-27"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-27">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Streamable HTTP only, no stdio:</strong> rejected — most MCP servers in the ecosystem ship as stdio-only subprocesses.</li> <li><strong>No cassettes, mock MCP servers per test:</strong> rejected — would duplicate test infrastructure and give weaker compliance guarantees than replaying real protocol traffic.</li> <li><strong>Inline contracts in lockfile (no <code>.tau/mcp/</code> files):</strong> rejected — contracts can be 50 KB+ each; this would bloat the lockfile and make it hard to read.</li> <li><strong>MCP-only (deprecate plugin protocol immediately):</strong> rejected as out-of-scope for β.3; tracked separately as future work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-20"><a class="header" href="#references-20">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>β.3 PR-1 (#280) — crate scaffolds + protocol types + ADR placeholder</li> <li>β.3 PR-2 (#281) — stdio transport + host lifecycle + mock-mcp-server fixture</li> <li>β.3 PR-3 (#283) — HTTP Streamable transport + CassetteTransport</li> <li>β.3 PR-4 (#284) — lowering + lockfile v7 + <code>tau build</code> wiring</li> <li>β.3 PR-5 (#287) — McpBridge + WiredHostHandlers + runtime drift check</li> <li>β.3 PR-6 (this PR) — CLI verbs + conformance fixture #07 + this ADR + docs</li> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-01-beta-3-mcp-facilitator-design.md</code></li> <li>Philosophy: <code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code></li> <li>Adjacent ADRs: ADR-0030 (Skills-6), ADR-0034 (target triple registry), ADR-0035 (bundle format), ADR-0037 (workflow IR β.2)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0039-ci-strategy--three-tier-model"><a class="header" href="#adr-0039-ci-strategy--three-tier-model">ADR-0039: CI Strategy — Three-Tier Model</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted (superseded in part by ADR-0063 — per-PR Tier 1 job set) <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-09 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> —</p> <h2 id="context-41"><a class="header" href="#context-41">Context</a></h2> <p>Pre-2026-06-09 CI ran every check on every PR (~24 jobs, ~15-25 min wall-clock). This was comprehensive but slow + costly. Pain points included recurring macOS infra flakes (chat_ephemeral_writes_no_file, echo-tool fixture race), linker bus errors on Linux, and CI-only clippy lints catching things local rustc missed.</p> <h2 id="decision-35"><a class="header" href="#decision-35">Decision</a></h2> <p>Adopt a three-tier CI model plus a periodic security-scan layer:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Tier</th><th>Trigger</th><th>Required to merge?</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>1 — PR (fast loop)</td><td>every push to PR branch + merge-queue + push to main</td><td>YES (via ci-summary aggregator)</td></tr> <tr><td>2 — Nightly + label (heavy validation)</td><td><code>0 4 * * *</code> cron against main HEAD; PR <code>full-matrix</code> label opt-in</td><td>NO (informational; auto-opens issue on cron regression)</td></tr> <tr><td>3 — Release (tag-driven)</td><td><code>push: tags: ['v*']</code></td><td>YES (gates GitHub Release artifact creation)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Plus security cron: daily <code>cargo audit</code> + <code>osv-scanner</code>, weekly Mon CodeQL, weekly Sun cargo-geiger.</p> <p>Six DevOps add-ons: concurrency groups everywhere, flaky-test quarantine scaffold, action SHA pinning + dependabot bumps, dependabot patch auto-merge, required-checks audit guard, auto-bisect on nightly regression.</p> <h2 id="rationale"><a class="header" href="#rationale">Rationale</a></h2> <ul> <li>Tier 1 keeps the cheap signal (fmt, clippy, deny, audit, osv, gitleaks, cargo-check × 3, nextest linux, doctests, msrv, fixtures-ports, feature-flag-matrix, no_std). The slow + flake-prone macOS + Windows nextest jobs moved to Tier 2.</li> <li>24h regression detection via nightly cron beats waiting weeks for the next release tag.</li> <li>Release model is feature-driven (tag whenever a meaningful batch is ready), not time-driven (no Rust-style 6-week train). The 24h drift detection compensates for irregular release cadence.</li> <li>Security depth: <code>Strong</code> bundle (cargo-deny + audit + osv + gitleaks + CodeQL + cargo-geiger + SBOM at tag). Provides defense-in-depth without enterprise-grade ceremony.</li> <li><code>full-matrix</code> PR label gives an escape hatch for high-risk PRs (sandbox, transports) that want pre-merge cross-platform confirmation without losing the fast PR loop default.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-35"><a class="header" href="#consequences-35">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Pros</strong>: ~5-7 min PR turnaround (warm) vs ~15-25 min. Nightly drift detection. Signed release artifacts with SBOM. Security findings flow into GitHub Security tab automatically.</li> <li><strong>Cons</strong>: Cross-platform regressions slip onto main and surface ≤24h later. Mitigations: cargo-check on macOS + Windows still runs on PR; <code>full-matrix</code> label opts into Tier 2 pre-merge.</li> <li>Required to merge: only <code>ci-summary</code> (unchanged). Tier 2 / 3 are gated by their own workflow success.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-28"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-28">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>(A) Every-main-commit Tier 2</strong> — would catch regressions within minutes of merge but multiplies CI cost. Rejected: nightly is sufficient for tau's commit volume.</li> <li><strong>(B) Time-driven release (Rust 6-week train)</strong> — predictable cadence but forces ship-or-skip decisions on artificial dates. Rejected: feature-driven serves a workspace repo better.</li> <li><strong>(C) Tag-only validation (no nightly)</strong> — simpler but late detection. Rejected: 24h detection is worth the cron infra.</li> </ul> <h2 id="links"><a class="header" href="#links">Links</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-ci-strategy-redesign.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-09-ci-strategy-redesign.md</code></li> <li>Predecessor CI documentation: (none formal; this is the first ADR for CI strategy)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0040-tau-dev-repl--the-β7β75-split"><a class="header" href="#adr-0040-tau-dev-repl--the-β7β75-split">ADR-0040: <code>tau dev</code> REPL + the β.7/β.7.5 split</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-10 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-42"><a class="header" href="#context-42">Context</a></h2> <p>β.7 as originally written in <code>ROADMAP.md</code> bundled two distinct deliverables: the <code>tau dev</code> hot-reload REPL (Vercel-DX feel for the engine) and the ahead-of-time IR-to-wasm compiler ("AOT lands in β.7" footnote on β.2). After β.3 PR-5/PR-6 expanded the MCP facilitator's surface significantly, the in-wasm MCP-facilitator path's complexity ballooned, making the bundled β.7 a 6–10 week sub-project with a high-risk tail (wasm component model is a moving target; no prior art for agent harnesses).</p> <h2 id="decision-36"><a class="header" href="#decision-36">Decision</a></h2> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Split β.7 into two sub-projects:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>β.7 (this ADR):</strong> REPL only — <code>tau dev <project></code> over the existing β.3 runtime path. ~2 weeks.</li> <li><strong>β.7.5 (separate, ADR-0046 + ADR-0047):</strong> IR-to-wasm AOT compiler. ~4–8 weeks.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><strong>REPL uses explicit <code>:reload</code>, not auto-reload by default.</strong> Industry prior art for agent dev loops is sparse (Mastra is the only meaningful one, and it picked Next.js-style auto-reload). For agents specifically, auto-reload destroys the iterative debug loop where the user wants to tweak an agent mid-conversation without restarting from turn 0. Erlang/ Elixir's REPL with <code>recompile</code> is the better prior art. <code>--watch</code> flag opts into auto-reload for users who prefer Mastra's UX.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Manifest-only hot reload in v1.</strong> Tool code reload requires the TS surface (β.8); shipping it in β.7 would require an embedded JS engine (QuickJS/V8) or a Rust dylib reload story, both significant scope.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="consequences-36"><a class="header" href="#consequences-36">Consequences</a></h2> <p>Positive:</p> <ul> <li><code>tau dev</code> ships fast (~2 weeks) and unblocks β.8 + β.6 design work.</li> <li>AOT gets its own focused sub-project with its own ADR + conformance scope.</li> <li>The REPL's explicit-reload semantics let users iterate mid-conversation without losing context.</li> </ul> <p>Negative:</p> <ul> <li>ROADMAP β.2's footnote needs amending (deferred AOT one phase).</li> <li>γ.1's dependency line gains β.7.5 (cosmetic).</li> <li>Two sub-projects to ship instead of one larger one — slightly more coordination overhead.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-29"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-29">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Ship β.7 bundled (REPL + AOT) as originally specced:</strong> rejected because AOT's complexity post-β.3 makes the bundled sub-project too large for one spec to manage; design holes more likely to slip through.</li> <li><strong>Mastra-style auto-reload as default:</strong> rejected because the agent debug loop benefits from explicit reload (see §2 above).</li> <li><strong>Skip the REPL, go straight to AOT:</strong> rejected because the REPL is the ergonomic on-ramp that the philosophy doc promises; deferring it leaves a hole in the Vercel-DX-feel story until β.7.5 + γ.1 both ship.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-21"><a class="header" href="#references-21">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-beta-7-tau-dev-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-10-beta-7-tau-dev.md</code></li> <li>Philosophy: <code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code> (DEV column of the two-profiles diagram)</li> <li>Related ADRs: 0037 (workflow IR), 0038 (MCP facilitator), 0039 (CI strategy)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0041-β8-ts-authoring-surface--declarations-only-via-static-ast-analysis"><a class="header" href="#adr-0041-β8-ts-authoring-surface--declarations-only-via-static-ast-analysis">ADR-0041: β.8 TS authoring surface — declarations-only via static AST analysis</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-10 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-43"><a class="header" href="#context-43">Context</a></h2> <p>The 2026-05-29 philosophy doc names TS as a sugar layer over the canonical IR. The β.8 ROADMAP entry adds the <code>@tau/sdk</code> factory functions but is ambiguous about whether TS code is statically analyzed or runtime-executed.</p> <p>After β.7 (tau dev REPL) shipped, the choice becomes load-bearing for β.6 (conformance gate). Two interpretations are honest:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Declarations-only via swc static AST analysis</strong> — TS file is parsed, factory calls recognized as data, no JS execution. Tool bodies remain Rust-native (referenced via <code>native: "ReadTemp"</code> string).</li> <li><strong>Full Vercel-DX feel</strong> — embed a JS runtime (rquickjs / deno_core), execute the TS file, factories build IR objects at runtime, inline tool bodies (<code>run: async () => ...</code>) work in dev mode.</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-37"><a class="header" href="#decision-37">Decision</a></h2> <p>Ship <strong>declarations-only via swc static AST analysis</strong> for β.8 v1. Defer the runtime JS execution path (and inline tool bodies) to δ.2.</p> <p>Specific decisions:</p> <ul> <li>New workspace crate <code>tau-ts-extract</code> does the TS → ProjectConfig conversion via swc 41.x.</li> <li>Snake_case fields throughout — matches TOML 1:1 to keep the conformance test (TOML↔TS byte-equal IR) simple.</li> <li>File-extension dispatch in <code>cmd/project_load.rs</code> — <code>.ts</code> → TS extractor; everything else → TOML.</li> <li><code>contextManager</code> factory exists in the SDK shape but rejects at parse time with a <code>Deferred</code> error (β.4 prerequisite).</li> <li>Multi-file TS imports rejected with helpful hint; v1.1 work.</li> <li>The TS extractor uses a TOML serialization bridge internally: emit a TOML string from the AST, then call <code>ProjectConfig::parse_str</code>. This reuses ALL existing validation — no parallel validation path.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-37"><a class="header" href="#consequences-37">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>β.8 ships in ~2 hours, comparable to β.7's footprint.</li> <li>No embedded JS engine in tau-cli; ~3 MB swc dep is the only binary cost.</li> <li>TOML↔TS conformance is straightforward (same lower path, same canonical encoder, byte-equal check).</li> <li>β.7.5 (IR-to-wasm AOT) doesn't need to handle in-wasm JS execution.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Users expecting Vercel AI SDK-style <code>run: async () => ...</code> get a rejection at parse time. The error message points them at the <code>native:</code> reference pattern + notes the δ.2 plan.</li> <li>Multi-file projects must wait for v1.1 (single-file constraint).</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-30"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-30">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Embed rquickjs for runtime JS</strong> — rejected for v1 because it adds ~600KB binary + a Rust↔JS capability bridge (significant scope). δ.2 picks this up.</li> <li><strong>Subprocess to tsx / Node</strong> — rejected because it requires external toolchain ("no toolchain required" promise from the philosophy doc).</li> <li><strong>CamelCase TS fields with auto-mapping to snake_case TOML</strong> — rejected because the conformance test would need a canonicalization layer; snake_case-on-both-sides is simpler and consistent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-22"><a class="header" href="#references-22">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-beta-8-ts-authoring-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-10-beta-8-ts-authoring.md</code></li> <li>Philosophy: <code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code> (TS sugar over IR)</li> <li>Related ADRs: 0037 (workflow IR), 0040 (β.7 tau dev REPL)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0042-cross-repo-ci-template-sync-tau--source-of-truth"><a class="header" href="#adr-0042-cross-repo-ci-template-sync-tau--source-of-truth">ADR-0042: Cross-repo CI template sync (tau = source of truth)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-11 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> —</p> <h2 id="context-44"><a class="header" href="#context-44">Context</a></h2> <p>tau is the most mature of four sibling repos (cairn, cairn-ui, tau-ui, tau) and is the de-facto canonical CI source. But nothing <em>operationalized</em> "tau = source of truth": there was no <code>renovate.json</code>, no <code>repo-file-sync-action</code> config, and no sync workflow on <code>main</code> — only <code>.github/dependabot.yml</code>, which bumps dependencies but does not distribute shared files cross-repo. CI drift between the four repos was therefore silent rot, not a visible signal.</p> <p>The audit (<code>audit/devops.md</code> §3 anti-drift, §4 sync-template item, Diagram 1) defines the target as the <strong>"B+C"</strong> model:</p> <ul> <li><strong>B — self-contained workflows.</strong> Each repo keeps its FULL <code>ci.yml</code>; there is NO runtime <code>workflow_call</code> to a central moving-tag workflow. One bad change can never red all four repos at once, and every <code>ci.yml</code> is debuggable in isolation.</li> <li><strong>C — thin SHA-pinned composite actions.</strong> Stable atomic steps only (<code>setup-rust</code>, <code>place-fixture-binaries</code>), consumed via <code>uses: ./.github/actions/...</code>.</li> </ul> <p>tau already satisfies B and C. The missing piece is the <strong>sync mechanism</strong> that propagates the canonical surface to the three siblings as a reviewable PR. This ADR also justifies adding a new workflow <code>name:</code> (<code>sync-template</code>) per the <code>required-checks-audit</code> guard (ADR-0039 add-on).</p> <h2 id="decision-38"><a class="header" href="#decision-38">Decision</a></h2> <p>Add the <strong>SOURCE side</strong> of the sync in tau, using <strong><code>BetaHuhn/repo-file-sync-action</code></strong> (SHA-pinned <code>@v1.21.1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><code>.github/sync.yml</code> — declares the target repos (<code>tau-rs/cairn</code>, <code>tau-rs/cairn-ui</code>, <code>tau-rs/tau-ui</code>) and the canonical template surface (<code>.github/workflows/</code> minus <code>sync-template.yml</code>, <code>.github/actions/</code>, <code>deny.toml</code>, <code>lefthook.yml</code>; <code>justfile</code> pending its own landing).</li> <li><code>.github/workflows/sync-template.yml</code> — runs the action on push-to-main of the template surface, plus a <code>workflow_dispatch</code> <code>dry_run</code> toggle (default true). The action copies file <strong>bytes</strong> into each target's own tree and opens a PR; drift becomes a VISIBLE open PR the target repo owns and merges.</li> <li><code>scripts/verify-sync-config.py</code> — resolves the config against the tree as a local DRY_RUN stand-in and asserts the recursion guard; wired as a pre-flight step in the sync workflow.</li> </ul> <p>The sync workflow (<code>sync-template.yml</code>) is <strong>excluded</strong> from its own synced set, so a sibling never becomes a second sync source. Cross-repo writes use a documented <code>REPO_FILE_SYNC_TOKEN</code> secret, never <code>GITHUB_TOKEN</code> or a hardcoded token.</p> <h2 id="consequences-38"><a class="header" href="#consequences-38">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Pros:</strong> "tau = source of truth" is now an executable artifact; CI drift surfaces as a reviewable PR within minutes of a template change. Composite actions stay byte-identical across repos. Constraint B is preserved — no runtime SPOF.</li> <li><strong>Negatives:</strong> A UI repo (cairn-ui / tau-ui) receives a sync PR mirroring the full workflows directory, including Rust/tau-specific workflows it cannot run. This is intentional — the target owner triages per-PR; a future iteration may move to per-target file subsets (the action supports per-repo <code>files:</code> groups).</li> <li><strong>Obligations:</strong> the <code>REPO_FILE_SYNC_TOKEN</code> secret must be configured before the first live sync (documented in <code>docs/dev-environment.md</code>); the sibling repos do their own copy work (out of scope here). Phase-2 optional follow-ups: a projen-style generator + <code>synth</code>-diff CI check, and cosign/SLSA provenance.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-31"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-31">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Renovate config that also distributes shared files</strong> — Renovate updates <em>dependencies</em> / SHA pins; it has no primitive to copy arbitrary files from a source repo into targets, and pin freshness is already handled by <code>.github/dependabot.yml</code>. Rejected: does not solve the file-distribution gap.</li> <li><strong>multi-gitter</strong> — distributes files, but as an ad-hoc local CLI a human runs from a laptop. Rejected: leaves no committed in-repo SOURCE artifact, so it does not operationalize "tau = source of truth."</li> <li><strong>Central reusable workflow invoked via runtime <code>workflow_call</code> + moving tag</strong> — rejected by the model: blast radius (one bad push reds all four repos) and indirection (a repo's CI can't be read in isolation). Violates constraint B.</li> </ul> <h2 id="links-1"><a class="header" href="#links-1">Links</a></h2> <ul> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-11-devops-antidrift-sync-template.md</code></li> <li>Audit: <code>audit/devops.md</code> §3 (anti-drift "B+C"), §4 (sync-template item), Diagram 1</li> <li>Predecessor: ADR-0039 (CI strategy three-tier model; <code>required-checks-audit</code> guard)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="0044--trigger-ingress-slice-1-cron--manual--retry-policy"><a class="header" href="#0044--trigger-ingress-slice-1-cron--manual--retry-policy">0044 — Trigger ingress, slice 1: cron + manual + retry policy</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted</p> <p><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-13</p> <p><strong>Relates to:</strong> the framing doc <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-trigger-ingress-and-serve-transport-framing.md</code>, <a href="decisions/0043-trigger-ingress.html">ADR-0043</a> (the trigger-ingress stance), <a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">ADR-0037</a> (workflow IR), the egress-only capability vocabulary, NG3 / NG5 / NG6.</p> <h2 id="context-45"><a class="header" href="#context-45">Context</a></h2> <p>The framing doc takes the position <em>compile the trigger; delegate the substrate.</em> This ADR records the implementation decisions for the first slice: the self-contained kinds (<code>cron</code>, <code>manual</code>) plus a <code>[trigger.*.retry]</code> policy and <code>tau build --emit-trigger=systemd|k8s</code>. <code>webhook</code> / <code>queue</code> (which require a host-adapter contract that <code>tau check</code> enforces) are slice 2.</p> <h2 id="decisions-1"><a class="header" href="#decisions-1">Decisions</a></h2> <h3 id="d1--triggers-is-a-sibling-of-workflow-ir_format-is-not-bumped"><a class="header" href="#d1--triggers-is-a-sibling-of-workflow-ir_format-is-not-bumped">D1 — <code>triggers</code> is a sibling of <code>workflow</code>; <code>ir_format</code> is NOT bumped</a></h3> <p><code>IrModule</code> gains <code>triggers: Vec<TriggerBinding></code> as a sibling of <code>workflow</code> (triggers are about <em>invocation</em>, not the call graph). The field carries <code>#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]</code>, so a trigger-less module emits no <code>triggers</code> key and its canonical bytes — and content hash — are byte-identical to a pre-trigger module; a trigger-bearing module appends a <code>triggers</code> array, which differentiates its hash on its own.</p> <p><code>ir_format</code> stays <code>v1.0.0</code> in all cases — it is <strong>not</strong> bumped. The framing doc leaned toward a minor bump, but <strong>triggers are inert at runtime</strong>: a trigger decides when/whether the host invokes tau, a decision made before tau's process starts, so an old runtime that silently ignores the <code>triggers</code> field still executes the workflow correctly. There is no reader-side gate on <code>ir_format</code> and we deliberately add none (it would reject a runnable workflow). The gate with teeth is the bundle <code>schema_version</code> (D3), read at build/inspect time. Since nothing keys off the IR language version, a bump would be a label with no consumer — so we leave it at <code>v1.0.0</code>. An unconditional bump was independently disqualified: it would re-hash every existing trigger-less module.</p> <h3 id="d2--dlq-envelope-shape-deferred"><a class="header" href="#d2--dlq-envelope-shape-deferred">D2 — DLQ envelope shape deferred</a></h3> <p>Slice 1 compiles the retry <em>policy</em> (<code>max_attempts</code>, <code>backoff</code>, <code>dead_letter</code> sink reference). The dead-letter <em>envelope</em> is a runtime artifact produced when a trigger fires and exhausts its attempts; nothing in tau fires triggers yet (retry is host-honoured), so the envelope shape lands with the host-adapter runtime work.</p> <h3 id="d3--bundle-schema_version-bumps-to-3-only-when-triggers-are-present"><a class="header" href="#d3--bundle-schema_version-bumps-to-3-only-when-triggers-are-present">D3 — bundle <code>schema_version</code> bumps to 3 only when triggers are present</a></h3> <p>A trigger-less bundle stays <code>schema_version = 2</code> and serialises identically to today. A trigger-bearing bundle is <code>3</code>, so an old tau rejects it loudly rather than silently dropping the binding. <code>BundleManifest</code> accepts <code>{1, 2, 3}</code>, and <code>parse_str</code> additionally rejects a trigger-bearing bundle whose <code>schema_version < 3</code> — the invariant is enforced at parse time, not merely produced by <code>tau build</code>.</p> <h3 id="d4--systemd-needs-a-crononcalendar-converter-k8s-takes-cron-verbatim"><a class="header" href="#d4--systemd-needs-a-crononcalendar-converter-k8s-takes-cron-verbatim">D4 — systemd needs a cron→OnCalendar converter; k8s takes cron verbatim</a></h3> <p>k8s <code>CronJob.schedule</code> consumes 5-field cron exactly. systemd <code>OnCalendar</code> does not, so slice 1 ships a converter for the subset where each field is <code>*</code> or a plain integer. Schedules outside that subset are skipped for systemd (with a logged note) but still emit exactly for k8s. <code>tau.toml</code> validation additionally range-checks any plain-integer cron field (e.g. rejects hour <code>25</code>) at build time.</p> <h3 id="non-goal-cross-check"><a class="header" href="#non-goal-cross-check">Non-goal cross-check</a></h3> <p>No inbound capability verb was added. cron/manual are egress-shaped: the host invokes tau as a child process. The egress-only vocabulary remains load-bearing for NG3. Retry is host-honoured (NG6 — no durable state in core); <code>dead_letter</code> is a sink reference, never a tau-owned store.</p> <h2 id="consequences-39"><a class="header" href="#consequences-39">Consequences</a></h2> <p><code>tau.toml</code> authors can declare cron/manual triggers that compile into the content-hashed artifact and reproduce across targets. <code>tau build --emit-trigger</code> generates the scheduler wiring; the operator owns the substrate. Slice 2 adds <code>webhook</code> / <code>queue</code> plus the <code>tau check</code> host-adapter rule.</p> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0043-trigger-ingress--compile-the-trigger-delegate-the-substrate"><a class="header" href="#adr-0043-trigger-ingress--compile-the-trigger-delegate-the-substrate">ADR-0043: Trigger ingress — compile the trigger, delegate the substrate</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-13 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-46"><a class="header" href="#context-46">Context</a></h2> <p>tau today is a stdio-driven automation step with no trigger ingress. <code>tau serve</code> speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON on stdin/stdout (<a href="decisions/0033-tau-serve-mode.html">ADR-0033</a>); a parent process initiates every <code>runtime.run</code>. Nothing inside tau ever <em>initiates</em> work, listens on a socket, schedules a future invocation, or persists a failed message.</p> <p>The recurring ask is whether tau should grow (1) triggers — cron schedules, webhook receivers, queue consumers; (2) an HTTP serve transport; and (3) declarative retry / DLQ — or stay "host drives it", with the scheduler, the listener, and the durable queue all living in the host (systemd, k8s, Lambda, an API gateway, Temporal, n8n).</p> <p>The framing doc (PR #330) establishes a load-bearing finding: <strong>"host drives it" is not a posture tau happens to take — it is wired into three layers of the engine.</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>The IR has no trigger and no retry concept.</strong> A lowered module is <code>IrModule { ir_format, tau_version, target, workflow }</code>; failures propagate, but there is no durable timer, retry counter, or persisted message anywhere in the interpreter (<a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">ADR-0037</a>).</li> <li><strong>The capability vocabulary is egress-only.</strong> <code>net.http</code> is <code>{ hosts, methods }</code> — <em>outbound</em> allow-listing. There is no <code>net.listen</code>, no inbound verb, no bind primitive anywhere in <code>Capability</code>.</li> <li><strong>The sandbox model has no inbound shape.</strong> <code>CapabilityShape</code> enumerates <code>FilesystemRead/Write</code>, <code>ProcessExec</code>, <code>NetworkHttp</code>, <code>AgentSpawn</code>, … — every shape an adapter can enforce. None is "accept a socket" (<a href="decisions/0014-sandboxing.html">ADR-0014</a>).</li> </ul> <p>So an inbound trigger is <strong>un-grantable by tau by construction</strong> — NG3 enforced at the type level, not by policy. This ADR records the stance taken on top of that finding. It cites ROADMAP non-goals NG3 (not a hosted service), NG5 (not a general workflow engine), NG6 (no persistent store in core), NG9 (no identity/credentials), and NG11/NG12 (developer tool; compiler, not a framework).</p> <h2 id="decision-39"><a class="header" href="#decision-39">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>Compile the trigger; delegate the substrate.</strong></p> <p>tau adds a declarative <code>[trigger]</code> table that compiles into the IR and the bundle as portable, capability-safe metadata. A <strong>host adapter</strong> reads that metadata and wires the real trigger. tau emits the <em>binding</em>; the host owns the <em>substrate</em> — the scheduler, the socket, the durable queue. This is the same delegation pattern tau already applies to inference and credentials: <em>tau declares the trigger; operators choose the scheduler.</em></p> <p>Per-axis verdicts:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Ask</th><th>Verdict</th><th>The line</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>[trigger]</code> <em>declaration</em> → IR → bundle</td><td>✅ <strong>ADD</strong></td><td>Portable metadata; a host adapter wires the real trigger</td></tr> <tr><td>Retry / DLQ <em>policy</em> (<code>[trigger.*.retry]</code>)</td><td>✅ <strong>ADD</strong></td><td>Declarative attempts / backoff is portable metadata</td></tr> <tr><td>tau-owned in-process <strong>cron daemon</strong></td><td>❌ <strong>REJECT</strong></td><td>Long-lived scheduler = NG3; substrate is systemd / k8s / Lambda</td></tr> <tr><td>Public <strong>webhook listener</strong></td><td>❌ <strong>REJECT</strong></td><td>Inbound ingress = NG3; no inbound capability shape exists, by design</td></tr> <tr><td>Built-in <strong>durable DLQ store</strong></td><td>❌ <strong>REJECT</strong></td><td>Persistent store in core = NG5 + NG6-adjacent; dead-letter is a <em>sink contract</em></td></tr> <tr><td>HTTP serve transport — <strong>host-driven RPC</strong> (LSP-over-TCP)</td><td>◐ <strong>DEFER (defensible)</strong></td><td>Host still initiates each request; identical request/response shape to stdio. Not a non-goal violation — just not needed yet</td></tr> <tr><td>HTTP serve transport — <strong>internet-facing ingress</strong></td><td>❌ <strong>REJECT</strong></td><td>That is the webhook listener wearing a transport hat</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>A trigger has two halves. The <strong>substrate</strong> (the timer that fires at 03:00, the TCP socket + TLS + public URL, the queue connection) stays with the host. The <strong>binding</strong> ("fire <code>summarizer</code> on <code>0 3 * * *</code>"; "POST /ingest → <code>classifier</code>, retry 3×, DLQ to <code>sink</code>") is declared once in <code>tau.toml</code>, compiled, and made portable. The proposal adds <strong>only the binding</strong>.</p> <p>Concrete decisions:</p> <ul> <li>A project declares zero or more named triggers. Each binds an external event (<code>kind = cron | webhook | queue | manual</code>) to a workflow <code>agent</code> entrypoint validated at build against the project. Substrate fields — bind address, port, TLS material, public hostname, auth scheme, listener concurrency, queue connection strings — are <strong>deliberately absent</strong> from <code>tau.toml</code>; including them would make tau the service.</li> <li>A <code>[trigger.*.retry]</code> sub-table declares <code>max_attempts</code>, <code>backoff</code> (<code>fixed | exponential</code>, <code>base</code>, <code>max</code>), and <code>dead_letter</code>. <strong>Retry is a trigger-level re-invocation policy honored by the host, not a per-node interpreter retry</strong> — putting retry inside the engine would require durable timers and persisted attempt counters (durable state in core), which is NG3 + NG6-adjacent. Retry is durable exactly where the host is durable, and nowhere else.</li> <li><code>dead_letter</code> names a <strong>sink contract</strong> — an MCP contract (<code>mcp:<name></code>) or an already-granted capability target (an <code>fs.write</code> path, a <code>net.http</code> host). tau never stands up a queue, table, or spool of its own.</li> <li>Triggers lower as <strong>metadata</strong> parallel to the <code>tau.caps</code> custom section, adding no executable IR nodes. Because the binding lives in the canonical IR, it is content-hashed and reproducible, and <code>tau verify --bundle</code> covers it for free — "the trigger is part of the program" becomes literally true.</li> <li><code>tau build --emit-trigger=<adapter></code> optionally emits a host-adapter descriptor (systemd <code>.timer</code>+<code>.service</code>, k8s <code>CronJob</code>/<code>Ingress</code>, cf-workers cron stanza, Lambda EventBridge rule) the operator applies. The cargo → systemd-unit analogy made literal: tau produces the wiring; the operator owns the substrate. The descriptor set is open and additive.</li> </ul> <h3 id="egress-only-capability--ng3-enforced-at-the-type-level"><a class="header" href="#egress-only-capability--ng3-enforced-at-the-type-level">Egress-only capability = NG3 enforced at the type level</a></h3> <p>A webhook receiver needs to accept an inbound connection. tau has no capability that grants inbound — and <strong>that is the resolution, not a problem to patch.</strong> The egress-only vocabulary means tau cannot grant "receive an inbound connection" because tau is not a service. An inbound trigger is therefore un-grantable by tau by construction: NG3 is structural, not a policy that could be relaxed.</p> <h3 id="inbound-resolves-to-a-host-adapter-contract-never-a-runtime-capability"><a class="header" href="#inbound-resolves-to-a-host-adapter-contract-never-a-runtime-capability">Inbound resolves to a host-adapter contract, never a runtime capability</a></h3> <p><code>cron</code> and <code>manual</code> triggers need no inbound primitive — the host invokes tau as an ordinary child process (an egress-shaped, already-expressible relationship). They lower to IR metadata only and are the cleanest fit, hence the natural v1 priority.</p> <p><code>webhook</code> and <code>queue</code> triggers require a primitive tau has no capability shape for. Their binding lowers to IR metadata <strong>plus a "host-adapter required" marker</strong>. The host adapter owns the socket and is the only thing that can satisfy it. This gives <code>tau check</code> a real, enforceable rule: a <code>webhook</code> or <code>queue</code> trigger with no corresponding host adapter is a <strong>deploy-time hole tau can name statically</strong> — Rust-class build-time enforcement of what would otherwise be a silent runtime surprise. The line stays bright: ingress is always a host adapter that invokes the artifact, never a mode of <code>tau serve</code>.</p> <p>The HTTP serve transport is a <strong>separate axis, gated on who initiates</strong>, not on the wire protocol. An HTTP-as-RPC transport where the host POSTs <code>runtime.run</code> and gets a response (LSP-over-TCP) keeps the host driving and is defensible but deferred (no demand). The moment an HTTP endpoint starts accepting events and initiating runs on its own, it has become the rejected webhook listener regardless of label.</p> <h2 id="consequences-40"><a class="header" href="#consequences-40">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>The trigger lives <em>inside</em> the content-hashed artifact: "when and how am I invoked" becomes versioned, portable across every target, and reproducible — killing the dev/prod drift the compiler philosophy exists to eliminate.</li> <li>Adds the one thing only tau can add (a portable, capability-checked, content-hashed trigger binding) and delegates everything that would make tau a service. Triggers join inference and credentials as a third delegated substrate.</li> <li>Every non-goal "no" is structural, not promissory — the egress-only vocabulary and the "retry = host re-invocation" boundary make the violations <em>un-expressible</em>, not merely discouraged (NG3/NG5/NG6/NG9/ NG11/NG12 all cross-check clean).</li> <li><code>tau check</code> gains a statically enforceable deploy-time rule for webhook/queue triggers.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Operators of <code>webhook</code>/<code>queue</code> triggers must supply a host adapter; tau names the gap but does not fill the socket. (Intentional — that is NG3.)</li> <li>An HTTP serve transport that some users will want is deferred, not shipped.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Neutral / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li>This ADR records a <strong>framing stance, not a roadmap commitment.</strong> No code, no plan, no phase pull. An implementation spec must still be written; the framing fixes the boundary, the spec fixes the surface.</li> <li>If pursued, the cleanest first slice is <code>cron</code> + <code>manual</code> + retry policy + <code>--emit-trigger=systemd|k8s</code> — the self-contained kinds that need no host-adapter contract — with <code>webhook</code>/<code>queue</code> following once the host-adapter contract in <code>tau check</code> is specified.</li> <li>Open questions deferred to the impl spec: IR placement of <code>triggers</code> (sibling of <code>workflow</code> vs. field inside it); the additive <code>ir_format</code> bump <ul> <li>forward-compat read; dead-letter envelope shape; <code>tau check</code> rule severity (warning at build vs. error under <code>--require-deployable</code>); which <code>--emit-trigger</code> targets ship first; cron dialect + timezone handling; one-agent-per-trigger vs. fan-out.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-32"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-32">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Road A — pure "host drives it", add nothing.</strong> tau ships no <code>[trigger]</code> table; operators hand-write systemd units, k8s CronJobs, and gateway routes that call <code>tau run</code>/<code>tau serve</code>. <em>Rejected because:</em> the trigger then lives outside the content-hashed artifact — the program's "when and how am I invoked" is unversioned, non-portable, and re-authored per target, exactly the dev/prod drift the compiler philosophy kills. The cost of Road A is precisely the value tau adds elsewhere.</li> <li><strong>Road B — full orchestrator (the n8n / Temporal trap).</strong> tau grows a cron daemon, a webhook server, a durable queue, a DLQ store, visual retry policies, and a run-history database. <em>Rejected because:</em> this is NG3 + NG5 in their purest form, forces durable state into core (NG6), and turns tau from a developer-facing compiler (NG11/NG12) into an operations platform. The market already has Temporal, n8n, Airflow, and every cloud scheduler; tau's differentiator is the portable capability-safe artifact, which those tools do not produce. Road B trades a unique position for a crowded one.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-23"><a class="header" href="#references-23">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Framing spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-trigger-ingress-and-serve-transport-framing.md</code> (PR #330)</li> <li>Philosophy: <code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code> (the compiler convictions)</li> <li>Related ADRs: <a href="decisions/0014-sandboxing.html">0014</a> (sandbox capability shapes), <a href="decisions/0033-tau-serve-mode.html">0033</a> (serve mode v1), <a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">0037</a> (workflow IR), <a href="decisions/0035-bundle-format.html">0035</a> (bundle format)</li> <li>ROADMAP non-goals: NG3, NG5, NG6, NG9, NG11, NG12</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0044-deliverables--goals--build-time-checked-postcondition-steps"><a class="header" href="#adr-0044-deliverables--goals--build-time-checked-postcondition-steps">ADR-0044: Deliverables & goals — build-time-checked postcondition steps</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-13 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-47"><a class="header" href="#context-47">Context</a></h2> <p>tau pipelines could run a sequence of agents and tools but had no first-class way to assert that the pipeline produced what it was supposed to, or that a named goal was met. The failure mode was "ran clean, delivered nothing" — discovered by a human reading the output, not by the system.</p> <p>tau's standing principle (<a href="decisions/../explanation/tau-philosophy.html"><code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code></a>) is <strong>Rust-class build-time enforcement: any check that could run at build time must run at build time.</strong> A postcondition feature must therefore fail the <em>build</em> of a pipeline that cannot deliver its stated output, not only the runtime execution.</p> <p>This ADR records the seven architecture decisions made during the plan phase (see <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-deliverables-and-goals.md</code>, "Key implementation decisions") and the honest limits / deferrals that were not resolved in v1.</p> <p>The prerequisite — an engine-sequenced IR pipeline executor with an addressable <code>steps.<id>.output</code> store — was delivered as Plan 1 (workflow IR, ADR-0037). This ADR covers Plan 2 only.</p> <h2 id="decisions-2"><a class="header" href="#decisions-2">Decisions</a></h2> <h3 id="decision-1--check-is-not-a-node-enum-variant"><a class="header" href="#decision-1--check-is-not-a-node-enum-variant">Decision 1 — <code>Check</code> is NOT a <code>Node</code> enum variant</a></h3> <p>The <code>Node</code> enum (<code>Agent</code> / <code>Tool</code> / <code>Deterministic</code> / <code>Subflow</code>) is a type abstraction that never appears in the serialized <code>IrModule</code>. Only the <code>Workflow</code> <code>BTreeMap</code>s do. Adding a <code>Check</code> variant to <code>Node</code> would create ripple through every exhaustive <code>match</code> on <code>Node</code> across the codebase and tie a cross-cutting control-flow concept to an abstraction whose purpose is typing individual steps.</p> <p><strong>Decision:</strong> <code>Check</code> lives in a new <code>workflow.checks: BTreeMap<CheckId, Check></code> map. It is positioned in the pipeline via a new <code>StepRun::Check(CheckId)</code> step variant. <code>Node</code> is untouched.</p> <p>This is exactly the same pattern used for capabilities (carried in separate maps, not embedded in the node type).</p> <h3 id="decision-2--checks-are-pipeline-steps-default-appended-at-the-tail"><a class="header" href="#decision-2--checks-are-pipeline-steps-default-appended-at-the-tail">Decision 2 — Checks are pipeline steps, default-appended at the tail</a></h3> <p>The authoring surface (<code>[goals.*]</code> / <code>[deliverables.*]</code>) carries no position field. Lowering auto-appends one <code>StepRun::Check</code> step per check at the end of <code>pipeline.steps</code>, in deterministic order (goals by id, then deliverables by id).</p> <p>A check may also be placed at an explicit checkpoint by writing a pipeline step <code>run = "check:<id>"</code>. An explicitly-placed check is not auto-appended — it is used only at the explicit position.</p> <p><strong>Why not a separate "tail" concept:</strong> keeping checks as ordinary pipeline steps means the pipeline array is the single source of execution order. Introspection, trace spans, and step-output references all work uniformly. The "checkpoints anywhere" door is left open with zero rework.</p> <h3 id="decision-3--all-build-time-semantic-checks-live-in-tau-pkgvalidate"><a class="header" href="#decision-3--all-build-time-semantic-checks-live-in-tau-pkgvalidate">Decision 3 — All build-time semantic checks live in <code>tau-pkg::validate()</code></a></h3> <p><code>tau-pkg</code> owns <code>ProjectConfig</code>, the pipeline order, agent <code>produces</code>, tool capabilities, and glob subset logic, and has <code>std</code> (including regex). <code>tau-ir</code> depends on <code>tau-pkg</code> — not the reverse — so performing the producer/gate/judge/regex checks in <code>tau-pkg</code> needs no new cross-crate dep and keeps <code>tau-ir</code> lowering to structural integrity only (referenced IDs exist, locus step order is respected).</p> <p>This is the existing split: <code>tau-pkg</code> owns semantics, <code>tau-ir</code> owns structure.</p> <h3 id="decision-4--goal-predicates-are-host-registered-deterministicregistry-fns"><a class="header" href="#decision-4--goal-predicates-are-host-registered-deterministicregistry-fns">Decision 4 — Goal predicates are host-registered <code>DeterministicRegistry</code> fns</a></h3> <p><code>tau-runtime-core</code> is <code>#![no_std]</code> + <code>alloc</code> and cannot run regex or <code>std::fs</code>. The six menu predicates (<code>exists</code> / <code>non_empty</code> / <code>equals</code> / <code>matches</code> / <code>min_count</code> / <code>schema_valid</code>) and the native-fn escape hatch all route through the existing <code>DeterministicRegistry</code> port.</p> <p><code>run_pipeline</code> resolves the locus to content (file via the artifact reader, or named output from the output store), builds a JSON args object <code>{ present, content, ...params }</code>, and calls <code>registry.invoke(fn_name, &args)</code>. The host (<code>tau-cli</code> / conformance) registers the six menu predicates under reserved fn names (<code>__tau::goal::exists</code>, etc.). The escape-hatch <code>fn</code> routes to the same registry.</p> <p><strong>Why not a separate predicate evaluator:</strong> the deterministic-fn machinery already handles the exact shape (named fn, JSON args, JSON result). Reusing it means the escape hatch is one registry entry, not a new dispatch path.</p> <h3 id="decision-5--the-artifact-reader-is-a-defaulted-tooldispatcher-method"><a class="header" href="#decision-5--the-artifact-reader-is-a-defaulted-tooldispatcher-method">Decision 5 — The artifact reader is a defaulted <code>ToolDispatcher</code> method</a></h3> <p>Mirroring <code>deterministic_registry()</code> / <code>clock()</code> / <code>random()</code>, a new <code>fn artifact_reader(&self) -> Option<Arc<dyn ArtifactReader>> { None }</code> is added as a defaulted method on <code>ToolDispatcher</code>. No change to <code>run_pipeline</code>'s signature or its callers. The tokio host returns a <code>std::fs</code> reader; tests return an in-memory mock (<code>InMemoryArtifactReader</code>).</p> <p>This keeps <code>tau-runtime-core</code> I/O-free and the host substitutable (the conformance test harness and the production binary register different readers via the same interface).</p> <h3 id="decision-6--judge_model-is-a-runtime-no-op-in-v1-honest-limit"><a class="header" href="#decision-6--judge_model-is-a-runtime-no-op-in-v1-honest-limit">Decision 6 — <code>judge_model</code> is a runtime no-op in v1 (honest limit)</a></h3> <p>The <code>judge_model</code> field is <strong>parsed, validated at build time, stored in the IR, and included in the bundle hash</strong> — so it is meaningful as declarative intent. However, at runtime in v1, it is a <strong>no-op</strong>.</p> <p>The reason is structural: the <code>ToolDispatcher</code> exposes a single <code>llm_backend()</code> and <code>Agent.model</code> is already ignored at runtime today (every request uses <code>backend.name()</code>). Per-judge (and per-agent) model selection requires multi-backend resolution — routing an inference request to a specific model provider given a model name — which does not exist yet.</p> <p>So the built-in judge and any custom judge run on the ambient backend in v1. This is stated in the how-to guide and in this ADR, not papered over.</p> <p><strong>Consequence:</strong> a <code>tau check</code> that validates <code>judge_model = "claude-opus-4-5"</code> succeeds; the runtime silently uses the ambient backend. When multi-backend routing is implemented, the stored <code>judge_model</code> value is already in the IR and will begin to take effect without an authoring change.</p> <h3 id="decision-7--bundle-format-v110--v120-additive-minor-bump"><a class="header" href="#decision-7--bundle-format-v110--v120-additive-minor-bump">Decision 7 — Bundle format <code>v1.1.0</code> → <code>v1.2.0</code> (additive MINOR bump)</a></h3> <p><code>workflow.checks</code> is serialized with <code>#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "BTreeMap::is_empty")]</code> and <code>StepRun::Check</code> never appears in a check-free pipeline. Every existing fixture's canonical bytes are unchanged (asserted by the conformance suite).</p> <p>The bump is MINOR per semver: new fields, backward-compatible read (a v1.1.0 reader ignores <code>workflow.checks</code>; a v1.2.0 reader handles both).</p> <h2 id="honest-limits-and-deferrals"><a class="header" href="#honest-limits-and-deferrals">Honest limits and deferrals</a></h2> <h3 id="judge_model-runtime-no-op-decision-6-above"><a class="header" href="#judge_model-runtime-no-op-decision-6-above"><code>judge_model</code> runtime no-op (Decision 6 above)</a></h3> <p>Repeated here for emphasis: the field is fully supported at the config / IR / bundle level; it is only the <em>runtime selection</em> that is deferred to the multi-backend resolver.</p> <h3 id="output_schema-judge-compatibility-warning-is-deferred"><a class="header" href="#output_schema-judge-compatibility-warning-is-deferred"><code>output_schema</code> judge-compatibility warning is deferred</a></h3> <p>The design spec includes a build-time warning:</p> <blockquote> <p><code>warn: agent 'house_critic' used as a judge declares an output_schema</code> <code>incompatible with the verdict contract { met, rationale }</code></p> </blockquote> <p>This warning is not implemented in v1. <code>AgentEntry</code> has no <code>output_schema</code> field today — only <code>Deterministic</code> steps have one. When <code>AgentEntry</code> gains an <code>output_schema</code>, checking compatibility with the <code>{ met, rationale }</code> verdict contract is a straightforward follow-up (one <code>validate_postconditions</code> check). Nothing prevents adding it then.</p> <h3 id="multi-check-feedback-uses-single-gate-semantics"><a class="header" href="#multi-check-feedback-uses-single-gate-semantics">Multi-check feedback uses single-gate semantics</a></h3> <p>When multiple checks exist in a pipeline and a check rewinds to its gate, feedback from earlier checks that passed within the same rewind span may be cleared when the rewind re-executes those steps. The current implementation uses a single <code>feedback: Option<String></code> variable — per-check feedback isolation (each check's rationale travels independently through its own span) is acceptable-for-v1 future work.</p> <h3 id="tau-check---json-reports-kind--other-for-new-projectconfigerror-variants"><a class="header" href="#tau-check---json-reports-kind--other-for-new-projectconfigerror-variants"><code>tau check --json</code> reports <code>kind = "Other"</code> for new <code>ProjectConfigError</code> variants</a></h3> <p>The human-readable and SARIF outputs of <code>tau check</code> carry the full error message for all new <code>ProjectConfigError</code> variants (<code>DeliverableNoProducer</code>, <code>GateAfterProducer</code>, etc.). The structured JSON <code>kind</code> field, however, classifies these as <code>"Other"</code> rather than a specific kind string. Adding precise <code>kind</code> classification is a minor follow-up that requires extending the <code>kind</code> discriminant mapping in the check renderer.</p> <h3 id="loci-deferred-from-v1"><a class="header" href="#loci-deferred-from-v1">Loci deferred from v1</a></h3> <p>The following deliverable locus types are explicitly out of scope and not implemented:</p> <ul> <li>External resources via capability (HTTP/MCP side-effects).</li> <li>Provenance/trace evidence ("tool X was invoked").</li> <li>Process outcome loci ("step exited 0" — belongs in <code>goal</code>).</li> </ul> <h3 id="legacy-tau-workflow-runner"><a class="header" href="#legacy-tau-workflow-runner">Legacy <code>tau-workflow</code> runner</a></h3> <p>The standalone <code>tau-workflow</code> runner (<code>workflows/*.toml</code>) never lowers to IR and does not gain this feature. Unifying it onto the IR is a separate migration project.</p> <h2 id="consequences-41"><a class="header" href="#consequences-41">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Pipelines that cannot produce a deliverable are rejected at <code>tau build</code> / <code>tau check</code> before any run — zero tokens spent on a structurally broken pipeline.</li> <li>The producer binding (<code>produces</code> + <code>fs.write</code> coverage) brings Rust-style explicit intent to artifact ownership — ambiguity (two agents claiming the same path) is a build error.</li> <li>The retry loop is bounded at two levels (<code>max_attempts</code> + <code>AgentBudget</code>) and structurally guaranteed (gate ≤ producer, span has an LLM step) at build time — guaranteed-no-op loops are rejected before runtime.</li> <li>The deterministic-fn reuse means the six menu predicates share the same registration and extension story as any native fn — no separate predicate evaluator to maintain.</li> <li>Every verdict (pass, fail, retry) is durable in the trace with the <code>rationale</code> at each attempt — the full retry history is observable.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li><code>produces</code> is an explicit declaration — an agent that writes a file without declaring <code>produces</code> will not bind to a deliverable. This is intentional (intent > inference) but requires authors to be explicit.</li> <li><code>judge_model</code> silently does nothing in v1. Authors who write it will not see an error; they will see no effect. The ADR and how-to guide document this clearly.</li> <li>The <code>output_schema</code> judge-compatibility check is absent — a custom judge that returns something other than <code>{ met, rationale }</code> fails at runtime (parse error → <code>met: false</code>), not at build time.</li> <li>Multi-backend routing (to make <code>judge_model</code> effective) is a prerequisite for the "tune" judge level to work end-to-end.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-33"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-33">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <p><strong>A — Make <code>Check</code> a <code>Node</code> enum variant.</strong> Avoids the new <code>workflow.checks</code> map. Rejected because <code>Node</code> is exhaustively matched throughout the codebase (interpreter, typecheck, capability-fit, etc.); adding a variant creates structural ripple and couples a cross-cutting control-flow concept to a type-abstraction enum whose purpose is individual step typing.</p> <p><strong>B — Infer the producer from capability paths (no <code>produces</code> field).</strong> Build time checks capabilities to find which agent <em>could</em> write the deliverable path. Rejected because capability paths are glob patterns — inference produces ambiguity (multiple agents may have covering capabilities) and loses intent (the agent intended to write the file, not just that it was allowed to). <code>produces</code> is the Rust-fn-signature analogue: explicit, verifiable, binding.</p> <p><strong>C — Reuse the existing <code>DeterministicStep.fn_ref</code> mechanism vs. a new predicate enum.</strong> The predicate menu could be encoded as six specific <code>fn_ref</code> values registered at host init. Chosen: the enum (<code>GoalPredicate</code>) makes the serialized IR self-documenting and keeps common predicates readable in bundles; the native-fn escape hatch (<code>NativeFn(fn_ref)</code>) gives the power path. The registry remains the single execution point.</p> <p><strong>D — Run the judge inline in <code>run_pipeline</code> without synthesizing an <code>Agent</code>.</strong> Simpler code path. Rejected because the <code>run_agent</code> / <code>AgentBudget</code> budget cap then does not apply to the judge, making it possible to burn unbounded tokens in a judge with no cap. Synthesizing an <code>Agent</code> with <code>budget.max_turns = Some(1)</code> gives the judge the same budget machinery as every other agent.</p> <h2 id="references-24"><a class="header" href="#references-24">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Implementation plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-13-deliverables-and-goals.md</code></li> <li>Design spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-deliverables-and-goals-design.md</code></li> <li>How-to guide: <a href="decisions/../how-to/assert-pipeline-postconditions.html"><code>docs/how-to/assert-pipeline-postconditions.md</code></a></li> <li>Related ADRs: <a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">ADR-0037</a> (workflow IR, Plan 1), <a href="decisions/0010-tool-args-schema-validation.html">ADR-0010</a> (JSON schema validation), <a href="decisions/0014-sandboxing.html">ADR-0014</a> (capability model)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0045-context-manager-primitive-β4"><a class="header" href="#adr-0045-context-manager-primitive-β4">ADR-0045: Context-manager primitive (β.4)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-14 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-48"><a class="header" href="#context-48">Context</a></h2> <p>The runtime currently sends the <strong>entire conversation history on every inference turn</strong> — no truncation, compaction, or budgeting. This produces three failure modes at scale: hitting the context window (hard failure), paying for re-sent stale tool dumps every turn (cost scales with tokens), and "context rot" as the window fills. The ROADMAP β.4 milestone and <code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code> call for an opt-in, declarative <strong>context manager</strong> that is backward-compatible by absence, lowered to IR, and portable into a wasm bundle.</p> <p>β.4 is also a prerequisite for the β.6 canonical <code>fan-monitor</code> conformance scenario (which declares a context block) and for the β.8 <code>contextManager()</code> TS factory (currently parse-rejected pending β.4).</p> <p>tau's standing principle — <em>any check that could run at build time must run at build time</em> — applies here: unknown transformer names, a missing <code>fit_budget</code> terminus, duplicate steps, unresolved custom-node references, and ungranted capability declarations are all rejected at <code>tau build</code> / <code>tau check</code>, not discovered at runtime.</p> <p>Full design detail is in <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-4-context-manager-design.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>ADR numbering note:</strong> two <code>0044-*.md</code> files currently collide (<code>0044-trigger-ingress-slice-1.md</code> and <code>0044-deliverables-and-goals.md</code>). This ADR claims 0045 regardless; the collision is a separate cleanup.</p> <h2 id="decisions-3"><a class="header" href="#decisions-3">Decisions</a></h2> <h3 id="decision-1--layered-hybrid-architecture"><a class="header" href="#decision-1--layered-hybrid-architecture">Decision 1 — Layered hybrid architecture</a></h3> <p>v1 ships a deterministic <strong>context pipeline</strong> (Layer 1) as the conformance-gated core. Agent-driven memory tools (β.4.4) and retrieval via contracted MCP (γ.6) are additive layers above it.</p> <pre><code>AGENT — every inference turn LAYER 1 — declarative context pipeline (CORE) ← β.4 v1 trim_old → compact_tool_outputs → fit_budget pure, runtime-applied, author-declared ★ THE CONFORMANCE-GATED PART (β.6 bit-identical) later transformers slot in here via the same trait: offload_tool_outputs (β.4.2, pure → fs) summarize_oldest (β.4.3, LLM, cassette-replayed) recite_goal (β.4.4, pure) LAYER 2 — agent-driven memory TOOLS (capability) ← β.4.4 LAYER 3 — retrieval via contracted MCP ← γ.6 (NG6) </code></pre> <p>The SOTA→tier roadmap, anchored to industry/research sources:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Technique</th><th>Source</th><th>Determinism</th><th>tau tier</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Truncation / sliding window</td><td>ubiquitous</td><td>pure</td><td><code>trim_old</code> — v1</td></tr> <tr><td>Tool-result clearing</td><td>Anthropic ("safest lightest compaction")</td><td>pure</td><td><code>compact_tool_outputs</code> — v1</td></tr> <tr><td>Token-budget fitting</td><td>ubiquitous</td><td>pure</td><td><code>fit_budget</code> — v1</td></tr> <tr><td>Restorable externalization</td><td>Manus; Anthropic "just-in-time"</td><td>pure + fs</td><td>β.4.2</td></tr> <tr><td>LLM compaction / summary</td><td>Anthropic; LangChain; Mem0</td><td>LLM-backed</td><td>β.4.3</td></tr> <tr><td>Structured memory tools</td><td>Anthropic memory tool; Manus <code>todo.md</code></td><td>agent-driven</td><td>β.4.4</td></tr> <tr><td>Retrieval / vector memory</td><td>MemGPT; RAG</td><td>external store</td><td>γ.6 (NG6)</td></tr> <tr><td>Hierarchical paging</td><td>MemGPT / Letta</td><td>agent + MCP</td><td>apex tier</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Sources: Anthropic — Effective context engineering for AI agents; Manus — Context Engineering for AI Agents; MemGPT: LLMs as Operating Systems (arXiv:2310.08560); CoALA (arXiv:2309.02427).</p> <h3 id="decision-2--determinismclass-is-the-conformance-boundary-enforced-structurally"><a class="header" href="#decision-2--determinismclass-is-the-conformance-boundary-enforced-structurally">Decision 2 — <code>DeterminismClass</code> is the conformance boundary, enforced structurally</a></h3> <p>The <code>ContextTransformer</code> trait declares <code>fn determinism() -> DeterminismClass</code> (<code>Pure | LlmBacked | Stateful</code>). <code>TransformCx</code> gates what a transformer can <em>access</em> based on its declared class:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Class</th><th><code>TransformCx</code> exposes</th><th>β.6 conformance</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>Pure</code></td><td><code>estimate_tokens()</code> + config</td><td>gated (bit-identical)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>LlmBacked</code></td><td>+ <code>llm: &dyn LlmBackend</code></td><td>gated via cassette replay (β.4.3)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Stateful</code></td><td>+ <code>store: &mut dyn MemoryStore</code></td><td>excluded (Layer 2)</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>A <code>Pure</code> transformer has <em>no handle</em> to a model — the type system prevents it from calling one. This is structural enforcement, not documentation. v1 ships three <code>Pure</code> transformers: <code>trim_old</code>, <code>compact_tool_outputs</code>, <code>fit_budget</code>.</p> <h3 id="decision-3--e1-heuristic-token-estimator-behind-a-swappable-port"><a class="header" href="#decision-3--e1-heuristic-token-estimator-behind-a-swappable-port">Decision 3 — E1 heuristic token estimator behind a swappable port</a></h3> <p><code>fit_budget</code> needs per-message token counts; the backend only provides usage <em>after</em> a call. v1 ships <code>ceil(serialized_bytes / 4)</code> plus per-role/structural overhead as the <code>TokenEstimator</code> implementation:</p> <pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust"><span class="boring">#![allow(unused)] </span><span class="boring">fn main() { </span>trait TokenEstimator { fn estimate(&self, msg: &Message) -> u32; } // v1: ceil(bytes/4) + per-role overhead <span class="boring">}</span></code></pre></pre> <p>This is pure arithmetic — deterministic, portable (works unchanged in wasm), and requires no vocabulary blob. <code>fit_budget</code> enforces a <em>ceiling</em>, so a conservative over-estimate is safe: at worst it drops one extra old turn. A real per-model tokenizer or a backend-provided count can replace this later behind the same port with no change to the transformer contract.</p> <h3 id="decision-4--public-extension-contract-open-registry-native-first"><a class="header" href="#decision-4--public-extension-contract-open-registry-native-first">Decision 4 — Public extension contract: open registry, native-first</a></h3> <p><code>ContextTransformer</code> is a <strong>public, stable SDK surface</strong>. The registry is <strong>open</strong> (not a closed enum). A <code>kind="custom"</code> IR node is reserved in v1.</p> <p>v1 ships the <strong>native lane</strong> (Lane 3): users implement <code>ContextTransformer</code> in Rust and register via the host static builder. Two further lanes are reserved but deferred:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Wasm component lane</strong> — a WIT <code>context-transformer</code> interface; rides β.7.5/γ.1. WIT sketch:</p> <pre><code class="language-wit">interface context-transformer { record message { /* mirrors tau-domain Message shape */ } enum determinism { pure, llm-backed, stateful } transform: func(msgs: list<message>, config: string) -> result<list<message>, string>; } </code></pre> </li> <li> <p><strong>MCP lane</strong> — stateful/external nodes contracted over MCP; β.4.4+.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Native custom nodes run in-process; capability enforcement is build-time (declared vs. granted). The wasm lane is the recommended path for third-party nodes once it lands (sandboxed by construction).</p> <h3 id="decision-5--five-locked-contracts"><a class="header" href="#decision-5--five-locked-contracts">Decision 5 — Five locked contracts</a></h3> <p>Five cross-cutting contracts are locked in v1 so later tiers slot in without an IR or trait break:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Contract</th><th>Why it must be in v1</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>1</td><td><code>DeterminismClass</code> on the trait</td><td>conformance boundary + <code>cx</code> scoping (Decision 2)</td></tr> <tr><td>2</td><td>Per-transformer capability declaration (<code>required_capabilities()</code>)</td><td>safety for all nodes including custom</td></tr> <tr><td>3</td><td>Restorable-handle convention</td><td>β.4.2 offload + γ.6 retrieve share a stable handle shape</td></tr> <tr><td>4</td><td>KV-cache / append-only invariant</td><td>cheap now, expensive to retrofit; prefix-busting is declared metadata</td></tr> <tr><td>5</td><td><code>ContextTransformer</code> = public SDK + open registry + <code>kind="custom"</code> IR node</td><td>user nodes slot in with no IR or trait break</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Contract 3 detail: v1's <code>compact_tool_outputs</code> uses a <strong>non-restorable</strong> truncation marker; the handle shape for restorable externalization is defined but the fs-write path is deferred to β.4.2.</p> <p>Contract 4 detail: v1's three transformers are prefix-stable except <code>fit_budget</code> when it must drop from the head — a declared, unavoidable cache cost.</p> <h3 id="decision-6--transformers-run-on-a-copy-stored-history-is-never-mutated"><a class="header" href="#decision-6--transformers-run-on-a-copy-stored-history-is-never-mutated">Decision 6 — Transformers run on a copy; stored history is never mutated</a></h3> <p>The per-turn pipeline transforms <code>msgs: Vec<Message></code> — a copy assembled for the current turn. The result (budgeted view) is what gets projected to the LLM via <code>agent_messages_to_provider_messages()</code>. Stored conversation history is untouched. This means re-running the same turn against the same history always produces the same budgeted view (deterministic).</p> <h3 id="decision-7--context-pipeline-failures-are-kernel-errors-not-agent-failures"><a class="header" href="#decision-7--context-pipeline-failures-are-kernel-errors-not-agent-failures">Decision 7 — Context-pipeline failures are kernel errors, not agent failures</a></h3> <p>A <code>ContextError</code> (e.g. <code>BudgetUnsatisfiable</code> — the system prompt + live turn alone exceed <code>max_tokens</code>) routes through <code>RuntimeError::ContextPipeline</code>, not through <code>RunOutcome::Failed</code>. Per ADR-0006's error/failure dichotomy: an error is a kernel-level abort; a failure is an agent-level outcome the orchestrator can handle. A budget that cannot be satisfied is structural — retrying the agent loop cannot fix it.</p> <h3 id="decision-8--build-time-ir-typecheck-enforces-fit_budget-terminus"><a class="header" href="#decision-8--build-time-ir-typecheck-enforces-fit_budget-terminus">Decision 8 — Build-time IR typecheck enforces <code>fit_budget</code> terminus</a></h3> <p>The IR typecheck rejects any context pipeline that does not end with <code>fit_budget</code>, references an unknown builtin, or contains a duplicate step. This is the "any check that could run at build time must run at build time" discipline applied to the context surface.</p> <p><strong>Beneficial behavior change:</strong> implementing this check surfaced a latent defect — <code>tau build</code> previously swallowed all <code>IrError</code>s from lowering (warn + exit 0) and exited 0. It now exits 2 on any lowering error, consistent with tau's enforcement discipline. This is a breaking change for pipelines with lowering errors that were silently passing <code>tau build</code>; those pipelines were already broken at runtime.</p> <h3 id="decision-9--deferred-scope"><a class="header" href="#decision-9--deferred-scope">Decision 9 — Deferred scope</a></h3> <p>The following are out of scope for v1 and banked as sequenced future work:</p> <ul> <li><code>offload_tool_outputs</code> — restorable fs externalization (β.4.2, pure, needs <code>fs.write</code> capability).</li> <li><code>summarize_oldest</code> / <code>compact</code> — LLM-backed transformers (β.4.3, requires cassette-replayed determinism for conformance).</li> <li>Memory-tool layer + <code>recite_goal</code> (β.4.4, agent-driven, Layer 2 begins).</li> <li>Retrieval via contracted vector-store MCP (γ.6, NG6 keeps it external).</li> <li>Real per-model tokenizer (available behind the <code>TokenEstimator</code> port on demand).</li> <li>Wasm/MCP custom-node loaders (contract reserved; loaders ride β.7.5/γ.1 and β.4.4).</li> <li><strong>Runtime capability enforcement for custom nodes</strong> — deferred to β.4.2, when the first capability-declaring node (fs-write offload) exists. v1 builtins declare no capabilities;
