native custom nodes run in-process and capabilities are checked at build time only.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-42"><a class="header" href="#consequences-42">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Long-horizon runs no longer hit the context window with no recovery path — <code>fit_budget</code> enforces a hard ceiling before the request is sent.</li> <li>All three v1 transformers are <code>Pure</code> → β.6 conformance is bit-identical with zero special casing.</li> <li>Backward compatibility is absolute: an agent with no context block behaves byte-identically to today (no <code>ContextStepRan</code> events emitted).</li> <li>The five locked contracts ensure β.4.2/β.4.3/β.4.4/γ.6 slot in without an IR or trait break.</li> <li>The open registry means users can define native custom nodes today; the wasm sandbox lane arrives with β.7.5 without touching the contract.</li> <li><code>tau build</code> now exits 2 on any lowering error — a latent silent-failure class is closed.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Authors must declare a context block explicitly — context management is opt-in. There is no auto-inferred context policy.</li> <li><code>fit_budget</code> must be the last pipeline step (build-time enforced) — authors who omit it or place it mid-pipeline get a build error, not a runtime surprise.</li> <li>The E1 heuristic may over-count tokens, causing <code>fit_budget</code> to drop one extra old turn. This is acceptable; a real tokenizer can be swapped in.</li> <li>Native custom nodes run in-process; the wasm sandboxed lane is deferred. Third-party custom nodes are in-process until β.7.5.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-34"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-34">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <p><strong>Pipeline-only forever (no agent-driven layers):</strong> the three v1 transformers plus future offload/summarize would be the full story. Rejected because no deterministic transformer can match MemGPT-style hierarchical paging (which requires agent invocation and an external store). The layered architecture is the only shape that reaches the SOTA apex while keeping tau's invariants.</p> <p><strong>MemGPT-in-core (bake a memory store into <code>tau-runtime-core</code>):</strong> would collapse all tiers into one system. Rejected because: (a) it violates constitutional non-goal NG6 ("no built-in persistent memory store"); (b) it wrecks determinism (the core becomes stateful against an external store); (c) wasm portability requires I/O-free core. MemGPT-style paging is achievable via Layer 2 + Layer 3 without touching the core.</p> <p><strong>Closed transformer enum (no open registry):</strong> simpler dispatch. Rejected because the public extension point (custom nodes) is load-bearing — power users need it before wasm lands, and closing the enum would require an IR bump for every new builtin.</p> <p><strong>Real per-model tokenizer in v1:</strong> exact token counts. Rejected because: a vocabulary blob is model-specific (tight coupling to Anthropic/OpenAI internal tokenizers), heavy (wasm size cost), and non-portable (MCU). The E1 heuristic is sufficient for a ceiling-enforcement use case; the port accepts a drop-in later.</p> <p><strong>Route <code>BudgetUnsatisfiable</code> through <code>RunOutcome::Failed</code>:</strong> allows the agent orchestrator to handle the error. Rejected because a budget that cannot be satisfied for the <em>system prompt + live turn</em> is a structural misconfiguration — the agent cannot recover by retrying; a human must fix the <code>max_tokens</code> or <code>keep_last_turns</code> settings. Routing it through <code>RuntimeError</code> is consistent with ADR-0006's error/failure split.</p> <h2 id="references-25"><a class="header" href="#references-25">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Design spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-4-context-manager-design.md</code></li> <li>Related ADRs: <a href="decisions/0006-tau-runtime.html">ADR-0006</a> (error/failure dichotomy), <a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">ADR-0037</a> (workflow IR + IR checks), <a href="decisions/0044-deliverables-and-goals.html">ADR-0044</a> (build-time checks pattern), <a href="decisions/0014-sandboxing.html">ADR-0014</a> (capability model)</li> <li>Philosophy: <a href="decisions/../explanation/tau-philosophy.html"><code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code></a></li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0046-wasm-aot-artifact--wit-world-β75"><a class="header" href="#adr-0046-wasm-aot-artifact--wit-world-β75">ADR-0046: Wasm AOT artifact + WIT world (β.7.5)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Proposed <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-14 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-49"><a class="header" href="#context-49">Context</a></h2> <p>β.7.5 extends tau's "one engine, two modes" architecture with an <strong>ahead-of-time path</strong>: <code>tau build wasm <project></code> lowers the project's workflow IR + <code>tau-runtime-core</code> + native tools into a single runnable <strong>WASI 0.2 wasm component</strong>. The artifact runs in wasmtime and reproduces the same observable side-effects as <code>tau dev</code> / <code>tau run --bundle</code>.</p> <p>Two design forces shape every decision here:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Philosophy: "your tools linked statically."</strong> The wasm artifact must be self-contained — host imports are inference + nondeterminism only. Everything else (context manager, MCP facilitator, cassette replay) must compile <em>into</em> the guest.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The IR interpreter (<code>run_ir</code>) never emitted <code>RunEvent</code>s.</strong> That is a <code>Runtime::run_streaming</code> (legacy) concept. The <em>implemented</em> conformance contract is <code>ConformanceReport</code> (D-7a multiset). Promoting the observable to a literal <code>RunEvent</code> stream is a <strong>β.6</strong> decision (the conformance gate lives there); this ADR records that tension explicitly rather than papering over it.</p> </li> </ol> <p>ADR-0040 split β.7 (the <code>tau dev</code> REPL) from β.7.5 (this) because the in-wasm MCP-facilitator path ballooned after β.3 PR-5/PR-6. ADR-0047 (in-wasm MCP facilitator, forthcoming in Phase 5) records the facilitator specifics; this ADR records the artifact shape, toolchain, and conformance boundary.</p> <p>Full design detail is in <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-7-5-wasm-aot-design.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="decisions-4"><a class="header" href="#decisions-4">Decisions</a></h2> <h3 id="decision-1--approach-b-fully-linked-guest"><a class="header" href="#decision-1--approach-b-fully-linked-guest">Decision 1 — Approach B: fully-linked guest</a></h3> <p>Native tools, the context manager (β.4), the MCP facilitator, and the cassette replayer all compile <strong>into</strong> the wasm guest. There is no thin-guest option where host imports supply tool logic.</p> <p>Rationale: the philosophy's "harness everywhere with statically linked tools" wedge; it hits portability wedge #2 (MCP host in wasm). This is feasible because <code>tau-mcp</code>, the context manager, and <code>tau-runtime-core</code> are all <code>no_std</code> in core. Alternative A (thin guest, tool logic in host imports) is rejected because it defeats the portability goal and collapses back to a different remotely-hosted architecture with no wasm-isolation benefit.</p> <h3 id="decision-2--observable--conformancereport-d-7a-multiset"><a class="header" href="#decision-2--observable--conformancereport-d-7a-multiset">Decision 2 — Observable = <code>ConformanceReport</code> (D-7a multiset)</a></h3> <p>The guest exports a serialized <code>ConformanceReport</code>; the host reuses the existing <code>assert_conform</code> to compare dev↔wasm. The observable is <strong>not</strong> a literal <code>RunEvent</code> stream.</p> <p>Rationale: <code>run_ir</code> never emitted <code>RunEvents</code> — promoting to a literal <code>RunEvent</code> stream is a β.6 decision. Recording this as an explicit named gap is correct; papering over it with a new internal stream just for wasm would be speculative scope. The <code>ConformanceReport</code> D-7a multiset is the implemented conformance contract and is sufficient to enforce dev↔wasm parity.</p> <h3 id="decision-3--toolchain-wasm32-wasip2--wit-bindgen-no_std-no-cargo-component"><a class="header" href="#decision-3--toolchain-wasm32-wasip2--wit-bindgen-no_std-no-cargo-component">Decision 3 — Toolchain: <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> + <code>wit-bindgen</code> (<code>no_std</code>), no <code>cargo-component</code></a></h3> <p>Rust ≥ 1.82 emits a wasm component directly from a <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> crate; no <code>cargo-component</code> wrapper is needed. <code>wit-bindgen</code> is used for guest binding generation (supports <code>no_std</code>). <code>cargo-component</code> is experimental and std-leaning — rejected.</p> <h3 id="decision-4--the-taurun-wit-world"><a class="header" href="#decision-4--the-taurun-wit-world">Decision 4 — The <code>tau:run</code> WIT world</a></h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>Amended 2026-06-22:</strong> the package was renamed <code>tau:run</code> → <code>tau:host</code> to match ADR-0056 (the embedding contract is <code>tau:host</code>). The historical text below is preserved; see <code>docs/reference/wit-host-world.md</code> for the current contract.</p> </blockquote> <p>A single world <code>tau:run/runner</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-wit">package tau:run@0.1.0; interface host { /// Delegated inference. `request-json` is a serialized /// tau_ports::llm::CompletionRequest; returns a serialized /// CompletionResponse. (Cassette-backed in conformance.) complete: func(request-json: string) -> result<string, string>; /// Monotonic-ish wall clock in milliseconds (deterministic in conformance). now-millis: func() -> u64; /// Next u64 from the host RandomSource (deterministic in conformance). next-u64: func() -> u64; } world runner { import host; /// Drive the baked IR from its entry agent with `prompt`. /// Returns a serialized ConformanceReport (D-7a observable) on success. export run: func(prompt: string) -> result<string, string>; } </code></pre> <p><strong>Principle: host imports = inference + nondeterminism only; everything else is in-guest.</strong> The IR is <strong>not</strong> a parameter — it is baked into the guest at build time (<code>include_bytes!</code>). JSON-string payloads at the boundary (not rich WIT records) in v1 to minimise <code>wit-bindgen</code> surface and keep the guest <code>no_std</code>. Richer WIT records are a γ refinement.</p> <p>A <code>tau:mcp</code> interface for real (non-cassette) MCP transport is <strong>reserved but unused</strong> in β.7.5; it is recorded in ADR-0047 as the γ.1 expansion.</p> <h3 id="decision-5--guest-executor-single-threaded-block_on--p2p3-hedge"><a class="header" href="#decision-5--guest-executor-single-threaded-block_on--p2p3-hedge">Decision 5 — Guest executor: single-threaded <code>block_on</code> + p2/p3 hedge</a></h3> <p><code>run_ir</code> is <code>async</code> and its future is <strong>non-Send</strong> (RefCell internals). WASI 0.2 guests are single-threaded, so <code>Send</code> is irrelevant inside the guest. The exported <code>run</code> is synchronous-looking to the host; internally it drives the future to completion with a single-threaded <code>block_on</code> (<code>pollster</code>-style or a small custom waker). No wasmtime async, no host event loop in v1.</p> <p><strong>p2/p3 hedge:</strong> WASI 0.3 / Component Model Async shipped 2026-06-11 but cross-language tooling is immature. β.7.5 targets p2 + guest <code>block_on</code>. The executor is isolated behind a thin seam so a p3 lift (wasmtime 46 GA, native async) is a γ follow-on without reshaping the WIT world.</p> <h3 id="decision-6--ir-baking--cargo-hand-off"><a class="header" href="#decision-6--ir-baking--cargo-hand-off">Decision 6 — IR baking + cargo hand-off</a></h3> <p><code>tau build wasm <project></code> pipeline:</p> <ol> <li>Load + validate the project (reuse existing <code>tau build</code> front-end).</li> <li>Lower: <code>lower_project(config, any-wasi-strict, caches) → IrModule</code>. Capability-fit checks the project's required shapes against <code>any-wasi-strict</code>'s <code>{FsRead, FsWrite, NetHttp}</code> — a project needing <code>ProcessExec</code> / <code>AgentSpawn</code> is <strong>refused at build time</strong> (Rust-like build-time enforcement).</li> <li><code>to_canonical_bytes(module) → bytes</code>; write to a build-scratch file.</li> <li><code>include_bytes!</code> wiring: the guest embeds the bytes at build time. Reproducible: same source ⇒ same bytes.</li> <li>Shell <code>cargo build -p tau-wasm-guest --target wasm32-wasip2 --release</code> (with CARGO hygiene).</li> <li>Emit the artifact; print its hash.</li> </ol> <p>Per-project Rust codegen of arbitrary user tools is deferred to γ; β.7.5 links a fixed <code>no_std</code> tool library and bakes the IR.</p> <h3 id="decision-7--determinism-config"><a class="header" href="#decision-7--determinism-config">Decision 7 — Determinism <code>Config</code></a></h3> <p>Host <code>wasmtime::Config</code>:</p> <ul> <li><code>cranelift_nan_canonicalization(true)</code> — canonicalise all NaNs (f32/f64/v128).</li> <li><code>wasm_relaxed_simd(false)</code> or <code>relaxed_simd_deterministic(true)</code>.</li> <li>Fuel-based interruption (not epoch) if any bounding is needed.</li> </ul> <p>Time + randomness are <strong>host imports</strong> seeded deterministically for conformance (the existing <code>Clock</code> / <code>RandomSource</code> ports from β.1). Guest iteration order is guarded by <code>BTreeMap</code> / <code>hashbrown</code> discipline already in <code>tau-runtime-core</code>.</p> <h3 id="decision-8--new-triple-any-wasi-strict-reserved--available"><a class="header" href="#decision-8--new-triple-any-wasi-strict-reserved--available">Decision 8 — New triple <code>any-wasi-strict</code> (Reserved → Available)</a></h3> <p>Graduates the <code>any-wasi-strict</code> triple: <code>Platform::Any + AdapterFamily::Wasi + Strict</code>. Capability shapes: <code>{FilesystemRead, FilesystemWrite, NetworkHttp}</code>. <strong>No <code>ProcessExec</code> / <code>AgentSpawn</code></strong> — wasm guests cannot subprocess or OS-spawn, and this is enforced at build time (see Decision 6).</p> <h3 id="decision-9--wasmwasi-triples-are-exempt-from-the-process-gate-adapter-registry"><a class="header" href="#decision-9--wasmwasi-triples-are-exempt-from-the-process-gate-adapter-registry">Decision 9 — Wasm/WASI triples are exempt from the process-gate adapter registry</a></h3> <p><code>AdapterFamily::Wasi</code> has <strong>no <code>RegistryKind</code></strong> by design. Capability enforcement for wasm happens at the <strong>WASI boundary</strong> (the wasm host + the WIT capability imports), not via an OS process-gate adapter. The <code>registry_shape_coverage_check</code> test asserts this positively: a Wasi Available triple must have no process-gate registration.</p> <p><code>tau check --target any-wasi-strict</code> currently emits a non-fatal "no local adapter; static cross-check only" Warning — which is correct until the wasm host runner (<code>tau-wasm-host</code>) lands in β.7.5 Phase 3.</p> <h2 id="consequences-43"><a class="header" href="#consequences-43">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>The same <code>run_ir</code> and <code>tau-native-tools</code> implementations run in both the dev and wasm profiles — divergence can only enter via the 3 pinned host imports or wasmtime codegen (NaN-canon + deterministic relaxed-SIMD). This is structural parity, not aspirational.</li> <li><code>tau build wasm</code> refuses at build time any project that requires capabilities wasm guests cannot satisfy (<code>ProcessExec</code>, <code>AgentSpawn</code>) — consistent with tau's build-time enforcement discipline.</li> <li>The p2/p3 executor seam means WASI 0.3 async is a γ lift with no WIT world or API break.</li> <li>ADR-0047 (in-wasm MCP facilitator) can land independently in Phase 5 without reshaping this ADR's decisions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li><code>tau-wasm-guest</code> is a new <code>no_std</code> + alloc crate; CI must <code>rustup target add wasm32-wasip2</code> and build the exact release profile early (PR-2) to catch <code>no_std</code>/LTO toolchain bugs.</li> <li>The observable is <code>ConformanceReport</code>, not a literal <code>RunEvent</code> stream. Any consumer that expects a stream (β.6 conformance gate) is a <strong>named gap</strong>: promoting to a literal stream is deferred to β.6.</li> <li>Real (non-cassette) MCP transport from inside wasm is <strong>reserved but unimplemented</strong> in β.7.5. Projects that require live MCP connections cannot <code>tau build wasm</code> until the γ.1 <code>tau:mcp</code> host import lands.</li> <li><code>tau check --target any-wasi-strict</code> emits a non-fatal Warning ("no local adapter; static cross-check only") until the wasm host runner lands. This is intentional and correct.</li> </ul> <blockquote> <p><strong>Status (PR-E2, 2026-06-20):</strong> the guest now drives <code>run_ir_streaming</code> over the baked IR and returns the serialized typed <code>RunEvent</code> stream; the <code>dev == wasm</code> conformance arm (<code>WasmMode</code>) is flipped live in PR-G.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-35"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-35">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Approach A — thin guest, tools in host imports:</strong> rejected because it defeats the portability goal. The guest would merely be a protocol adapter, not a self-contained harness. Wasm-isolation benefit evaporates.</li> <li><strong>Literal <code>RunEvent</code> stream observable:</strong> deferred to β.6, not rejected. <code>run_ir</code> never emitted <code>RunEvent</code>s; adding a new internal stream purely for wasm would be speculative scope at this phase. <code>ConformanceReport</code> is the implemented contract.</li> <li><strong><code>cargo-component</code>:</strong> rejected; experimental, std-leaning, and adds build complexity without benefit over <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> + raw <code>wit-bindgen</code>.</li> <li><strong>WASI 0.3 async in v1:</strong> deferred to γ; cross-language tooling is immature (shipped 2026-06-11, 3 days before β.7.5 started). The thin executor seam keeps the door open.</li> <li><strong>Process-gate adapter for wasm triples:</strong> rejected; capability enforcement for wasm is at the WASI host boundary, not via OS process-gate adapters. Forcing a <code>RegistryKind</code> for <code>AdapterFamily::Wasi</code> would be architecturally wrong and would mislead <code>tau check</code> into treating wasm the same as a native triple.</li> </ul> <h2 id="references-26"><a class="header" href="#references-26">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Design spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-7-5-wasm-aot-design.md</code></li> <li>Plan: <code>docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-14-beta-7-5-wasm-aot.md</code></li> <li>Related ADRs: <a href="decisions/0034-target-triple-registry.html">ADR-0034</a> (target registry), <a href="decisions/0037-workflow-ir.html">ADR-0037</a> (workflow IR), <a href="decisions/0040-tau-dev-repl.html">ADR-0040</a> (<code>tau dev</code> REPL + β.7/β.7.5 split), <a href="decisions/0038-mcp-facilitator.html">ADR-0038</a> (MCP facilitator)</li> <li>ADR-0047 — in-wasm MCP facilitator (forthcoming, Phase 5)</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0047-credential-provider-chain-β5"><a class="header" href="#adr-0047-credential-provider-chain-β5">ADR-0047: Credential provider chain (β.5)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-14 <strong>Supersedes:</strong> none</p> <h2 id="context-50"><a class="header" href="#context-50">Context</a></h2> <p>The five in-tree plugins are separate subprocesses, and each rolls its own credential loader <em>inside its own process</em>: <code>anthropic</code>/<code>openai</code> read an API key from <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code>/<code>OPENAI_API_KEY</code> (configurable var name) and hold it as <code>secrecy::SecretString</code>; <code>ollama</code> reads an optional <code>OLLAMA_BEARER_TOKEN</code>; <code>fs-read</code>/<code>shell</code> take none. There is no way to source a credential from anywhere other than the plugin's own process environment — a mounted Kubernetes secret, a Vault lease, or an IRSA workload identity cannot reach a plugin without bespoke per-plugin code.</p> <p>ROADMAP §β.5 calls for a Strategy + Chain credential port so that <strong>deployment</strong>, not the plugin author, decides where a credential comes from, while <strong>every existing env-var path keeps working byte-for-byte</strong>. The per-plugin migration table couples actual plugin migration to a <em>separate</em> later event (in-tree <code>LlmBackend</code> extraction); β.5 lands the port + chain and makes unmodified plugins benefit via a host-side bridge.</p> <p>tau's standing principle — <em>any check that could run at build time must run at build time</em> — applies: an agent's declared credential <code>id</code>/<code>env</code> and a deployment's chain config are validated at <code>tau build</code> / config load, not discovered at spawn time.</p> <p>Full design detail is in <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-5-credential-provider-chain-design.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="decisions-5"><a class="header" href="#decisions-5">Decisions</a></h2> <h3 id="decision-1--async-strategy--chain-port-in-tau-ports"><a class="header" href="#decision-1--async-strategy--chain-port-in-tau-ports">Decision 1 — Async Strategy + Chain port in <code>tau-ports</code></a></h3> <p><code>CredentialProvider</code> is a public port in <code>tau-ports</code>, matching that crate's idioms (<code>#![no_std]</code> + <code>alloc</code>, native <code>async fn in trait</code>, <code>Send + Sync</code>, <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> <code>thiserror</code>):</p> <pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust"><span class="boring">#![allow(unused)] </span><span class="boring">fn main() { </span>#[allow(async_fn_in_trait)] pub trait CredentialProvider: Send + Sync { fn name(&self) -> &str; async fn resolve(&self, req: &CredentialRequest) -> Result<Option<ResolvedCredential>, CredentialError>; } <span class="boring">}</span></code></pre></pre> <p><code>resolve</code> is <strong>async</strong> even though v1's three providers are effectively sync, because the deferred providers (SecretManager, WorkloadIdentity, TokenBroker) are network calls. Async now means they slot in with zero port churn. <code>CredentialChain</code> is a composite that walks members in order and is <em>itself</em> a <code>CredentialProvider</code> (Strategy + Chain). The Chain is pure logic and lives in <code>tau-ports</code>; concrete I/O adapters live in adapter crates.</p> <h3 id="decision-2--oknone-walk-semantics-with-fail-fast-on-err"><a class="header" href="#decision-2--oknone-walk-semantics-with-fail-fast-on-err">Decision 2 — <code>Ok(None)</code> walk semantics with fail-fast on <code>Err</code></a></h3> <p>The chain distinguishes three member outcomes:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Outcome</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Chain action</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>Ok(Some(_))</code></td><td>provider resolved the credential</td><td>return it (first match wins)</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Ok(None)</code></td><td>provider does not hold this credential</td><td>continue to next member</td></tr> <tr><td><code>Err(e)</code></td><td>provider owns it but failed (e.g. Vault down)</td><td><strong>fail-fast</strong> — return <code>Err(e)</code></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Fail-fast is security-motivated: a <em>configured</em> secret manager that is unreachable must surface as an error, not silently fall through to a weaker provider. A whole-chain <code>Ok(None)</code> becomes "credential not found" at the same point today's <code>InvalidEnvVar</code> surfaces, so when <code>env</code> is the only member the error UX is unchanged.</p> <h3 id="decision-3--tau-native-secret-over-re-exporting-secrecy"><a class="header" href="#decision-3--tau-native-secret-over-re-exporting-secrecy">Decision 3 — tau-native <code>Secret</code> over re-exporting <code>secrecy</code></a></h3> <p>The port boundary speaks a new <code>tau-ports</code> type rather than re-exporting <code>secrecy::SecretString</code>:</p> <pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust"><span class="boring">#![allow(unused)] </span><span class="boring">fn main() { </span>pub struct Secret(zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>); // redacting Debug, zeroize-on-drop <span class="boring">}</span></code></pre></pre> <p>Rationale: (a) keeps <code>tau-ports</code> <code>no_std</code>-clean — <code>zeroize</code> is <code>no_std</code>-capable, <code>secrecy</code> is heavier and std-leaning; (b) holds <strong>bytes</strong>, not <code>String</code> — device / secure-element keys are binary, so a <code>String</code>-typed secret would be a design hole the moment <code>DeviceIdentity</code> lands. Plugin crates keep <code>secrecy</code> internally; only the port boundary uses <code>Secret</code>.</p> <h3 id="decision-4--host-resolve-then-inject-bridge-plugins-unmodified"><a class="header" href="#decision-4--host-resolve-then-inject-bridge-plugins-unmodified">Decision 4 — Host resolve-then-inject bridge; plugins unmodified</a></h3> <p>Before spawning a plugin, the tokio host runs the chain for each credential the agent declares and injects the resolved <code>Secret</code> into the child's environment under the declared env-var name. The plugin then reads that env var exactly as it does today. This is the integration that makes a File/Vault secret reach an <strong>unmodified</strong> subprocess plugin.</p> <p>Two backward-compat invariants, both byte-identical to today:</p> <ul> <li>An agent that declares <strong>no</strong> credentials → host injects nothing; child inherits the parent environment as today.</li> <li>No <code>[credentials]</code> block in scope config → chain defaults to <code>["env"]</code>; <code>EnvProvider</code> reads the same var the plugin would have read itself.</li> </ul> <p>Opting into the chain requires <em>declaring a credential</em>; changing where it resolves requires <em>configuring a non-env member</em>. When a plugin later migrates to an in-tree <code>LlmBackend</code>, it calls the chain directly and the thin env-injection shim retires; the port, providers, config, and declarations stay.</p> <h3 id="decision-5--two-layer-config-declaration-in-the-bundle-chain-in-the-deployment"><a class="header" href="#decision-5--two-layer-config-declaration-in-the-bundle-chain-in-the-deployment">Decision 5 — Two-layer config: declaration in the bundle, chain in the deployment</a></h3> <p>Credentials have two concerns with different homes:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Concern</th><th>Home</th><th>Why</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td>Per-agent declaration <code>[[agents.<id>.credentials]]</code> (<code>id</code> + <code>env</code>)</td><td><code>tau.toml</code> → <code>tau-pkg::project</code>, Unchecked→validate</td><td>intrinsic to the agent; travels in the bundle; reproducible</td></tr> <tr><td>Chain config <code>[credentials]</code> (providers + order)</td><td><code>TAU_HOME</code> scope config → <code>tau-pkg::scope</code>, Unchecked→validate</td><td>deployment-specific; same bundle runs env-locally / file-in-k8s / Vault-in-prod without rebuild</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>Baking Vault endpoints into a reproducible bundle would be a design hole; the split keeps the bundle portable. Both halves are validated at build/load time (unknown provider names, bad <code>id</code>/<code>env</code>, duplicate <code>env</code>, missing <code>file.dir</code>).</p> <h3 id="decision-6--ship-env--file--baked-reserve-the-four-heavy-providers"><a class="header" href="#decision-6--ship-env--file--baked-reserve-the-four-heavy-providers">Decision 6 — Ship Env + File + Baked; reserve the four heavy providers</a></h3> <p>v1 ships three providers:</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Provider</th><th>Crate</th><th><code>no_std</code></th><th>Role</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>BakedProvider</code></td><td><code>tau-ports</code> (fixtures)</td><td>yes</td><td>deterministic test provider; seeds embedded/wasm</td></tr> <tr><td><code>EnvProvider</code></td><td><code>tau-runtime-tokio</code></td><td>no</td><td>today's behavior; zero-config default</td></tr> <tr><td><code>FileProvider</code></td><td><code>tau-runtime-tokio</code></td><td>no</td><td>mounted-secret dir + <code>key_map</code>; the DoD CI provider</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>SecretManager (Vault/AWS/GCP/Azure), WorkloadIdentity (SPIFFE/IRSA), DeviceIdentity (secure-element), and TokenBroker (OIDC/OAuth2 BFF) are deferred. The async port + <code>Ok(None)</code>/<code>Err</code> walk + <code>expires_at</code> rotation hook + binary <code>Secret</code> make each a non-breaking addition (a new struct + a config arm).</p> <h3 id="decision-7--resolvedcredentialexpires_at-reserves-rotation-without-a-handle"><a class="header" href="#decision-7--resolvedcredentialexpires_at-reserves-rotation-without-a-handle">Decision 7 — <code>ResolvedCredential.expires_at</code> reserves rotation without a handle</a></h3> <p><code>resolve</code> returns a <em>value</em> (<code>ResolvedCredential { secret, expires_at, source }</code>), not a refreshable handle. Rotating providers (TokenBroker, Vault leases) carry <code>expires_at</code>; the consumer re-resolves past expiry. This keeps the port a pure resolver (like <code>CapabilityResolver</code>) and avoids a handle-lifecycle contract in v1 while reserving the rotation story.</p> <h2 id="consequences-44"><a class="header" href="#consequences-44">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>A mounted Kubernetes secret or Vault lease can reach an <strong>unmodified</strong> plugin today, with no plugin-code change.</li> <li>Backward compatibility is absolute: no declaration / no chain block → byte-identical to today's env-var path.</li> <li>The async port, byte <code>Secret</code>, fail-fast walk, and <code>expires_at</code> hook make all four deferred providers non-breaking additions.</li> <li>Bundle reproducibility is preserved: deployment wiring lives in scope config, not the bundle.</li> <li>The chain is exercised end-to-end by a new CI lane (<code>test (credential-chain / linux)</code>) via the File provider.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Negative / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li>The host gains a resolve-then-inject step in the spawn path (one injection point); it is a no-op when nothing is declared.</li> <li>Two config-validation surfaces must stay in sync with the provider set (project declaration + scope chain).</li> <li><code>Secret</code>-as-bytes means UTF-8 string consumers call <code>expose_str()</code> and handle the (practically impossible for API keys) non-UTF-8 case.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-36"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-36">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <p><strong>Standalone port, plugins fully untouched (synthetic CI consumer only).</strong> Rejected: lands an unused port that reads as dead code and rots; the resolve-then-inject bridge is a genuinely useful capability (mounted secret → live plugin) and is not throwaway — only the thin shim retires at the later LlmBackend extraction.</p> <p><strong>Re-export <code>secrecy::SecretString</code> as the port type.</strong> Rejected: pulls a heavier, std-leaning crate into <code>no_std</code> <code>tau-ports</code>, and <code>String</code>-typed secrets exclude binary device/secure-element keys — a future breaking change.</p> <p><strong>Chain config in <code>tau.toml</code> (single validate path).</strong> Rejected: bakes deployment wiring (Vault endpoints) into the reproducible bundle — the wrong layer; every redeploy would edit the bundle. The ROADMAP explicitly says deployment configures the chain order.</p> <p><strong>Sync <code>resolve</code>.</strong> Rejected: SecretManager/WorkloadIdentity/TokenBroker are network calls; a sync port would force a breaking signature change when the first network provider lands.</p> <p><strong>Migrate the five plugins onto the port now.</strong> Rejected: the migration-trigger table couples plugin migration to in-tree <code>LlmBackend</code> extraction, a separate event; doing it now means solving (and then discarding) the subprocess credential-injection boundary the bridge already covers.</p> <p><strong>Flat single-credential-per-agent declaration.</strong> Rejected: caps an agent at one credential — a design hole the moment any agent needs two (e.g. an API key plus an org token). The per-agent list costs one table entry for the common case.</p> <h2 id="references-27"><a class="header" href="#references-27">References</a></h2> <ul> <li>Design spec: <code>docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-14-beta-5-credential-provider-chain-design.md</code></li> <li>Related ADRs: <a href="decisions/0006-tau-runtime.html">ADR-0006</a> (error/failure dichotomy), <a href="decisions/0014-sandboxing.html">ADR-0014</a> (capability model), <a href="decisions/0044-deliverables-and-goals.html">ADR-0044</a> (build-time checks pattern)</li> <li>ROADMAP: §β.5; per-plugin migration triggers; CI gate <code>test (credential-chain / linux)</code></li> <li>Philosophy: <a href="decisions/../explanation/tau-philosophy.html"><code>docs/explanation/tau-philosophy.md</code></a></li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0048-β6-cross-target-conformance-gate--dual-channel-conformanceevent-contract"><a class="header" href="#adr-0048-β6-cross-target-conformance-gate--dual-channel-conformanceevent-contract">ADR-0048: β.6 cross-target conformance gate — dual-channel <code>ConformanceEvent</code> contract</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-14 <strong>Deciders:</strong> Titouan (architect), implementing session</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Update (2026-06-16):</strong> Decision 1 below (dual-channel sourcing) is <strong>superseded by <a href="decisions/0049-single-channel-typed-conformance-observable.html">ADR-0049</a></strong>. The four tracing-sourced events are promoted to typed <code>RunEvent</code> variants and conformance now sources from <code>run_ir_streaming</code> alone, so a <code>no_std</code> wasm guest can emit the full stream. The <code>ConformanceEvent</code> output contract</p> <ul> <li>golden file (defined here) are unchanged.</li> </ul> </blockquote> <h2 id="context-51"><a class="header" href="#context-51">Context</a></h2> <p>β.6 adds the conformance gate: the canonical fan-monitor scenario must produce a bit-identical, ordered event stream across execution profiles (interpreted dev vs compiled wasm), the behavioral sibling of <code>verify --bundle</code>'s byte-level check. This phase ships the scaffolding (dev profile live; wasm profile stubbed pending β.7.5).</p> <p>Three forces shaped the contract:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong>The ROADMAP's "EXPECTED EVENT STREAM" is not a real channel.</strong> Its names (<code>RunStarted</code>, <code>ContextStepRan</code>, <code>InferenceCall*</code>, <code>ToolCall*</code>, <code>RunCompleted</code>) are a conceptual union. The actual <code>RunEvent</code> enum has 6 variants and lacks context steps and run/ inference lifecycle marks; the tracing-event stream has those but lacks tool args and success-path tool results (<code>dispatch.tool_resolved</code> logs <code>tool_name</code> only; <code>message.added</code> logs <code>role</code> only).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The gate must survive incidental observability churn.</strong> Binding the diff directly to raw tracing fields would break the gate whenever an unrelated log line or field is added.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>The wasm profile (β.7.5) must reproduce whatever we pick.</strong> The contract has to be something a wasm guest can emit across the component boundary, ideally an artifact we own rather than tracing internals.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-40"><a class="header" href="#decision-40">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>Define a small, versioned, crate-owned <code>ConformanceEvent</code> model</strong>, and source it from <strong>both</strong> the <code>RunEvent</code> enum and the tracing stream — each event kind from exactly one channel.</p> <ul> <li><code>RunStarted</code>, <code>ContextStepRan</code>, <code>InferenceCallStarted</code>, <code>InferenceCallCompleted</code> ← tracing vocabulary events.</li> <li><code>ToolCallStarted</code>, <code>ToolCallCompleted</code>, <code>RunCompleted</code> ← <code>RunEvent</code> enum (the only channel carrying tool args + results).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Interleave the two channels at the engine generator's yield barrier.</strong> The dev profile drives the engine generator (<code>run_ir_streaming</code>, a new thin entry in <code>tau-runtime-core::interpreter</code>) with a <code>Captor</code> tracing layer installed. Because the executor is single-threaded (<code>current_ thread</code>, required since <code>run_ir</code> is non-<code>Send</code>), all tracing emitted between two <code>yield</code>s belongs to that step; the interleaving is causal by construction, with no timestamps or heuristics.</p> <p><strong>Normalization (the canonical comparison).</strong> Modulo (stripped/ canonicalized): timestamps, <code>run_id</code>, <code>agent_id</code> (ULID), provider tool-call ids (→ first-seen ordinals so the started/completed pair correlates). Compared: event kind + ordering, tool name + args + result, context step name + <code>tokens_in</code>/<code>tokens_out</code>, inference <code>stop_reason</code> + token usage, run outcome. <strong>Token counts are compared, not modulo</strong> — deterministic under a cassette LLM + Pure transformers + a deterministic estimator, and comparing them is what makes context-pipeline agreement meaningful. The model carries <code>CONFORMANCE_EVENT_VERSION</code>, recorded in the golden file.</p> <p><strong>Crate shape.</strong> New <code>tau-conformance</code> crate (<code>publish = false</code>), no dependency on <code>tau-ir-conformance</code> (different axis: cross-<em>profile</em> ordered stream vs cross-<em>mode</em> multiset; and it needs a streaming driver the older crate lacks). Two assertions: <code>(a) dev == golden</code> (live this phase), <code>(b) dev == wasm</code> (<code>#[ignore]</code> until β.7.5). The dev arm runs in Tier 1 CI as <code>conformance (linux)</code>.</p> <h2 id="consequences-45"><a class="header" href="#consequences-45">Consequences</a></h2> <p>Positive:</p> <ul> <li>A stable, owned comparison contract decoupled from incidental tracing fields; β.7.5 only has to <em>produce</em> the stream from the wasm guest, not <em>design</em> it.</li> <li>The yield-barrier interleave is provably causal — no flaky timestamp-based ordering, directly mitigating the ROADMAP's "conformance gate flakiness" risk.</li> <li>Context-pipeline behavior (the β.4 transformers) is a first-class part of the gate, not proven separately.</li> </ul> <p>Negative / obligations:</p> <ul> <li>Adds <code>run_ir_streaming</code> to <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (justified independently; mirrors <code>run_agent</code> construction to avoid drift).</li> <li><code>SequencedLlm</code> is duplicated from <code>tau-ir-conformance</code> (~30 lines) rather than coupling the crates; a third consumer triggers extraction of <code>tau-conformance-support</code> (rule of three).</li> <li>Two conformance crates now exist on different axes; the distinction must stay documented to avoid confusion.</li> <li>The wasm arm is dead-stubbed (<code>unimplemented!</code>) and <code>#[ignore]</code>d until β.7.5; the full β.6 DoD is not met until that unstub. Tracked here and in the ROADMAP β.6 entry.</li> </ul> <p>Neutral:</p> <ul> <li>A golden file (<code>expected_events.json</code>) with a bless workflow (<code>TAU_CONFORMANCE_BLESS=1</code>) becomes part of the review surface.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-37"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-37">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Bind the gate to the <code>RunEvent</code> enum only.</strong> Rejected: the enum cannot see <code>ContextStepRan</code>, so the fan-monitor's context pipeline (the β.4 deliverable the scenario is built to exercise) would be invisible to the gate. Trade-off: simpler single-channel capture, but the gate would fail to prove the thing it most needs to prove.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Bind the gate to the raw tracing stream only.</strong> Rejected on two counts: tracing carries neither tool args nor success-path tool results (so <code>set_fan{on:true}</code> / <code>read_temp→32</code> — the scenario's decision logic — would be unverifiable), and coupling to free-form tracing fields makes the gate brittle to unrelated log changes.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Enrich tracing so a single channel suffices</strong> (add args/result fields to dispatch events). Rejected for this phase: a broader change to the hot run path for a conformance-only need, when the yield-barrier interleave gets causal ordering from two channels at zero run-path cost.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Merge the two channels by timestamp / sequence number.</strong> Rejected: reintroduces exactly the timing-nondeterminism flakiness the ROADMAP warns about; the generator yield barrier gives deterministic causal order for free.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Extend <code>tau-ir-conformance</code> instead of a new crate.</strong> Rejected: it asserts cross-<em>mode</em> multiset equivalence via the batch <code>run_ir</code> path; β.6 needs cross-<em>profile</em> <em>ordered</em> streams via a streaming driver. The axes and drivers differ; a new crate keeps each focused.</p> </li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0049-single-channel-typed-conformance-observable"><a class="header" href="#adr-0049-single-channel-typed-conformance-observable">ADR-0049: single-channel typed conformance observable</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-16 <strong>Deciders:</strong> Titouan (architect), implementing session <strong>Supersedes:</strong> ADR-0048 Decision 1 (dual-channel <code>ConformanceEvent</code> sourcing)</p> <h2 id="context-52"><a class="header" href="#context-52">Context</a></h2> <p>ADR-0048 defined the β.6 cross-target conformance gate around a small, crate-owned <code>ConformanceEvent</code> model, and sourced it from <strong>two</strong> channels (Decision 1 of that ADR):</p> <ul> <li><code>ToolCallStarted</code>, <code>ToolCallCompleted</code>, <code>RunCompleted</code> ← the typed <code>RunEvent</code> enum yielded by <code>run_ir_streaming</code>.</li> <li><code>RunStarted</code>, <code>ContextStepRan</code>, <code>InferenceCallStarted</code>, <code>InferenceCallCompleted</code> ← a std <code>tracing</code> <code>Captor</code> layer that string-parses log lines (<code>map_tracing</code>), interleaved with the typed stream at the generator's yield barrier.</li> </ul> <p>That dual-channel design was sound for the <strong>dev</strong> profile, where a std <code>tracing</code> subscriber is always available. β.7.5 then revealed the hole: the gate's whole purpose is <strong>cross-profile</strong> parity (interpreted dev vs compiled wasm), and a <code>no_std</code> <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> guest <strong>cannot run the std <code>tracing</code> subscriber</strong>. The four tracing-sourced event kinds would therefore be unreproducible from inside the wasm artifact — the wasm arm of the gate (<code>fan_monitor_dev_matches_wasm</code>, <code>#[ignore]</code>'d pending β.7.5) could never go live as designed.</p> <p>The forces:</p> <ol> <li><strong>The gate must be emittable from a <code>no_std</code> guest.</strong> Whatever the wasm artifact exports across the WIT component boundary has to carry every event kind the gate compares, with no host-side subscriber in the loop.</li> <li><strong>No logging regression.</strong> The tracing events exist for real observability (OTLP, structured logs); they must keep firing.</li> <li><strong>Don't churn the frozen contract.</strong> ADR-0048 froze the <code>ConformanceEvent</code> output model + <code>CONFORMANCE_EVENT_VERSION</code> + the golden file. β.6 already shipped against them. Changing the <em>sourcing</em> must not change the <em>output</em>.</li> </ol> <p>ADR-0048 anticipated this: it noted the wasm profile "must reproduce whatever we pick" and that the chosen contract should be "an artifact we own rather than tracing internals." Single-channel sourcing is the resolution of that foresight, now that the wasm boundary is concrete.</p> <h2 id="decision-41"><a class="header" href="#decision-41">Decision</a></h2> <p><strong>Promote the four tracing-only gate events to typed <code>RunEvent</code> variants</strong>, and source <code>ConformanceEvent</code> from <strong><code>run_ir_streaming</code> alone</strong> — one typed channel, in both the dev and wasm profiles.</p> <p>New <code>RunEvent</code> variants (emitted by <code>run_ir_streaming</code> directly):</p> <pre><pre class="playground"><code class="language-rust"><span class="boring">#![allow(unused)] </span><span class="boring">fn main() { </span>RunStarted, ContextStepRan { step, tokens_in, tokens_out }, InferenceCallStarted, InferenceCallCompleted { stop_reason, tokens_in, tokens_out }, <span class="boring">}</span></code></pre></pre> <p>(joining the existing <code>ToolCallStarted</code> / <code>ToolCallCompleted</code> / <code>RunCompleted</code>.)</p> <p>Consequently:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>tau-conformance</code> maps <code>ConformanceEvent</code> from the typed <code>RunEvent</code> stream only.</strong> The std <code>Captor</code> tracing layer, the <code>map_tracing</code> translation, and the yield-barrier dual-channel <strong>interleave are deleted</strong>.</li> <li><strong>Tracing events stay for logging.</strong> The same call sites still emit their <code>tracing</code> events; conformance simply stops re-parsing them. There is no logging or OTLP regression.</li> <li><strong>The frozen output contract is unchanged.</strong> The <code>ConformanceEvent</code> model, its version, and the golden <code>expected_events.json</code> are byte-for-byte the same; only where the events come from changes. <code>dev == golden</code> keeps passing without a re-bless.</li> <li><strong>The wasm guest exports the typed stream.</strong> β.7.5's WIT <code>run</code> export returns the serialized typed <code>RunEvent</code> stream; the gate's <code>dev == wasm</code> arm (<code>fan_monitor_dev_matches_wasm</code>) goes live in β.7.5 PR-G with no host-side subscriber.</li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-46"><a class="header" href="#consequences-46">Consequences</a></h2> <p>Positive:</p> <ul> <li>The conformance stream is now fully reproducible from a <code>no_std</code> wasm guest — the β.6 / Phase-β capstone (<code>dev == wasm</code>) is unblocked.</li> <li>One sourcing path instead of two: no yield-barrier interleave to reason about, no causal-ordering argument tied to the single-threaded executor, no string-parsing of free-form tracing fields.</li> <li>The gate is decoupled from <code>tracing</code> entirely; incidental log churn can no longer perturb conformance (a goal ADR-0048 pursued via the owned model; this completes it at the source).</li> </ul> <p>Negative / obligations:</p> <ul> <li><code>RunEvent</code> (in <code>tau-runtime-core</code>) grows four variants — a typed-API surface change. <code>run_ir_streaming</code> must emit them at the same points the tracing events fire, with the same field payloads, or dev/wasm parity silently drifts. A drift test pins the two emission sites together.</li> <li>The deleted <code>Captor</code> / <code>map_tracing</code> code path removes the only consumer that proved the tracing-vs-typed correspondence; that correspondence is no longer asserted (it no longer needs to be, since there is one channel).</li> </ul> <p>Neutral:</p> <ul> <li>ADR-0048's golden-file bless workflow (<code>TAU_CONFORMANCE_BLESS=1</code>) is retained unchanged.</li> <li>Recorded in the β.7.5 design spec (§5 WIT world, §10 conformance integration, §14 ADRs) and the ROADMAP β.7.5 status line.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-38"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-38">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Keep dual-channel; run a <code>no_std</code> tracing subscriber in the guest.</strong> Rejected: <code>tracing-subscriber</code> is std-only and string-formats records; a bespoke <code>no_std</code> re-implementation in the guest would be a large, parity-fragile surface whose entire output we'd then have to match against the host's — exactly the brittleness ADR-0048 wanted to avoid.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Emit <code>ConformanceEvent</code>s directly from the engine</strong> (skip <code>RunEvent</code>). Rejected: <code>ConformanceEvent</code> is a conformance-crate concept; making <code>tau-runtime-core</code> depend on it inverts the dependency direction and bakes a test artifact into the kernel. The typed <code>RunEvent</code> enum is the kernel's own vocabulary and already crosses the WIT boundary.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Leave the four events tracing-only and exclude them from the wasm arm.</strong> Rejected: <code>ContextStepRan</code> carries the β.4 context-pipeline token deltas — the precise behavior the canonical scenario exists to prove. Dropping it from the wasm comparison would make the cross-profile gate blind to the thing it most needs to verify (the same objection ADR-0048 raised against the <code>RunEvent</code>-only alternative, now in the opposite direction).</p> </li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0050-agent-output_schema--additive-field-plumbing-ir-v130"><a class="header" href="#adr-0050-agent-output_schema--additive-field-plumbing-ir-v130">ADR-0050: Agent <code>output_schema</code> — additive field plumbing (IR v1.3.0)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-16 <strong>Deciders:</strong> Titouan (architect), implementing session</p> <h2 id="context-53"><a class="header" href="#context-53">Context</a></h2> <p>Deterministic steps already carry an <code>output_schema: Option<serde_json::Value></code> field (introduced in the deliverables-and-goals track). Agents did not.</p> <p>A downstream judge-compatibility check — planned for a later task — needs to cross-reference a deliverable's judge agent against a declared output schema: the judge must produce output that conforms to the schema the deliverable expects. Without an <code>output_schema</code> field on the agent, that check has no schema to compare against; the check would be forced to defer to runtime, which conflicts with tau's Rust-like build-time enforcement principle (any check that <em>could</em> run at build time <em>must</em> run at build time).</p> <p>This ADR records only the additive field plumbing — not the downstream judge-compatibility check itself.</p> <h2 id="decision-42"><a class="header" href="#decision-42">Decision</a></h2> <p>Add <code>output_schema: Option<serde_json::Value></code> to three layers, mirroring the existing <code>[steps.*].output_schema</code> pattern:</p> <ol> <li> <p><strong><code>tau-pkg</code></strong> — <code>UncheckedAgent</code> / <code>AgentEntry</code>: a new optional TOML key <code>output_schema</code>, deserialized as a raw JSON-compatible value. No deep JSON-schema validation at this layer; the field is stored verbatim.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>tau-ir</code> IR node</strong> — <code>Agent</code>: a new optional field <code>output_schema: Option<serde_json::Value></code> gated with <code>#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]</code>. The lowering stage (<code>lower_project</code>) threads the value from <code>AgentEntry</code> into the IR node with no transformation. The IR format version is bumped <code>v1.2.0 → v1.3.0</code> — a MINOR/additive bump per the ADR-0006 / <code>module.rs</code> semver discipline (MAJOR = breaking, MINOR = additive optional field, PATCH = spec-only). A v1.2.0 reader ignores the absent-when-<code>None</code> key; a v1.3.0 reader handles both. All pre-existing conformance fixtures' canonical bytes are unchanged (verified by the full <code>tau-ir-conformance</code> suite, which runs fixtures 01–14 after this change with 28/28 passing).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>tau-ts-extract</code></strong> — <code>outputSchema</code> extraction: static AST analysis of <code>.ts</code> project files extracts the <code>outputSchema</code> field from agent declaration objects and includes it in the extracted <code>UncheckedAgent</code>, matching the TOML surface.</p> </li> </ol> <p>All three layers are pass-through — no deep validation, no runtime behavior change.</p> <h2 id="consequences-47"><a class="header" href="#consequences-47">Consequences</a></h2> <p><strong>Positive:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Unblocks the downstream judge-compatibility build-time check without requiring another round of field-plumbing at that point.</li> <li>Consistent surface: TOML, IR, and TS authoring now all carry <code>output_schema</code> on both steps and agents.</li> <li>IR version bump is MINOR/additive, so existing bundles (v1.2.0) continue to load correctly in a v1.3.0 reader with no migration.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Neutral / obligations:</strong></p> <ul> <li><code>tau_ir::node::Agent</code> <strong>keeps its <code>Eq</code> derive</strong> — <code>serde_json::Value</code> implements <code>Eq</code>, so <code>Option<serde_json::Value></code> does not force dropping <code>Eq</code>. No public-API regression.</li> <li>The field is inert at runtime until the downstream judge-compat task consumes it. Tests confirm it round-trips but do not assert on its semantic effect (there is none yet).</li> <li>Conformance fixture 14 (<code>14_agent_output_schema</code>) is the acceptance test: it mirrors fixture 01 (agent + one native tool, two turns) with an <code>output_schema</code> added to the agent, and asserts DevMode + BundleMode cross-mode equivalence, proving the schema survives the canonical encode/decode cycle unchanged.</li> </ul> <p><strong>No negative consequences identified.</strong></p> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-39"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-39">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Validate the JSON schema value at parse time</strong> (e.g., check that it is a valid JSON Schema object). Rejected for this phase: validation adds a <code>jsonschema</code> / <code>boon</code> dependency at the <code>tau-pkg</code> parse layer and introduces a new error variant consumers must handle. The downstream judge-compat check will know exactly what shape it requires; general schema validation is deferred until that check is specified. Mirroring the existing step <code>output_schema</code> precedent (which is also unvalidated at parse time) keeps the two surfaces consistent.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Represent <code>output_schema</code> as a typed <code>JsonSchema</code> struct rather than <code>serde_json::Value</code></strong>. Rejected: no agreed-upon schema-validation AST exists in the codebase today, and defining one is out of scope for an additive field that is currently inert. <code>serde_json::Value</code> is the existing convention for unvalidated JSON blobs at this layer (see <code>[steps.*].output_schema</code>).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Defer the field entirely until the judge-compat task is specified</strong>. Rejected: the judge-compat task explicitly needs this field to be already present in the TOML surface, IR, and TS surface — adding it mid-spec would widen that PR unnecessarily. The field is small, additive, and its plumbing is independently testable (fixture 14).</p> </li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0051--tau-ir-crate-split-a-structural-no_std-boundary"><a class="header" href="#adr-0051--tau-ir-crate-split-a-structural-no_std-boundary">ADR-0051 — tau-ir crate split: a structural no_std boundary</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted (β.7.5) <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-16 <strong>Supersedes / amends:</strong> none. Complements ADR-0046 (wasm AOT).</p> <h2 id="context-54"><a class="header" href="#context-54">Context</a></h2> <p>β.7.5 requires <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (the executor-agnostic kernel) to cross-compile to <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> so it can run inside the wasm guest. <code>tau-runtime-core</code> declares <code>#![no_std]</code>, but it never actually built for a no_std target — no CI lane exercised it — and had drifted.</p> <p>Two leaks of <code>tau-pkg</code> (→ <code>tokio</code>, <code>fs4</code> → <code>rustix 0.38.44</code>, which uses <code>feature(wasip2)</code> rejected on stable, plus tokio's <code>compile_error!</code> on wasm) reached the kernel:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Direct</strong> — <code>tau-runtime-core</code> depended on <code>tau-pkg</code> for skill resolution. Removed by the <code>SkillResolver</code> port (PR-A): skill resolution is now a <code>tau-ports</code> port with a host-side <code>TauPkgSkillResolver</code> adapter, mirroring <code>CapabilityResolver</code>.</li> <li><strong>Transitive</strong> — <code>tau-pkg → tau-ir → tau-runtime-core</code>. <code>tau-ir</code>'s <strong>default</strong> feature <code>with-std-adapters</code> gated a <code>lower</code> module that depends on <code>tau-pkg</code>. Member-level <code>default-features = false</code> on the inherited workspace dep did <strong>not</strong> reliably suppress it (feature unification), and <code>tau-ir</code> could not compile <code>--no-default-features</code> at all (<code>IrError::McpBuild</code> referenced the gated <code>lower</code> module unconditionally).</li> </ol> <h2 id="decision-43"><a class="header" href="#decision-43">Decision</a></h2> <p>Split <code>tau-ir</code> along a <strong>crate boundary</strong>, not a feature flag:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>tau-ir</code></strong> — pure <code>#![no_std] + alloc</code>. IR types, <code>check</code>, <code>context</code>, <code>pipeline</code>, <code>template</code>, <code>canonical</code>/<code>hash</code>, <code>message</code> (std adapters behind an opt-in, <strong>non-default</strong> <code>with-std-adapters</code> that no longer pulls <code>tau-pkg</code>). Builds for <code>wasm32-wasip2</code>.</li> <li><strong><code>tau-ir-lower</code></strong> — std-side. The <code>lower</code> pass (<code>tau_pkg::ProjectConfig → IrModule</code>) and its <code>LowerError</code>. Linked by <code>tau-cli</code>, <code>tau-pkg</code>, <code>tau-conformance</code>, <code>tau-ir-conformance</code>, <code>tau-ts-extract</code>.</li> </ul> <p><code>tau-runtime-core</code> depends only on pure <code>tau-ir</code> (default-features off) and now cross-compiles to <code>wasm32-wasip2</code>.</p> <p><strong>Why a crate boundary, not a feature flag:</strong> a feature is an interface the build resolver can silently violate — exactly what happened with <code>default-features = false</code> under unification. A crate boundary is one it cannot. The kernel's std-freedom must be <em>structural</em>, matching tau's "any check that could run at build time must run at build time" discipline. A CI guard (<code>runtime-core-no-std</code> job) builds <code>tau-runtime-core</code> for <code>wasm32-wasip2</code> so the boundary cannot re-drift.</p> <h2 id="consequences-48"><a class="header" href="#consequences-48">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>The kernel is genuinely substrate-agnostic — the precondition for the β.6 "one engine, N profiles" conformance claim.</li> <li><code>IrError</code> stays in <code>tau-ir</code> (the pure <code>check</code> pass raises most of its variants); only the lowering-specific <code>McpBuild</code> variant moved to <code>tau-ir-lower::LowerError</code>.</li> <li>Consumers of lowering import <code>tau-ir-lower</code> instead of <code>tau_ir::lower</code>.</li> <li>One more workspace crate (38 members).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0052-per-agent--per-judge-model-resolution"><a class="header" href="#adr-0052-per-agent--per-judge-model-resolution">ADR-0052: Per-agent / per-judge model resolution</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-19 <strong>Deciders:</strong> tau core</p> <h2 id="context-55"><a class="header" href="#context-55">Context</a></h2> <p><code>Agent.model</code> and a deliverable's <code>judge_model</code> were parsed, validated, and traced — but <strong>ignored at runtime</strong>. On the IR-interpreter path (<code>tau run --bundle</code>, <code>tau dev</code>) every agent ran on a single ambient backend:</p> <ul> <li><code>prepare_agent_run</code> called the arg-less <code>dispatcher.llm_backend()</code>, took <code>backend.name()</code>, and baked it into a synthesized <code>AgentDefinition</code>. The agent's declared backend was never consulted.</li> <li><code>ir::Agent.model</code> was never read.</li> <li><code>stream.rs</code> built <code>CompletionRequest::new(agent_def.llm_backend.as_str())</code>, so the request's <code>model</code> field received the <strong>backend package name</strong> (<code>"anthropic"</code>), not a vendor model id (<code>"claude-haiku-4-5"</code>).</li> </ul> <p>So "per-agent model" did not exist on this path — neither the model nor the backend selection. The builtin deliverable judge inherited the same limitation: <code>judge_model</code> was a documented v1 no-op (ADR-0044, Decision 6).</p> <p>tau's guiding principle is that any check that <em>can</em> run at build time <em>must</em> run at build time ("tau is a compiler"). Model selection is exactly such a check: the alias → concrete pair mapping is fully knowable offline.</p> <h2 id="decision-44"><a class="header" href="#decision-44">Decision</a></h2> <p>A declared <code>[models]</code> table maps an author alias to a concrete <code>{ backend, model }</code> pair. Lowering resolves every <code>agent.model</code> / <code>judge_model</code> alias into a <code>ModelRef { backend, model_id }</code> baked into the IR. The dispatcher becomes multi-backend; the synthesized <code>AgentDefinition</code> carries the resolved vendor model id so the <code>CompletionRequest</code> gets a real model string. The builtin judge becomes the implicit <code>JudgeRef::Default</code>, defaulting to its producer agent's model.</p> <pre><code class="language-toml">[models] haiku = { backend = "anthropic", model = "claude-haiku-4-5" } opus = { backend = "anthropic", model = "claude-opus-4-8" } [agents.writer] model = "haiku" # no llm_backend; backend derived from [models] [deliverables.report] must_satisfy = "ships a passing test suite" judge_model = "opus" # optional; resolves through the same [models] table </code></pre> <p>The seven sub-decisions:</p> <ul> <li><strong>D1 — Mapping mechanism: an explicit <code>[models]</code> table.</strong> Chosen over (B) backends self-advertising model lists and (C) opaque agent-config passthrough because it is the only option fully checkable at build time.</li> <li><strong>D2 — Resolution at lowering; the IR carries the concrete pair.</strong> The alias is resolved during lowering; the compiled IR carries the resolved <code>{ backend, model_id }</code>, never the alias. The bundle is self-describing and reproducible; the runtime performs zero alias logic.</li> <li><strong>D3 — Schema 1: the alias is the single knob.</strong> <code>[models]</code> is the single source of truth for both backend and model. The per-agent <code>llm_backend</code> field is <strong>removed</strong> (hard cutover — in this repo it was fixtures-only). There is no "alias or literal" duality: a literal escape hatch, if ever needed, is just another <code>[models]</code> entry.</li> <li><strong>D4 — Multi-backend dispatcher; <code>AgentDefinition</code> gains <code>model</code>.</strong> The <code>ToolDispatcher</code> trait method <code>llm_backend(&self) -> Arc<dyn DynLlmBackend></code> is replaced by <code>llm_backend_for(&self, backend: &str) -> Result<Arc<dyn DynLlmBackend>, RuntimeError></code>. <code>prepare_agent_run</code> reads <code>agent.model_ref</code>, resolves the backend by name, and bakes <code>model_id</code> into the synthesized <code>AgentDefinition</code>; <code>stream.rs</code> reads <code>agent_def.model</code>. The host <code>ForwardingDispatcher</code> holds the whole name-keyed registry and selects by name; single-backend test/conformance dispatchers return their one backend. The dispatcher stays policy-free: name → backend object; all policy happened at lowering.</li> <li><strong>D5 — The judge rides the agent machinery; <code>JudgeRef::Default</code>.</strong> The deliverable judge is already an <code>Agent</code> run through the same loop. The variant <code>JudgeRef::Builtin</code> is renamed <code>JudgeRef::Default { model_ref }</code> (the word "builtin" leaves the user surface). When a deliverable uses the canonical judge and omits <code>judge_model</code>, the judge resolves to its <strong>producer agent's</strong> <code>model_ref</code> (the producer is already resolved at build time). An explicit <code>judge_model</code> overrides it. A user <code>[agents.*]</code> named as judge clones that agent's own <code>model_ref</code> with zero judge-specific work.</li> <li><strong>D6 — Agents must declare <code>model</code>.</strong> Under Schema 1 there is no per-agent backend fallback and no sensible local default, so an agent that omits <code>model</code> is a build error (<code>MissingAgentModel</code>). A reserved-<code>default</code>-alias convention can be added later, additively.</li> <li><strong>D7 — Build-time validation, three stages with a guarantee gradient:</strong> <ul> <li><strong>Stage 1 — <code>tau build</code> (offline, <code>validate_models</code> in tau-pkg).</strong> Each <code>[models]</code> entry must have a non-empty <code>backend</code>+<code>model</code> (<code>MalformedModelEntry</code>) and a backend that is a declared package (<code>ModelBackendNotDeclared</code>); every agent must declare a <code>model</code> (<code>MissingAgentModel</code>) that resolves (<code>UnknownModelAlias</code>); a deliverable's <code>judge_model</code>, when present, must resolve. On pass, <code>{ backend, model_id }</code> is baked into <code>ir::Agent.model_ref</code> and <code>JudgeRef::Default</code>.</li> <li><strong>Stage 2 — <code>tau check</code> (probes plugins).</strong> For each backend referenced by <code>[models]</code>, the installed package must expose LLM completion (declare <code>provides = "llm_backend"</code>), else the <code>tau.models.backend_not_llm_capable</code> finding fires. This is a diagnostic finding, not an escape hatch.</li> <li><strong>Stage 3 — runtime.</strong> Resolve the backend by <code>model_ref.backend</code>; set <code>request.model = model_ref.model_id</code>; call <code>backend.complete(request)</code>.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-49"><a class="header" href="#consequences-49">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Per-agent and per-judge model selection is <strong>real</strong> on the IR-interpreter path. This <strong>closes the <code>judge_model</code> runtime no-op</strong> honest limit recorded in ADR-0044 (Decision 6).</li> <li><strong>IR format version: MAJOR bump v1.2.0 → v2.0.0.</strong> Changing <code>ir::Agent</code>'s <code>model: String</code> field to <code>model_ref: ModelRef</code> and renaming the <code>JudgeRef</code> variant are breaking shape changes per the semver rules in <code>crates/tau-ir/src/module.rs</code>. A drift test in <code>tau-ir</code> and the <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> IR-format mirror assert v2.0.0.</li> <li>New error variants on <code>ProjectConfigError</code>: <code>MalformedModelEntry</code>, <code>ModelBackendNotDeclared</code>, <code>UnknownModelAlias</code>, <code>MissingAgentModel</code> (<code>UnknownJudgeAgent</code> already existed).</li> <li>TypeScript authoring parity: <code>tau-ts-extract</code> gains a <code>models({...})</code> factory and a per-agent <code>model</code> alias; it infers the top-level <code>packages</code> set from the <code>[models]</code> backends (a bare key that never enters the IR, so TOML↔TS byte-equality is preserved). A multi-alias TOML↔TS conformance fixture proves it.</li> <li>Conformance: a <code>14_models_multi</code> fixture exercises a <code>[models]</code> table with two aliases on one backend, two agents on different models, one deliverable whose judge inherits its producer and one with an explicit <code>judge_model</code> override.</li> <li><strong>Honest limit (trusted vendor string).</strong> The vendor model id itself (e.g. <code>"claude-haiku-4-5"</code>) is <strong>trusted, never validated offline</strong> — a provider's catalog cannot be checked at build time. A correct-shape-but-wrong vendor string surfaces as a runtime provider error (Stage 3), not a build refusal.</li> </ul> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-40"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-40">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>(B) Backends self-advertise model lists.</strong> Rejected: a backend's model catalog is only knowable by probing the live provider, so it cannot gate <code>tau build</code> offline — it would push model validation to runtime, violating the build-time-enforcement principle.</li> <li><strong>(C) Opaque per-agent config passthrough</strong> (model string in <code>[agents.<id>.config]</code>). Rejected: the build has no way to distinguish a model selector from arbitrary plugin config, so neither the backend nor the model can be resolved or validated at lowering.</li> <li><strong>Keep <code>llm_backend</code> alongside <code>model</code></strong> (alias-or-literal duality). Rejected: two knobs for one selection invites drift (an agent could name a backend that disagrees with its model's backend) and doubles the validation surface; a single alias into <code>[models]</code> is the one source of truth.</li> <li><strong>A project-level default judge model.</strong> Rejected in favour of inheriting the producer agent's model (Q4): the producer is already build-time resolved and is the most relevant local default, with no new global config.</li> <li><strong>Reserved <code>default</code> agent-model alias</strong> (so agents may omit <code>model</code>). Deferred, not rejected: it is purely additive and can land later without a format change. For now, omitting <code>model</code> is a build error (D6).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="adr-0053-opt-in-turn-level-checkpointresume-durable-execution-a-minimal"><a class="header" href="#adr-0053-opt-in-turn-level-checkpointresume-durable-execution-a-minimal">ADR-0053: Opt-in turn-level checkpoint/resume (durable execution A-minimal)</a></h1> <p><strong>Status:</strong> Accepted <strong>Date:</strong> 2026-06-20 <strong>Deciders:</strong> tau core</p> <h2 id="context-56"><a class="header" href="#context-56">Context</a></h2> <p>tau's only durability surface was run-end-only: <code>RunSnapshot</code> (<code>tau-ports/src/orchestration.rs</code>) captures aggregate accounting when a run finishes. A crash at turn 9 of a 12-turn agent loop restarts at turn 1 and re-bills 8 completed LLM calls.</p> <p>Phase B (shipped — <code>docs/how-to/run-tau-under-a-durable-orchestrator.md</code>, ROADMAP NG5) made the <em>whole bundle</em> a safe-to-retry reentrant unit, so a host orchestrator (Temporal / Inngest / Cloudflare Workflows) owns durability across bundle invocations. But durability under Phase B is whole-bundle: an expensive multi-turn loop <em>inside</em> one bundle is opaque to the orchestrator and re-runs from the top on retry.</p> <p>A-minimal closes that intra-bundle gap with opt-in per-turn checkpoint/resume, while staying inside NG5 (tau is not a general-purpose workflow engine) and NG6 (no built-in DB). It deliberately avoids event-sourced replay (Phase A-full), which carries a permanent engine-determinism tax and is gated until a concrete workflow needs exactly-once.</p> <p>The substrate already supports this cheaply: β.1 put every nondeterminism source behind a port, and β.4's context pipeline is <em>stateless</em> (transformers re-apply to the message history each turn, accumulating nothing). So the resumable state is just the message history + token accounting + turn number — all already serde-derived.</p> <h2 id="decision-45"><a class="header" href="#decision-45">Decision</a></h2> <p>A durable agent persists a <code>TurnCheckpoint</code> after each completed turn; <code>tau run --resume <run_id></code> rehydrates the last committed checkpoint and re-enters at the next turn. <strong>No replay</strong> — re-enter at the last committed turn boundary.</p> <p><strong>Semantics: at-least-once for the crashed turn only.</strong> Committed turns never re-run; the single in-flight turn re-runs from its start. Tools under a durable agent <strong>must be idempotent</strong> — a side effect in the crashed turn may fire twice if the crash lands after it but before the checkpoint write. Exactly-once is A-full's job, not A-minimal's.</p> <p>Four sub-decisions:</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>D1 — The checkpoint write lives behind a <code>CheckpointStore</code> port.</strong> A new trait in <code>tau-ports</code> (<code>persist</code> + <code>load_latest</code>). The agent loop in <code>tau-runtime-core</code> (<code>#![no_std]</code>) calls <code>store.persist(&ckpt)</code> after <code>TurnCompleted</code> when the agent is durable; the tokio host supplies a <code>FileCheckpointStore</code>. Mirrors the existing <code>Clock</code> / <code>RandomSource</code> / <code>CapabilityResolver</code> injection. Keeps core I/O-free <em>and</em> lets the kill-and-resume DoD test run in-core against an in-memory <code>MockCheckpointStore</code> with no tokio harness.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>D2 — Ship <code>PerTurn</code> + <code>File</code> only; enums <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code>.</strong> <code>CheckpointGranularity::PerToolCall</code> requires mid-turn (partial-turn) rehydration — a harder state machine that leaks turn internals into the checkpoint format — and only <em>narrows</em>, never closes, the at-least-once window, so it is deferred. <code>DurableStore::Kv</code> is an MCP-contracted journal (NG6) and belongs to A-full. Both land later as additive minor bumps, exactly as <code>output_schema</code> did (IR v1.3.0).</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>D3 — Per-turn snapshot files, keep-all, atomic-rename.</strong> <code>.tau/runs/<run_id>/turn-<n>.json</code>, each the full history at turn <em>n</em>; resume reads the highest <em>n</em>. Write is <code>*.tmp</code> → atomic rename, so a crash mid-write leaves <code>turn-<n-1>.json</code> intact — the resume point, which is the promised at-least-once boundary. A single appended JSONL was rejected: a torn final line is a parsing problem, and full-history rehydration gets no storage win from JSONL without delta complexity A-minimal exists to avoid.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>D4 — Drop the handoff's <code>context_state</code> field.</strong> β.4's context pipeline carries no cross-turn runtime state, so <code>TurnCheckpoint</code> is <code>{ run_id, turn, history: Vec<Message>, tokens: TokenUsage }</code>. Rehydration feeds <code>history</code> back in and the pipeline re-derives deterministically.</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="consequences-50"><a class="header" href="#consequences-50">Consequences</a></h2> <ul> <li>Per-agent durable execution is real on the IR-interpreter path (<code>tau run</code>, <code>tau run --bundle</code>, <code>tau dev</code>). It composes with Phase B: the orchestrator still owns <em>when</em> to retry; A-minimal narrows <em>how much</em> re-runs per retry.</li> <li><strong>IR format version: MINOR bump v2.0.0 → v2.1.0.</strong> <code>Agent</code> gains <code>durable: Option<Durability></code> with <code>#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]</code>. The field is invisible when absent, so a durable-absent module's canonical bytes differ from v2.0.0 <em>only</em> in the version string — the honest signal that the schema grew (same treatment as <code>triggers</code> / <code>checks</code> / <code>context</code>). Drift tests in <code>tau-ir</code> and the <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code> mirror assert v2.1.0.</li> <li>New port surface in <code>tau-ports</code>: <code>TurnCheckpoint</code>, <code>CheckpointStore</code>, <code>CheckpointError</code>. New <code>RunOptions.checkpoint_store: Option<Arc<dyn CheckpointStore>></code> in <code>tau-runtime-core</code>.</li> <li>New host types in <code>tau-runtime-tokio</code>: <code>FileCheckpointStore</code>, <code>NoopCheckpointStore</code>. New CLI flag: <code>tau run --resume <run_id></code>.</li> <li>TypeScript authoring parity: <code>tau-ts-extract</code> carries the <code>durable</code> field; TOML↔TS canonical IR stays byte-equal (conformance fixture).</li> <li>Conformance: a new <code>16_durable_per_turn</code> fixture cross-mode conforms; all existing fixtures stay green (none are durable). Their absolute bundle hashes shift with the version bump — expected on any IR-format change.</li> <li><strong>Honest limit.</strong> At-least-once, not exactly-once. Documented as the idempotency contract; teams needing exactly-once wait for A-full.</li> </ul> <h2 id="follow-on-epic-61--intent-form-durable-knob"><a class="header" href="#follow-on-epic-61--intent-form-durable-knob">Follow-on: EPIC 6.1 — intent-form durable knob</a></h2> <p>EPIC 6.1 (shipped) adds a high-level <strong>intent</strong> spelling for the <code>durable</code> field: <code>durable = "survive-restarts"</code> (TOML) / <code>durable: "survive-restarts"</code> (TS). The intent lowers to <code>Durability::Intent(DurabilityIntent::SurviveRestarts)</code> in the IR; the host resolves it to a concrete granularity + store per target at run/build time, and <code>tau check --target <triple></code> prints the resolved pair. See <code>docs/how-to/run-tau-under-a-durable-orchestrator.md</code> §Opt-in per-agent checkpointing for authoring details.</p> <h2 id="alternatives-considered-41"><a class="header" href="#alternatives-considered-41">Alternatives considered</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Feature-gated I/O inside core</strong> (<code>#[cfg(feature = "host-fs")]</code> write after <code>TurnCompleted</code>) instead of a port. Rejected: it sprinkles <code>cfg</code> branches through the no_std hot path and forces the kill-and-resume test onto a real filesystem + tokio host, where a port lets it run in-core with a mock. The port also matches the established side-effect-injection discipline.</li> <li><strong>Ship <code>PerToolCall</code> now.</strong> Rejected for A-minimal: mid-turn rehydration is materially more complex and buys only a narrower (still unsafe) window, not exactly-once — a half-measure paid for in complexity. Deferred to a follow-up; the <code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> enum makes it additive.</li> <li><strong>Single appended JSONL run log</strong> (reusing workflow v1's shape).
