Native <code>async fn in trait</code> is not dyn-compatible; design accordingly (wrapper traits, <code>trait_variant::make</code>, or commit to monomorphic generics).</li> <li><strong>Are tests at integration-test level vs. unit-test level constrained by <code>pub(crate)</code> visibility?</strong> If yes, the spec should say which level for which test, not leave it to the implementer to discover at write time.</li> </ol> <h3 id="dont-ship-error-variants-without-a-triggering-codepath"><a class="header" href="#dont-ship-error-variants-without-a-triggering-codepath">Don't ship error variants without a triggering codepath</a></h3> <p>Sub-project 4 wired <code>RuntimeError::PluginContractViolation</code> at task 4 but had no v0.1 trigger (the <code>deserialize_tool_args</code> helper is a passthrough). The Task 15 integration test had to be <code>#[ignore]</code>'d.</p> <p>Pattern: don't add error variants speculatively. Either implement the trigger OR defer the variant until the use case is concrete (Phase 1 schema validation, in this case).</p> <h3 id="spec-language-vs-implementation-reality-1"><a class="header" href="#spec-language-vs-implementation-reality-1">Spec language vs. implementation reality</a></h3> <p>Sub-project 4 spec §6 originally said "~45 events across 9 subsystems". Actual implementation emitted ~22 events. The number was a brainstorm estimate that survived into the spec without re-grounding. ADR-0006 records the actual vocabulary; spec-phase numbers should be estimates-with-error-bars, not commitments.</p> <h2 id="implications-for-sub-project-5-tau-cli"><a class="header" href="#implications-for-sub-project-5-tau-cli">Implications for sub-project 5 (tau-cli)</a></h2> <h3 id="exit-code-taxonomy-mirrors-outcome--error"><a class="header" href="#exit-code-taxonomy-mirrors-outcome--error">Exit-code taxonomy mirrors Outcome / Error</a></h3> <pre><code>0 — agent completed successfully (RunOutcome::Completed) 1 — agent failed gracefully (RunOutcome::Failed{PolicyDenied, OutOfResources}) 2 — kernel or CLI broke (Err(RuntimeError) or CLI argument errors) </code></pre> <p>Decide in the brainstorm. The dichotomy maps cleanly.</p> <h3 id="first-end-user-binary"><a class="header" href="#first-end-user-binary">First end-user binary</a></h3> <p>Sub-projects 1-4 produced libraries; <code>tau-cli</code> produces a binary that real users invoke. Different concerns:</p> <ul> <li>stdout vs. stderr discipline (results vs. logs)</li> <li>color / verbose / quiet flag conventions</li> <li>clap subcommand structure</li> <li>config discovery (project root walk-up or <code>$TAU_HOME</code>?)</li> <li><code>tau init</code> semantics per ADR-0004 §6 (print hint, don't mutate <code>.gitignore</code>)</li> <li>handling of binary mode vs. interactive (TUI deferred to Phase 1?)</li> </ul> <h3 id="cross-crate-api-gaps-will-surface"><a class="header" href="#cross-crate-api-gaps-will-surface">Cross-crate API gaps will surface</a></h3> <p>Sub-project 5 is the first time tau-pkg and tau-runtime are exercised end-to-end through a real consumer. Expect at least one missing constructor, one error variant that's reachable but awkward to pattern-match, and one place where the public surface needed a convenience method that wasn't anticipated.</p> <p>Budget for additive amendments to tau-pkg and tau-runtime, each landing as part of the same task that surfaces them, with ADR coverage if the amendment is non-trivial.</p> <h3 id="plan-pre-flight-checklist"><a class="header" href="#plan-pre-flight-checklist">Plan pre-flight checklist</a></h3> <p>Before deriving the plan from the spec, run the three pre-flight checks above (<code>#[non_exhaustive]</code> constructors, dyn-compat, test visibility) and enumerate any gaps as commit-by-commit line items in the plan.</p> <h2 id="whats-not-in-scope-for-this-memo"><a class="header" href="#whats-not-in-scope-for-this-memo">What's NOT in scope for this memo</a></h2> <ul> <li>The formal Phase 0 retrospective (PG4) — happens after sub-project 5 ships, and considers Phase 1 priorities, ADR audit, crate reorganization, etc.</li> <li>Process changes that affect more than the next sub-project — those belong in Constitution amendments via the §4 process.</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="tau-dev-environment--linux-pre-commit-hook--opt-in-deep-gate"><a class="header" href="#tau-dev-environment--linux-pre-commit-hook--opt-in-deep-gate">tau dev environment — Linux pre-commit hook + opt-in deep gate</a></h1> <p>Goal: catch cross-platform build/runtime issues locally before pushing, so CI is confirmation rather than discovery. Also unblocks local debugging of F task 6.5 follow-ups (strict_net_filter integration test hang, Container-adapter network filtering).</p> <p>This iteration covers <strong>Linux only</strong> (running on Apple Silicon Mac). Windows + macOS legs are deferred to follow-up PRs.</p> <h2 id="tldr--one-time-setup"><a class="header" href="#tldr--one-time-setup">TL;DR — one-time setup</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-bash"># 1. Use rustup, not Homebrew rust (see "Toolchain setup" below if you have Homebrew rust installed). # rustup honors rust-toolchain.toml and auto-provisions cross-targets. # 2. Install tools (FOSS only) brew install lefthook podman brew install filosottile/musl-cross/musl-cross # for cross-compile-check (x86_64 included by default) # 3. Initialize Podman's hidden Linux VM (--rootful required for caps) podman machine init --cpus 4 --memory 8192 --rootful podman machine start # 4. Wire the pre-commit git hook lefthook install # 5. Verify lefthook run pre-commit --all-files # ~30-60s, must exit 0 lefthook run deep-gate --all-files # ~3-5min cold, opt-in pre-flight </code></pre> <p>After this, every <code>git commit</code> runs the fast checks. The deep Linux gate is <strong>opt-in</strong> — it is not a push hook; run <code>lefthook run deep-gate</code> on demand (e.g. before a release tag) when you want a full local pre-flight. CI runs the same Linux jobs on every PR, so CI is the gate.</p> <h2 id="toolchain-setup--rustup-not-homebrew-rust"><a class="header" href="#toolchain-setup--rustup-not-homebrew-rust">Toolchain setup — rustup, not Homebrew rust</a></h2> <p>This project requires the rustup-managed Rust toolchain. <code>rust-toolchain.toml</code> declares the channel, components, and cross-compile targets that rustup auto-provisions.</p> <p><strong>If you have Homebrew rust installed, remove it before installing rustup:</strong></p> <pre><code class="language-bash">which cargo # should be ~/.cargo/bin/cargo # if it shows /opt/homebrew/bin/cargo, fix below brew list rust 2>/dev/null && brew uninstall rust curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh # Restart your shell, or `source ~/.cargo/env`. which cargo # now ~/.cargo/bin/cargo cargo --version # should NOT say "(Homebrew)" </code></pre> <p>If you can't or won't uninstall Homebrew rust, ensure <code>~/.cargo/bin</code> precedes <code>/opt/homebrew/bin</code> in <code>$PATH</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc source ~/.zshrc which cargo # confirm rustup's cargo wins </code></pre> <p>The <code>check-linux-x86</code> pre-commit step requires the musl stdlib for the <code>x86_64-unknown-linux-musl</code> target. Homebrew rust doesn't ship this stdlib; rustup auto-installs it from <code>rust-toolchain.toml</code>'s <code>targets</code> list. Skipping this prerequisite means <code>check-linux-x86</code> will fail with "can't find crate for <code>core</code>".</p> <h2 id="architecture"><a class="header" href="#architecture">Architecture</a></h2> <pre><code>┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Apple Silicon Mac (host) │ │ │ │ git commit ──── lefthook pre-commit ─── ~30-60s (host, no VM) │ │ • cargo fmt --all -- --check │ │ • cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets │ │ • cargo nextest run --workspace --all-targets │ │ • cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl│ │ │ │ lefthook run deep-gate (opt-in) ────── ~3-5min (Linux VM) │ │ │ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ Podman machine (Linux VM, persistent) │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ ephemeral container per deep-gate run: │ │ │ │ podman run --rm │ │ │ │ --cap-add SYS_ADMIN --cap-add NET_ADMIN │ │ │ │ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined │ │ │ │ --security-opt apparmor=unconfined │ │ │ │ -v $WORKSPACE:/workspace │ │ │ │ -v cargo-cache:/usr/local/cargo/registry │ │ │ │ -v target-cache:/workspace/target/lefthook-podman │ │ │ │ rust:1.82-bookworm │ │ │ │ bash -c 'cargo nextest run --workspace --all-targets' │ │ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ </code></pre> <h2 id="interactive-linux-debugging"><a class="header" href="#interactive-linux-debugging">Interactive Linux debugging</a></h2> <p>When you need to investigate a test failure or reproduce a bug interactively (e.g., the strict_net_filter integration test hang from F task 6.5 follow-ups), use the same image and caps as the gate, just with <code>bash</code> instead of <code>cargo nextest</code>:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">podman run -it --rm \ --cap-add SYS_ADMIN --cap-add NET_ADMIN \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \ --security-opt apparmor=unconfined \ -v "$PWD":/workspace:Z \ -v cargo-cache:/usr/local/cargo/registry \ -v target-cache:/workspace/target/lefthook-podman \ -w /workspace \ docker.io/library/rust:1.82-bookworm \ bash </code></pre> <p>Inside the container, <code>apt-get install -y iproute2 nftables</code> then run cargo commands directly. Same kernel, same caps, same crate cache as the automated gate — what fails interactively will fail in the gate, and vice versa.</p> <h2 id="coverage"><a class="header" href="#coverage">Coverage</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-bash">cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked rustup component add llvm-tools-preview cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --no-fail-fast --html </code></pre> <p>Then open <code>target/llvm-cov/html/index.html</code> (or your <code>CARGO_TARGET_DIR</code>-relative equivalent). CI runs the same invocation on every PR and posts the percent + the <code>lcov.info</code> artifact to the workflow summary.</p> <p>Coverage is a signal, not a gate — do not write tests to hit a number.</p> <h2 id="bypassing-the-pre-commit-hook-emergencies-only"><a class="header" href="#bypassing-the-pre-commit-hook-emergencies-only">Bypassing the pre-commit hook (emergencies only)</a></h2> <pre><code class="language-bash">git commit --no-verify # skip pre-commit </code></pre> <p><code>git push</code> runs no hook (the deep gate is opt-in), so nothing to bypass there. Don't skip pre-commit routinely — it exists so CI doesn't have to find the bugs.</p> <h2 id="architecture-mismatch-known-gaps"><a class="header" href="#architecture-mismatch-known-gaps">Architecture mismatch (known gaps)</a></h2> <p>Apple Silicon is arm64; CI Linux runners are x86_64. The local gate will catch:</p> <ul> <li>✅ All cfg-gating bugs (<code>cfg(unix)</code>, <code>cfg(target_os)</code>)</li> <li>✅ All build-time API mismatches (the <code>std::os::fd</code> class)</li> <li>✅ Most Linux runtime regressions (sandbox tests, IPC, syscall behavior on arm64 Linux)</li> <li>✅ Privilege drift (selective-cap regressions)</li> </ul> <p>The local gate will NOT catch:</p> <ul> <li>❌ Arch-specific runtime bugs that only manifest on x86_64 (struct alignment, atomic ordering, syscall numbers in raw asm — landlock syscall numbers differ between x86_64 and arm64 Linux)</li> <li>❌ glibc-version differences (Podman ships current Debian; CI ships Ubuntu)</li> <li>❌ Windows-specific issues (deferred to follow-up PR)</li> <li>❌ macOS-specific issues that require a fresh macOS VM (deferred indefinitely; Mac coverage stays via the host)</li> </ul> <p>These remaining gaps are caught by CI. The deep gate covers ~95% of the cross-platform pain points; CI handles the rest.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"><a class="header" href="#troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a></h2> <p><strong><code>lefthook: command not found</code></strong>: open a new shell after <code>brew install lefthook</code> to pick up <code>$PATH</code> updates.</p> <p><strong><code>check-linux-x86</code> fails with "can't find crate for <code>core</code>"</strong>: Homebrew's <code>cargo</code> is shadowing rustup's shim on <code>$PATH</code>, and Homebrew rust doesn't ship the musl stdlib. Fix: see "Toolchain setup" above. Verify with <code>which cargo</code> — it should show <code>~/.cargo/bin/cargo</code>, not <code>/opt/homebrew/bin/cargo</code>.</p> <p><strong><code>podman machine</code> is non-rootful</strong>: privileged-style containers won't work. Recreate:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">podman machine stop podman machine rm podman machine init --cpus 4 --memory 8192 --rootful podman machine start </code></pre> <p><strong>Deep gate hangs at apt-get</strong>: the container is a fresh Debian — <code>apt-get update</code> reaches Debian mirrors. If you're behind a corporate proxy, configure Podman to use it (<code>podman machine ssh</code> then add proxy env vars to <code>/etc/profile.d/</code>).</p> <p><strong>Deep gate fails with permission denied on a syscall</strong>: a test is using a cap outside the documented list. Either expand the cap list in <code>lefthook.yml</code> (with a justifying comment) or fix the test to not need that cap. Never silently widen to <code>--privileged</code> — that defeats the gate.</p> <p><strong>Pre-commit hook didn't run</strong>: check <code>.git/hooks/pre-commit</code> exists. If not, re-run <code>lefthook install</code>.</p> <p><strong>Cargo target dir collision</strong>: lefthook uses <code>target/lefthook/{fmt,clippy,test,check-linux}</code> and <code>target/lefthook-podman</code>. These don't collide with <code>target/main</code> (main agent) or <code>target/agent-*</code> (sub-agents) per <a href="../CLAUDE.html">CLAUDE.md Rule 1</a>. If you see lock contention, ensure your bare cargo invocations are using the right <code>CARGO_TARGET_DIR</code>.</p> <p><strong>Container-VM disk space fills up</strong>: <code>podman machine</code> defaults are conservative. If you hit "no space left on device", increase the machine disk size:</p> <pre><code class="language-bash">podman machine stop podman machine set --disk-size 100 podman machine start </code></pre> <p><strong>QEMU <code>rustc</code> SIGSEGV during compilation</strong>: the Podman container is running aarch64 Linux natively (not x86_64 emulation), so this shouldn't happen. If you've added <code>--platform linux/amd64</code> somewhere and hit rustc crashes, remove it — Apple Silicon QEMU x86_64 emulation is unstable for rustc workloads.</p> <h2 id="what-this-enables"><a class="header" href="#what-this-enables">What this enables</a></h2> <p>After this PR ships:</p> <ol> <li>F task 6.5 follow-up #2 (strict_net_filter integration test hang) becomes debuggable locally — <code>podman run -it ...</code> reproduces the privileged-Linux environment for interactive <code>gdb</code>/<code>strace</code> work.</li> <li>F task 6.5 follow-up #1 (Container-adapter network filtering) becomes debuggable locally via the same mechanism.</li> <li>The cfg(unix) / cfg(target_os) class of bug is caught at commit time, not CI time.</li> <li>Privilege drift is caught at commit/push time, not silently masked by CI's previous <code>--privileged</code>.</li> </ol> <h2 id="ci-secrets"><a class="header" href="#ci-secrets">CI secrets</a></h2> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>Secret</th><th>Used by</th><th>Scope</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>REPO_FILE_SYNC_TOKEN</code></td><td><code>.github/workflows/sync-template.yml</code></td><td>classic PAT with <code>repo</code> + <code>workflow</code>, or fine-grained with Contents:write + Pull requests:write + Workflows on the three sibling repos</td><td>Lets the CI-template sync open PRs into <code>cairn</code> / <code>cairn-ui</code> / <code>tau-ui</code>. Read with <code>GITHUB_TOKEN</code> only — cross-repo writes need this PAT.</td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p>The sync workflow declares the canonical template surface in <code>.github/sync.yml</code> (see <code>audit/devops.md</code> §3, the anti-drift "B+C" model). Until <code>REPO_FILE_SYNC_TOKEN</code> is configured the workflow fails loudly at the sync step (never silently). Before granting write, run the workflow manually (<code>workflow_dispatch</code>) with <code>dry_run=true</code> (the default) to log the file→repo plan, or run <code>python3 scripts/verify-sync-config.py</code> locally for the same plan.</p> <h2 id="out-of-scope-follow-up-prs"><a class="header" href="#out-of-scope-follow-up-prs">Out of scope (follow-up PRs)</a></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Windows VM (UTM + Windows 11 ARM)</strong> — largest setup; tracked as PR2 candidate.</li> <li><strong>macOS VM (Tart)</strong> — Tart is Fair Source, not OSI FOSS; not pursued.</li> <li><strong>x86_64 Linux runtime via QEMU</strong> — too slow; CI provides x86_64 ground truth.</li> <li><strong>Pre-commit fix mode</strong> — the gate is verify-only (<code>cargo fmt -- --check</code>), not auto-rewrite (<code>cargo fmt</code>).</li> </ul> <div style="break-before: page; page-break-before: always;"></div><h1 id="test-ignore-inventory"><a class="header" href="#test-ignore-inventory">Test Ignore Inventory</a></h1> <p><strong>Refreshed:</strong> 2026-05-17 (supersedes 2026-05-13 inventory from PR #71) <strong>Workspace state:</strong> based on <code>origin/main</code> at <code>bcbac9a</code> <strong>Total <code>#[ignore = "..."]</code> annotations:</strong> 22</p> <p>22 <code>#[ignore]</code> annotations across the workspace, organised into four triage buckets. This file is the canonical reference for what each ignored test needs in order to run, and which CI job (existing or future) is responsible for lighting it up.</p> <p><strong>Rule:</strong> every PR that adds, removes, or promotes a <code>#[ignore]</code> annotation must update the corresponding row here in the same commit.</p> <p><strong>Bucket legend:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>LIVE-DOCUMENTED</strong> — needs a real upstream service / credential. Legitimately <code>#[ignore]</code>'d by default; opt-in via env var. Should never block CI.</li> <li><strong>DARK</strong> — could run in a dedicated CI job that satisfies the prereqs, but no such job exists today. These are the real coverage gaps. See plan <a href="superpowers/plans/2026-05-17-test-suite-upgrades.html"><code>2026-05-17-test-suite-upgrades.md</code></a> Task 11.</li> <li><strong>ENVIRONMENT-SPECIFIC</strong> — needs a host shape that no GH runner provides (e.g. "no Docker AND no Linux native sandbox available"). Will only ever run in a sub-project's bespoke e2e CI.</li> <li><strong>DEFERRED</strong> — waiting on an explicit dependency (helper, fixture, sibling PR). Should reference what is being awaited.</li> </ul> <hr /> <h2 id="what-changed-since-the-2026-05-13-inventory"><a class="header" href="#what-changed-since-the-2026-05-13-inventory">What changed since the 2026-05-13 inventory</a></h2> <p>Resolved and removed from the inventory:</p> <ul> <li>5 × <code>cmd_orchestration.rs</code> patterns A–E — Skills-4 T9 (PR #83) shipped <code>MockLlmBackend</code>; all five <code>#[ignore]</code> annotations removed.</li> <li>2 × <code>install_cross_check.rs</code> (<code>install_with_matching_manifest_succeeds_…</code>, <code>install_force_after_cross_check_fix_succeeds</code>) — PR #117 enabled both.</li> <li>1 × <code>run_kernel_errors.rs:127</code> (<code>plugin_contract_violation</code>) — PR #118 implemented the test body and removed the <code>#[ignore]</code>.</li> </ul> <p>Added since 2026-05-13 (Layer4 work merged):</p> <ul> <li>10 × <code>tau-plugin-compat/tests/layer4_{native,container}.rs</code> — were on a local branch when the previous inventory was generated; now on <code>main</code>.</li> </ul> <p>Net change: −8 + 10 = +2 entries (20 → 22).</p> <hr /> <h2 id="bucket-1--live-documented-6-tests"><a class="header" href="#bucket-1--live-documented-6-tests">Bucket 1 — LIVE-DOCUMENTED (6 tests)</a></h2> <p>Live API smoke tests. Opt-in via <code>TAU_<provider>_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + API key.</p> <div class="table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th>File:line</th><th>Test</th><th>Reason</th></tr></thead><tbody> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/anthropic/tests/live.rs:45</code></td><td><code>live_complete_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_ANTHROPIC_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/anthropic/tests/live.rs:59</code></td><td><code>live_stream_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_ANTHROPIC_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/ollama/tests/live.rs:49</code></td><td><code>live_complete_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_OLLAMA_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + running Ollama instance</td></tr> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/ollama/tests/live.rs:63</code></td><td><code>live_stream_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_OLLAMA_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + running Ollama instance</td></tr> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/openai/tests/live.rs:45</code></td><td><code>live_complete_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_OPENAI_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + <code>OPENAI_API_KEY</code></td></tr> <tr><td><code>crates/tau-plugins/openai/tests/live.rs:59</code></td><td><code>live_stream_smoke</code></td><td><code>TAU_OPENAI_LIVE_TESTS=1</code> + <code>OPENAI_API_KEY</code></td></tr> </tbody></table> </div> <p><strong>CI plan:</strong> keep <code>#[ignore]</code>'d. Each <code>live.rs</code> already documents the opt-in invocation in its module header. No regular CI job runs these by design; surface as a nightly secret-bearing job if/when the project wants live regression signal.</p> <hr /> <h2 id="bucket-2--dark-12-tests"><a class="header" href="#bucket-2--dark-12-tests">Bucket 2 — DARK (12 tests)</a></h2> <p>Sandbox-related tests that need Linux + a daemon (Docker/Podman) and/or prebuilt plugin binaries. <strong>Largest hidden coverage gap in the workspace today.</strong> Plan Task 11 introduces a dedicated <code>layer4-ignored</code> CI matrix.</p> <h3
